# Changelog

## [Unreleased] - Instrument detail: the rejected payload shows in full (2026-10-06)

Operator, reading why a device's data was being refused: "and also show
rejected payload fully in instruments page", then "rejected pay load table
was not enough payload is cutting not showing fully".

- **The Payload cell of the Rejected payloads card prints the WHOLE
  payload**, wrapped on any character, with no height cap. It was
  `max-w-xs truncate`: one line of a 100-device gateway batch showed and the
  device codes it named - the thing the reason refers to - were hidden. The
  server stored and sent all of it (up to 4,000 characters); only the cell
  cut it. A **Formatted** button on each row opens the payload pretty-printed
  as JSON (anything else as sent) with the reason and time in the dialog's
  header and a Copy button. The card is its own component now,
  `routes/instruments/rejected-payloads.tsx`, so it is tested bare: 7 cases in
  `__tests__/rejected-payloads.test.tsx` (the last device of a 100-device
  batch is in the cell; no `truncate` / `max-w-` class; the formatted view;
  the non-JSON fallback; no button for a row with no payload). Checked in
  headless Chrome with the built stylesheet at the detail column's width. No
  count moved.
- **What the operator was looking at, for the record:** the device connected
  as `CWH/RDU/001-00` had switched from a flat reading to a gateway-style
  `{"devices":[…]}` batch; that instrument is a CHILD of `IOTGW01`, not a
  gateway, so `ingest-core.ts` dead-letters it as `NOT_A_GATEWAY`. Every
  value in those batches was `"NA"` and three of the codes named
  (`CWH/RDU/001-01`, `emf-001`, `testdevice1`) do not exist. Device
  configuration, not code; nothing in the ingest path changed.

## [Unreleased] - Reports: ONE header block for every report (2026-10-05)

Operator: "make all reports header table same only dont put any differences
like table lines and font styles bold everything".

- **Every report's header block now prints identically**: dark rules, every
  cell bold (labels AND values), one size (`HEADER_BLOCK_PT` = 10, the
  Data Report's record size — so that report's header did not move and the
  Alarms page, trend and Instrument Alarms headers grew to match), and one
  label-column width (`HEADER_LABEL_MM` = 32, which the Data Report already
  used; the others were 26). ONE rule in `lib/pdf-report.ts` `addTable`:
  a headless table takes the header style whatever typography the report
  prints its records at; a headed table keeps the report's own. Pinned by
  `pdf-report-rules.test.ts` (6) across both typographies. No count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Trend report: the readings table is gone (2026-10-05)

Operator, pasting the report's own "Truncated: showing the first 2,000 of
2,058 rows for Last 30 days…" and "Readings — every stored reading in this
period": "remove the readings table from trend".

- **The Instrument Trend report (Temperature / Humidity) is now the ruled
  header block and the chart.** The readings table under the chart, its
  "Readings — every stored reading…" / "Averaged readings…" heading and the
  row-cap "Truncated:" notice are gone with it. The subtitle reads "The
  chart as seen on screen"; the sample and averaging notes speak of the
  chart alone and point at the Instrument Time Series report for the
  readings themselves. `TrendReportInput` lost `rows`, `keys` and
  `tableIsAveraged`; the page no longer pivots the plotted points into
  rows, and the review request's `recordCount` is the number of points
  plotted. The Data Report and the alarms reports keep their tables and
  their row cap. No count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Trend report: the header is the alarm report's ruled table (2026-10-05)

Operator: "make trend report header into table properly as like alarm report
header table".

- **The Instrument Trend report (Temperature / Humidity) opens with the same
  eight-field ruled table the trend page's Instrument Alarms report prints**
  — `Block : / Start Date :`, `Area : / Start Time :`, `Location : / End
  Date :`, `Inst ID : / End Time :` — through the same `instrumentAlarmsHeaderPairs`

  block. It replaces the Instrument / Name / Location / Limits in force /
  Period key-value block. Block and Area come from the functional location,

  Report's facts. `TrendReportInput` gains a required `header`. No count
  moved.

## [Unreleased] - Trend report: the period summary table is gone (2026-10-05)

Operator: "in trend repots remove period summary table".

- **The Instrument Trend report (Temperature / Humidity) no longer prints

## [Unreleased] - Layout Designer: the 2D design model is authored in the designer (2026-10-05)

Operator: "layout designer feature is should able to create 2d design model".
Asked what that should mean, of three options — full 2D authoring; a style
switch only; full authoring plus making the five traced floors designer-owned
— the operator chose **full 2D authoring**. Spec
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-layout-designer-2d-design.md`, plan
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-05-layout-designer-2d.md`.

- **A plan has a style, a floor and a north.** A Plan panel (shown when
  nothing on the canvas is selected) sets Standard / 2D architectural, the
  floor group / label / order (the Module-F floor switch) and north; a NEW
  plan is created in the 2D style. Switching back to Standard keeps the
  structure data — nothing is deleted by a style change.
- **Five structure tools** — Column and Equipment (drag a box), Window and
  Wall stub (two clicks; a segment drawn along a wall lands ON it through
  `segmentOnEdge` in `@digilog/shared`, and a window is stored as the thin
  box the traces store), Label (one click, text in the panel). Elements are
  selectable, draggable, editable by number and deletable (button or the
  Delete key, which takes the element before a room selected beside it).
  They show only on a 2D plan. The canvas draws the 2D look itself.
- **Doors in 2D**: the door row gains Hinge (start / end / none — a leafless
  opening), Swing (in / out), Width, and **Double leaf**, which replaces the
  door by two half-width doors with mirrored hinges (`splitDoor`; the
  traces' rule, no flag in the data); refused at six doors.
- **The API writes the layer**: `annotationsSchema` on plan create / update
  (coordinates 0..1, arrays bounded, label text 1..60, `north` < 360,
  `floor.order` 0..99, unknown keys refused; `hvac` / `water` / `airflow`
  pass through for the traced plans). Omitted = the column is untouched;
  given = replaced whole; `null` refused. The `FLOORPLAN_CREATED` /
  `_UPDATED` audit rows carry a COUNT summary of the layer, not the arrays.
- **The dashboard is unchanged** — a designer-made plan carries exactly the
  keys a traced plan carries and renders through the same 2D path
  (`floorplan-designer-2d.test.tsx`). The five script-drawn plans stay
  script-owned; the Plan panel says a re-run overwrites designer edits.
- **Whole-branch review, fixed in one pass (same day):** two structure
  edits in quick succession no longer lose the first (the page builds each
  save from the layer it LAST SENT, `latestAnnotations`, not from the plan
  list that has not revalidated yet); a box dragged to the plan's edge stops
  at the edge (the translation is clamped, the room move's rule) and a window
  drawn along the border stays inside it; the Structure panel refuses a
  zero-size box, a blank label or a zero-length stub IN PLACE with the reason;
  Escape discards a box being dragged out; the door Width input holds what is
  typed and clamps on blur; the plan routes' 400 carries a readable `message`.
  Deferred (minor): the room-drawing status line and Enter under the segment
  tools, the Remove button's title, `SCRIPT_DRAWN_PLANS` matching by name,
  `splitDoor` on a leafless opening, the label click not grid-snapped, and
  the audit summary recording counts only (so a move writes a row whose
  before and after match).
- Pinned by 6 shared unit, 12 API e2e, 10 reducer, 5 Plan panel, 13 structure
  tool, 5 door and 1 dashboard render cases; mutation-checked: `null`
  refused, tools hidden on a standard plan, the Delete key's precedence. No
  count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 16: one door to web storage, a failed fetch says so, dead web code out, client-side form schemas, the product's own name as the shipped default (2026-10-05)

Closes WEB-3, WEB-6, WEB-7, WEB-8, WEB-9, WEB-10, WEB-11, WEB-12, WEB-13,
WEB-14, WEB-15, WEB-16 and WEB-17 of
`docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`; WEB-18 is closed as a
non-defect (below).

- **`lib/safe-storage.ts` is the ONE door to `localStorage` /
  `sessionStorage`** (lib 21 → **22**). Every access — the auth hook, the
  single-tab hook, the API client, the API base, server-contact, the app
  layout, the Settings page, the offset-keys hook — goes through it, and the
  ACCESSOR itself is inside the try: under a block-site-data policy the
  property throws, and the shell white-screened before it rendered.
  Mutation-checked (a bare accessor fails the shell test).
- **A failed fetch no longer renders as an empty state.** New
  `components/ui/load-error.tsx` (`role="alert"`, "Could not load {what}.
  {message}"); seven pages destructure SWR's `error` and show it —
  instruments list, aggregate trend card, System Health, Audit Templates (a
  spinner forever until now), notification logs, the Configuration page
  (manifest AND access-matrix: a failed matrix hid every card from a
  non-admin), alarm filters. Mutation-checked.
- **The dashboard alarms panel's Acknowledge cell is sticky**, inheriting
  the row's own zebra colour (`bg-inherit`), so the panel stays transparent
  — the earlier objection ("a sticky cell needs an opaque background") no
  longer held once the `.alarm-grid` zebra painted every row.
- **Dead code out, with importer counts recorded in the report**:
  `alarm-rule-dialog.tsx` + its test (config pages 23 → **22** — it was
  counted though never a page), `logReportExportOrWarn`, `useFailureText`,
  `ACTIVE_QUADRANTS`, `TimeSeriesChart.lastReading`, the 26 unused
  `card.gradient` entries, the `/m/login` branch, the `window.Capacitor`
  redirect and both `access_token_backup` removals. `fetchReview` is
  module-private; `reviewSignatures` is KEPT (an internal caller and its own
  unit test — the audit's claim about its CLAUDE.md line was wrong).
- **`apiClient.getRaw()` / `getBlob()` on one `authHeaders()` builder**;
  the PDF report's user lookup and the Backup page's export / validate /
  restore use them instead of raw `fetch` — re-auth errors now reach the
  dialog (a REAUTH_FAILED on restore used to land in the result panel as a
  plain failure). The telemetry table's as-of tooltip uses the site
  formatter; the Date & Time page revalidates both its keys.
- **`hooks/use-row-keys.ts`** (hooks 25 → **26**) gives the LDAP, webhook
  and notification-rule row editors stable keys — React re-mounted every
  row on delete, losing focus and in-progress input.
- **Client-side zod schemas for four admin forms** in
  `packages/shared/src/schemas/admin-forms.ts` (shared schemas 7 → **8**):
  LDAP (`ldap(s)://`, required-when-enabled), notification rules and
  templates, help articles, instrument create (non-empty + profile only —
  the "no rule on the ID" decision stands). Wired with `safeParse` + per-field
  errors, NOT `zodResolver`: none of the four is a react-hook-form form.
- **The shipped product name is the product's own, everywhere it is
  defaulted**: `brandingConfigSchema` in `@digilog/shared` now defaults
  `appName` to `BRANDING_TAB_TITLE_DEFAULT` (`T&RH-Monitoring`), `logoText`
  to `TRH`, the tagline to "21 CFR Part 11 Compliant Monitoring" — these
  are what the API serves on a fresh install before Branding is saved. The
  web's own fallbacks (`use-branding`, `pdf-report`, email settings) read
  the same constant. An install that has saved Branding is unaffected.
- **Six `--quantity-*` colour tokens** in `app.css` are the ONE definition
  of the temperature / humidity hues the readings table, the Settings tiles
  and the history widget share; the permissions tab and the boot spinner
  read theme tokens. The quantity hues are deliberately NOT themed — they
  are vocabulary, the `--chart-limit-line` rule.
- **Notification rules: three `alert()` calls replaced by toasts** (a modal
  alert blocks the tab; every other outcome on the page is a toast). The
  trend page's try/catch that only rethrew is gone (eslint
  `no-useless-catch`, the one pre-existing lint error).
- **WEB-18 closed as a non-defect**: SWR 2.4.0 already skips polling while
  the document is hidden (`refreshWhenHidden` is unset everywhere), so no
  visibility hook was added; the non-SWR timers (single-tab heartbeat, JWT
  refresh) must NOT pause — a hidden tab is still the session.
- **Follow-ups from batch 14, on the web side**: System Health renders
  `disk.available === false` / `loadAvg.available === false` as
  "Unavailable" with the reader's error in a tooltip — never a zero bar.
  **Every instrument and profile write runs through `useReauth().execute`**
  under its SEC-7 action — create (`CREATE_INSTRUMENT`, single AND bulk —
  the bulk route had no gate at all until the web sweep found it; it has one
  now, pinned by the gates e2e), detail save / toggle (`UPDATE_INSTRUMENT`),
  delete (`DELETE_INSTRUMENT`), gateway link / unlink, the Settings rename
  (whose code PUT was a bare `put` inside the attribute batch and would have
  looped on the replay once the policy was on), profile save
  (`UPDATE_INSTRUMENT_PROFILE`) and delete (`DELETE_INSTRUMENT_PROFILE`) —
  with idempotent callbacks and a `ReauthDialog` where the page had none.
  One test per screen asserts the action. Profile CREATE is not wrapped: the
  server enforces no action on it.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 17: every user / role / request write is one transaction with its audit row, dates validated, redaction races closed, inactive roles grant nothing, notification visibility as data, reasons on the regulated writes, ended sessions end now (2026-10-05)

Closes API-7, API-12, API-13, API-14, API-15, API-16, API-18, the users /
roles / admin-request / config sub-items of API-20, DATA-11 (users, roles,
scopes, the Permissions tab) and DATA-13 of
`docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **Every user, role and admin-request write runs in `prisma.$transaction`
  with `auditLog(entry, tx)` inside it** — create / update / delete / bulk /
  enable / disable / unlock / reset / reset-request, role create / update /
  delete, and the admin-request decision (claim + act + audit in one
  transaction; the compensating "revert" is gone). A failed audit write now
  rolls the change back instead of leaving a change with no record.
- **Query dates are validated** (`lib/query-dates.ts`): a bad date or a
  reversed range is a 400 by field, and a date-only `endDate` means the end
  of that UTC day — the audit and notification lists read `Invalid Date`
  as "no filter" until now.
- **Redaction cannot race**: the redact UPDATE carries `AND redacted_at IS
  NULL` inside the transaction (a second redaction is 409, mutation-checked),
  and the bulk redact locks its rows `FOR UPDATE`.
- **Response schemas declare what the routes return**: notification rows
  (`targetUserId`, `forUserId`, `forRole`, `metadata`, `readAt`), audit
  detail (`userId`, `userRole` nullable), user `email` and role
  `description` as nullable — each asserted over `app.inject`, because
  Fastify strips an undeclared field silently.
- **An inactive role grants NOTHING** (`rbac.ts` resolves `[]` for it,
  mutation-checked); deactivating a role ends its holders' sessions in the
  same transaction and evicts BOTH auth caches. A system role's
  `hierarchyLevel` / `isActive` cannot be CHANGED (400); an echo of the
  stored value passes, because the Roles page sends the level on every save.
- **Notification visibility is ONE rule as data**
  (`notifications/notification-visibility.ts`: `visibilityWhere` +
  `isNotificationVisible`), used by the list, the single-row check and the
  bulk builder — the ADMIN / other-user and `targetUserId` widenings are
  closed. 25 unit cases, 4 e2e as an operator.
- **The three static config PUTs are validated with zod and re-auth gated**
  (`UPDATE_ROLE_CONFIG` for the access matrix, `UPDATE_CONFIG_PAGE` for
  export options and report page titles), the export-options enum is
  enforced, report page titles are strictly `{companyName, appName}`.
  The two pages save through the re-auth hook now.
- **API-20 sub-items**: the shared Prisma client in admin-requests and the
  email channel (two private pools gone); role-keyed upserts 404 on an
  unknown role instead of creating an orphan row; the role delete count sits
  inside the delete transaction; `LIKE` patterns are escaped with an
  explicit `ESCAPE` clause; `hiddenRolesFor()` feeds `/users` and
  `/users/stats` alike; a dead enum check removed; `MODIFY_USER` goes
  through `updateUserSchema` and refuses a SUPER_ADMIN target (403, the
  request rolls back to PENDING).
- **A REASON is required and stored on the audit row** (`lib/require-reason
  .ts`, 400 `REASON_REQUIRED`; the control is in the service, so a script or
  an older client is refused the same way) for: user delete, bulk delete and
  disable; a role permission CHANGE on the Roles page; a role or user
  instrument-scope save; **and the Permissions tab** (`PUT
  /api/config/roles/:role` when the permission SET changes — a grant or a
  revocation, measured against the stored set, after the privilege check so
  a forbidden grant is still 403). Web: the user dialogs and the scope tab
  collect it, the role dialog offers it, and the Permissions tab shows a
  Reason field once a toggle moves and saves through the re-auth hook (it
  called `put` bare — so did the scope tab; a role whose matrix asked for a
  password could never save either).
- **`purge-alarms.ts` and the redact routes write the actor's USERNAME**
  into `redacted_by`; legacy UUID rows are still resolved on read.
- **An ended session ends NOW, not after the 30 s auth cache.**
  `userRepository.terminateSessions` evicts each ended session from the
  plugin's session cache (keyed by session id, which
  `invalidateUserAuthCache` never touched): a user whose ROLE was changed
  kept the OLD token with the NEW role's grants for up to 30 s. Pinned by a
  users e2e (the old token is 401 on the very next request), mutation-
  checked.
- **The Permissions-tab reason is asked only on a PERMISSIONS save**: a
  Sidebar-tab save also moves an item's primary permission when the item is
  switched on, but that is the menu being arranged and the Sidebar tab
  collects no reason — the first cut gated it too and the sidebar-link unit
  test caught it. The API-wide run (208 files, one at a time) also found the
  instrument-scope-selection e2e still sending the pre-DATA-11 payloads and
  a room-history case whose "4 minutes ago" reading shared the seeded
  reading's epoch-aligned 180 s bucket only a third of the time; both tests
  fixed, no product code.
- Also: `config.service.test.ts` could not load at HEAD (its partial shared
  mock lacked `PERMISSIONS` since batch 2) — fixed. Found, not fixed: role
  delete is one transaction but not serialised against a concurrent
  user-create assigning the role (`users.role` has no FK); a vitest suite
  that opens a real `$transaction` and asserts `toHaveBeenCalledWith` at the
  wrong arity serialises the Prisma client into the diff (minutes per test,
  "Invalid string length") — use the right arity. Reauth actions unchanged
  (55); no other count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 15: the audit trail refuses an UPDATE that is not a redaction, a report snapshot is hashed and verified on download, retention drops are audited and administered, the audit registry matches the code (2026-10-05)

Closes DATA-6, DATA-7, DATA-9, DATA-10, DATA-14, DATA-15, DATA-16, DATA-18
and the report-reviews half of API-19 of
`docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **`audit_trail` has a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger** (migration
  `20261005120000_audit_trail_no_update`, also in `prisma/sql/invariants.sql`)
  that permits exactly one shape of change: `redacted_at` / `redacted_by` /
  `redaction_reason` going NULL → value with `before_value` and `after_value`
  cleared, and every other column byte-identical (compared over `to_jsonb`
  minus those five, so a column added later is guarded by default). Any
  other UPDATE — a checksum, an action, a user, an un-redaction, a second
  redaction — is refused by the database, not by the application.
  `audit-verify.ts` also cross-checks every redacted row against a LATER
  `AUDIT_RECORD_REDACTED` / `AUDIT_RECORDS_BULK_REDACTED` row (new anomaly
  `REDACTION_UNATTESTED`). Nine mutation cases over HTTP.
- **A report request's frozen snapshot is HASHED** — `snapshotDigest()` over
  the exported `canonicalize` (one canonical form, `hash-chain.ts`) — stored
  on `report_reviews.snapshot_hash` (migration
  `20261005121000_report_review_snapshot_hash`; nullable, models stay 37)
  and written into the `REPORT_REVIEW_REQUESTED` and `_APPROVED` audit rows.
  **The download recomputes it against the hash-chained audit row** and
  refuses a mismatch with 409 `SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH` — a snapshot edited in the
  table, even with the column edited to agree, no longer downloads as an
  approved document. Rows older than the column (13 locally) download as
  `snapshotAttested: false`, recorded on the download-log row.
- **Dropping an expired telemetry partition writes ONE `RETENTION_EXECUTED`
  SYSTEM audit row in the same transaction** (partition name, parent, row
  count, range, retention, cutoff). The schedule the worker had read for
  months with no def behind it is now **config def `telemetry-retention`**
  (34 → **35** defs; `monthsAhead`, `dropEnabled` — ships OFF —
  `retentionMonths`; SUPER_ADMIN; dynamic page; a Configuration card lands
  with the web batch). `TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DEFAULTS` is the one definition
  and the worker imports it. The dead-letter prune from batch 13 rides the
  same task.
- **The audit-action registry now matches what the code writes.** Measured
  first: zero rows in either local database under any removed name. Eleven
  actions written but never registered were ADDED (`AUDIT_RECORD_REDACTED`,
  `AUDIT_RECORDS_BULK_REDACTED`, `ROLE_CREATED/UPDATED/DELETED`,
  `ADMIN_REQUEST_SUBMITTED`, `LDAP_CONFIG_UPDATED`,
  `SUPER_ADMIN_API_ACCESS_CHANGED`, `UPDATE_EMAIL_CONFIG`,
  `UPDATE_SMS_CONFIG`, `DASHBOARD_CREATED`); 28 registered but written by
  nothing were REMOVED (`RETENTION_EXECUTED` kept — it is written now):
  actions 106 → **89**. Templates −2 (`ALARM_CLEARED`, `DATA_EXPORTED`, the
  only pruned names that had one) +4 (`INSTRUMENT_PROFILE_CREATED/UPDATED/
  DELETED`, `RETENTION_EXECUTED`): 100 → **102**. Two tests now LOCK this:
  every `action: '…'` literal under `apps/api/src` must be registered
  (`lib/__tests__/audit-actions-registry.test.ts`) and every registry key
  must have a template (`packages/shared/.../audit-actions.test.ts`).
  `SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACTIONS` is the three live names — the audit's claim that
  `NOTIFICATION_DISPATCH` is a live system action was wrong; nothing writes
  it.
- **The session sweep terminates each session in its own transaction** with
  the LOGOUT audit row inside it and a conditional update that rolls back
  when the session was already closed — no LOGOUT for a termination that did
  not happen here, and one failing session no longer stops the rest.
- **Ranged chain verification seeds from row N−1**, so a link break or a
  deletion at the window boundary is detected (`verifyAuditChain` with
  `fromPosition > 0`). `password_expiry_check` carries `fill=1d` (was `0s`,
  which replays every missed hour after an outage). Four stale "new writes
  use V1" comment blocks in `hash-chain.ts` rewritten — writes have been V2 /
  V3 since 2026-05-29 / 07-25.
- **`eligibleApprovers` resolves permissions once per role and scope once
  per (role, user-config) pair**, through the same resolvers as before.
- Both migrations applied to `compliance_core_db` and
  `compliance_core_db_test`; drift guard PASS. **AWS needs both at the next
  deploy.** Found, not fixed: the web `FAIL_ACTIONS` list names
  `UNAUTHORIZED_ACTION_ATTEMPT`, which nothing writes; `prisma generate`
  EPERMs on the engine DLL while ANY vitest process runs (not only `tsx
  watch`), leaving `.tmp*` copies under `node_modules/.prisma/client/`.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 14: uploads refuse an unsigned type, disk usage is read or reported absent, one-transaction deletes, five instrument re-auth actions, a reason for a room limit change (2026-10-05)

Closes SEC-3, SEC-7, API-17, API-19, DATA-11 and the uploads / backup /
webhook / functional-location / profile sub-items of API-20 of
`docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **The server refuses to START on an `UPLOAD_ALLOWED_TYPES` entry with no
  magic-byte signature** (`uploadConfigProblems()` in `uploads/routes.ts`),
  and `readValidatedImage` refuses a signature-less type before it reads the
  stream — an operator adding `image/svg+xml` to the env used to switch the
  magic check OFF for that type silently. `MAX_FILE_SIZE` is applied on every
  `req.file()`; `/photo` goes through the one validator; an oversize upload is
  413 on every route (it was 400 on `/photo`). 14 cases.
- **Disk usage is measured, or reported as unavailable — never zeros.**
  `system-health/disk.ts` tries `fs.statfs`, then `Get-CimInstance` on
  Windows / `df` elsewhere, and a total failure is logged and sent as
  `disk.available: false` + `disk.error`; `loadAvg.available` is false on
  win32. Both DECLARED in the response schema. The web page renders the flags
  in the web batch.
- **A backup restore failure answers a fixed message in production**; the raw
  error is logged, not returned.
- **Webhook target delete is ONE transaction** (count, delete, audit row); a
  foreign-key refusal (`P2003`) maps to 409 `REFERENCED` in `lib/errors.ts`
  for every route. Header names and values are validated at save through the
  platform's own `Headers` constructor — a bad pair used to fail only at
  delivery time, in the delivery log.
- **`PUT /api/functional-locations/:id/instruments` refuses an unknown
  instrument id (400, naming it) and links nothing**; the audit row lists
  codes only. **`GET /api/instrument-profiles/:id/attribute-usage` is
  visibility-scoped**; the PUT cascade is deliberately unscoped (a
  half-scoped profile would delete from half the plant and could not tell).
- **The alarms summary selects only attributes whose key is in the limit
  alias union, case-folded** (`resolveLimit` already folds case) instead of
  every attribute of every instrument.
- **Five configurable re-auth actions** under the existing Configuration
  category (50 → **55**): `CREATE_INSTRUMENT`, `UPDATE_INSTRUMENT`,
  `DELETE_INSTRUMENT`, `UPDATE_INSTRUMENT_PROFILE`,
  `DELETE_INSTRUMENT_PROFILE`. `enforceReauth` runs FIRST on instruments
  POST/PUT/DELETE and profiles PUT/DELETE. **They ship OFF** (the policy row
  default), so nothing changes until an admin switches one on under
  Configuration → Re-authentication; the web prompts land in the web batch.
  The instrument tree nodes carry no `reauthAction` badge yet (cosmetic).
- **A room's LIMIT change needs a stated reason** (`PUT
  /api/floorplans/:id/rooms/:roomId`, 400 `REASON_REQUIRED` with `field:
  'reason'`): a room's limits are a quality specification, and the change is
  recorded with the operator's statement the way an instrument attribute's
  is. `limitsChanged()` compares against the STORED row, so geometry drags,
  doors, label, grade and membership never ask. **The Layout Designer asks
  for the reason BEFORE the request** through the attributes `RemarkDialog`
  (which gained a `title`), listing the bounds being moved with before and
  after; `limitChanges()` in `routes/config/layout-designer/room-limits.ts`
  is the browser's copy of the rule and is tested against the same cases.
  Not covered, as scoped: POST `/:id/rooms` with limits and
  `scripts/trim-room-to-rooms.ts` carry no reason.
- Found, not fixed: `tests/e2e-scripts/*.sh` call `/api/auth/verify`,
  `/api/assets/templates`, `/api/rule-chains` and `/api/qr` — upstream
  DigiLog's surface, none of which exists here; they are dead smoke scripts
  and belong in `docs/archive/`. No count moved except reauth actions.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 13: ingest and alarm mediums — the bridge's own echoes, one SQL reading, TCP rate cap and dead-letter retention, offsets fail closed, webhook cooldown and regex, same-instant readings (2026-10-05)

Closes INGEST-7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 18 of
`docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **The MQTT bridge's own retained downlinks no longer count against its
  queue cap.** `isBridgeEcho(topic)` in `listeners/mqtt-bridge.ts` drops a
  downlink slot (not an attribute REPORT) synchronously in the `message`
  handler, BEFORE the `maxQueued` check — a flood of the bridge's own
  republished slots could otherwise push a device's reading over the cap and
  log it LOST. Pinned by `mqtt-topic.test.ts` and an e2e with `maxQueued: 1`.
- **ONE SQL definition of "a numeric reading"**: `NUMERIC_READING` in
  `telemetry.repository.ts` (number, or a string matching `coerceReading`'s
  regex), used by the range summaries, the trend aggregates
  (`telemetry-aggregate.ts`) and the room history buckets
  (`floorplans/room-history.ts`). The last two tested `jsonb_typeof =
  'number'` alone, so a quoted `"19.25"` counted on the chart and the Data
  Report but not in a bucket mean or a trend aggregate. Pinned both ways.
- **TCP listener: a per-connection rate cap** (600 framed lines per 60 s;
  exceeding it closes the socket with a coded log line) — the MQTT and
  WebSocket transports already had one. **Dead letters are pruned**:
  `pruneDeadLetters` (30 days, then the newest 2,000 per instrument) runs
  inside `telemetry_partition_maintenance`. **Residual**: that task is on the
  1st and 15th; between runs the table is bounded only by the rate caps.
- **A failed offset lookup no longer stores an UNCORRECTED reading as a
  corrected one.** `applySensorOffsets` THROWS instead of logging and handing
  the rows back; the throw lands in `writeBatchOrDeadLetter` (batch 1), so
  the payload is dead-lettered with the error and the device gets
  `WRITE_FAILED` (503) and retries. `offsetReadings` in `@digilog/shared` now
  takes the ingest `classifyValue`, so a corrected row carries `int` /
  `float` like every other instead of a literal `'number'`.
- **A webhook target's cooldown is released when every delivery attempt
  failed.** `shouldFire` still claims at check time (two concurrent jobs
  cannot both sound the hooter); `releaseCooldown(targetId, claimedAt)`
  clears that claim after an all-failed RAISED delivery so the NEXT raise is
  not silenced by a target that never sounded. A failed CLEARED releases
  nothing. Mutation-checked.
- **A flat-path reading keyed `__proto__` is kept, not swallowed**: parsed
  values are built on `Object.create(null)` (`ownKeys()` in
  `payload-parser.ts`).
- **Two readings at one instant: the LAST arrival wins everywhere.** Until
  now history kept the FIRST (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) while the latest
  table kept the LAST (`ts <= EXCLUDED.ts`), so the dashboard could show a
  value the history table never held. History is now `ON CONFLICT (instrument,
  key, ts) DO UPDATE` over `lastPerInstant()` of the batch. Stated plainly:
  a later arrival at the identical (instrument, key, timestamp) REPLACES the
  stored value and its `raw_value`; nothing is dead-lettered. An identical
  QoS 1 redelivery rewrites the row with the same values.
- **The operator's success regex runs against the stored 1,000-byte snippet
  inside a `vm` context with a 100 ms budget**; a timeout fails closed like
  a bad pattern, so a catastrophic pattern cannot hang the worker. Not done:
  refusing such a pattern at validation (`validation.ts`, next batch).
- **`telemetry-overview` reads `instrument_telemetry_latest` for the
  instruments in hand** (`WHERE instrument_id IN (…)`), not the whole table.
- **The MQTT reconnect "backoff" was dead code** — `mqtt` 5.15.2 arms ONE
  `setInterval(reconnectPeriod)` on first close and ignores a later change
  to `client.options.reconnectPeriod`. The mutation and its false comment are
  gone; the period is 1 s as it always was, and the LOG is throttled (first
  attempt, then every 60th) so a broker outage does not write a line a
  second. The e2e that asserted the period grew was pinning a mechanism that
  never worked; it now asserts the throttle.
- Found, not fixed: `dead_letters` has no index on `instrument_id` (the
  dead-letter route and the prune both filter on it). No count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 12: the gated-state allowlists match a segment, the password oracle is gone, one origin rule for the OAuth2 redirect, hard delete ships off (2026-10-05)

Closes SEC-4, SEC-5, SEC-6 and DATA-8 of
`docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **A forced-password-change user, and a SUPER_ADMIN whose API access is
  switched off, can no longer rewrite the password policy.** Both gates in
  `plugins/auth.ts` listed `/api/config/password-policy` and matched it with
  `startsWith`, which also admitted `PUT /api/config/password-policy` — the
  WRITE. A neutralised super admin could drop the complexity flags or set
  `maxFailedAttempts` to 1000 before anyone noticed. The lists now name the
  leaf the shell and the change-password page actually read,
  `/api/config/password-policy/current`, and are matched by
  `matchesPublicPath` on a segment boundary, the same rule as `PUBLIC_PATHS`
  (so `/api/auth/me-history` and `/current-evil` are refused too). Pinned by
  `public-paths.test.ts` (the exact lists) and nine cases in
  `auth.plugin.test.ts` driving the real hook.
- **`POST /api/auth/verify` is removed, with `signVerificationToken`,
  `verifyVerificationToken`, `authService.verify` and
  `VERIFICATION_TOKEN_SECRET`.** It proved a password and issued a 5-minute
  "verification token" that no route in the product ever accepted — re-auth
  is proven inline per request by `lib/reauth-check.ts` — so what remained
  was a live password oracle handing out a bearer-looking credential whose
  `purpose` claim nothing checked. `apps/web` and `packages/` had 0 callers.
  The installers (`scripts/install.ps1`, `scripts/linux/digilog-lib.sh`) no
  longer generate the secret; a leftover value in an existing `.env` is read
  by nothing.
- **The OAuth2 mail redirect URI comes from ONE rule**, `publicBaseUrl(req)`
  in `notification-delivery/routes.ts`: `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (new env, trailing
  slash stripped) when set, else Fastify's own `req.protocol` / `req.host`,
  which honour `X-Forwarded-*` only under `TRUST_PROXY`. The three OAuth2
  routes used to read the raw forwarded headers regardless of trust and
  defaulted the scheme to `http`, so an HTTPS install (the AWS unit has no
  proxy) registered an `http://` redirect and the provider refused it as a
  mismatch. Pinned by `e2e/oauth2-redirect-uri.e2e.test.ts` (4, mutation-
  checked: the raw-header read fails 2).
- **`AUDIT_HARD_DELETE_ENABLED=false` is written by both installer templates
  and `.env.example`.** The CODE default with the variable absent is still
  enabled (`lib/audit-immutability.ts` untouched, so a typo cannot silently
  remove a capability), which is why the templates write it explicitly; an
  existing `.env` without the line keeps hard delete on and should add it.
  **The AWS unit's env in SSM needs the line by hand.** Known gap, unchanged:
  the Audit Trail page gates its delete button on the permission alone, so
  with the switch off an `AUDIT_DELETE` holder sees a button that answers
  403 `AUDIT_HARD_DELETE_DISABLED`.
- Found, not fixed: `OFFLINE_REPLAY_SECRET` is generated by both installers
  and has no reader anywhere (`grep -rn OFFLINE_REPLAY_SECRET apps/api/src
  packages scripts`) — a leftover of the offline-sync removal, the same class
  as the secret above. No count moved.

Closes DOCS-2, DOCS-3, DOCS-14 and DOCS-17 (and DATA-17) of

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 10: signature inputs on the Super Admin card, a landing rule for `/`, the Users guard, the chart axis format (2026-10-05)

Closes WEB-1, WEB-2, WEB-4 and WEB-5 of `docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **The Super Admin API-access card and lockdown screen use
  `SignaturePasswordInput`.** They were bare `<input type="password"
  autoComplete="current-password">` in no form — the exact combination that
  makes Chrome fill the saved login password (the 08-31 acknowledge-dialog
  incident), so whoever sat at an unlocked super-admin workstation could
  press Enter and flip privileged APIs under the super admin's name.
- **`/` lands by rule** (`routes/dashboard/landing.ts`, pure;
  `landing-page.tsx`): the dashboard for SUPER_ADMIN or a role holding
  `DASHBOARD_VIEW`, else the first sidebar page the role can see (the
  sidebar's own visibility rule), else the profile page. Every login lands
  on `/` since 2026-10-03 and it was unguarded: a user-admin role saw "0
  instruments", an empty Blocks overview and a readings error with the 403
  toast suppressed. A redirect rather than a guard, so the first screen is
  never Access Denied.
- **`/users` guards on `USER_READ` alone**, the permission its list and
  stats routes require; the six other `users.*` nodes imply it, and a role
  granted one of them directly used to render the page onto a 403.
- **The chart x-axis prints the administered date / time format** through
  the same `useDatetimeFormat` the hover table uses, never the browser's
  locale and zone — on a workstation in another zone the axis endpoints sat
  hours from the rows beneath them, and the rasterised chart in the signed
  Trend PDF carried the wrong labels.
- Tests: new `routes/dashboard/__tests__/landing.test.ts` (4),
  `components/__tests__/super-admin-api-access.test.tsx` (2, both boxes read
  `autocomplete="one-time-code"` out of the DOM),
  `routes/dashboard/__tests__/chart-axis-format.test.tsx` (2).
  `route-guard-coverage` (2; `/` stays listed as unguarded by `RequireRole`
  — it guards itself), `time-series-chart` (3), `chart-limit-lines` (5) and
  `trend-downloads` (24) unchanged and green. Web typecheck clean. No count
  moved: `landing.ts` and `landing-page.tsx` are route files, not hooks or
  lib modules.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 9: a re-auth password is never stored; the hardcoded config re-auth applies lockout and LDAP (2026-10-05)

Closes SEC-1 and SEC-2 / API-11 of `docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **`stripPrivateFields()` in `lib/reauth-check.ts` removes every
  underscore-prefixed key from a request body, and both re-auth helpers call
  it BEFORE any early return.** `enforceReauth` used to delete
  `_currentPassword` only on the path where the role required a password; when
  it did not — a stale client cache, or any direct caller — the early return
  left the login password in the body, the dynamic config PUT spread the body
  into the stored row, and every later GET returned it to anyone holding
  `CONFIG_READ`. The dynamic PUT, the SMTP and SMS saves and the LDAP save
  strip as well, so no stored value may ever begin with `_`.
- **The four config saves with hardcoded re-auth (`password-policy`,
  `login-security`, `session`, `datetime`) verify through
  `enforceReauthAlways`** instead of a bare bcrypt compare: a wrong password
  now counts toward the account lockout (a stolen `CONFIG_UPDATE` session
  could guess at the rate limiter's pace), and a directory user is verified by
  an LDAP bind, where the compare against the LDAP sentinel could never pass,
  so an AD admin can save those four at last.
- Tests: new `lib/__tests__/reauth-strip.test.ts` (3; mutation-checked — the
  strip moved back after the early return fails it), `config.test.ts` 62 →
  **64** (a `_currentPassword` sent with no re-auth required is neither
  stored nor returned; a wrong password on `PUT /api/config/datetime` counts
  one failed attempt — driven through the operator, since SUPER_ADMIN is
  exempt from lockout by design). `ldap-directory.e2e.test.ts` (29) unchanged
  and green. No count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 8: one pass clears an alarm; the range pass reads quoted numbers; device timestamps and null readings (2026-10-05)

Closes INGEST-3, INGEST-4, INGEST-5, INGEST-6, INGEST-8 and INGEST-16 of
`docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **`claimClear()` in `alarm-evaluation.worker.ts` is the ONE way an alarm
  is cleared**: `updateMany … WHERE state = 'ACTIVE'`, exactly one caller
  gets the row, the loser gets null and announces nothing. The on-ingest pass
  and the cron pass run under different job keys on a worker with
  concurrency 10, so both could clear one alarm — two emails, two hooter
  "off" posts, two delivery rows. All five clear paths (limit disabled,
  limit, inactivity, RS485, range) go through it.
- **The sensor-range pass uses `coerceReading`**, the shared definition the
  dashboard, the limit pass and the SQL summaries use, instead of a raw
  `typeof === 'number'`. The plant firmware sends quoted numbers, so on every
  gateway-fed instrument a range fault neither raised nor cleared while the
  floor showed `OL`. The RS485 clear's `clearedValue` reads the same way
  (it printed blank for a quoted recovery).
- **`parseDeviceTs`**: a 10-digit epoch NUMBER is seconds (it was read as
  1970-01-21 and the whole batch refused); a stamp more than ten minutes
  ahead of the server, or before 2000, falls back to arrival time (a future
  stamp pinned `instrument_telemetry_latest` for as long as it was ahead,
  and every pass judged the stale value).
- **A JSON `null` reading is recorded, not silently dropped**:
  `nullReadingKeys()`; the flat path dead-letters the keys by name and the
  gateway fan-out reports them beside the block's other readings, which
  still land. `{"t":null,"h":45}` used to leave yesterday's temperature as
  current with every alarm source seeing a healthy probe.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 5: audit column widths, one signature bound, functional-location writes made atomic and the rename 500 (2026-10-03)

Closes DATA-3, API-3 and API-4 of `docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **`audit_trail.user_role` is `VARCHAR(50)`** (migration
  `20261003130000_audit_user_role_width`, schema updated, applied to both
  local databases, drift guard PASS). It was 20 while `roles.name` and
  `users.role` are 50 and the role zod allows 50; the raw audit insert has no
  clamp, so a user in a role named longer than 20 characters could not even
  log in (`LOGIN_SUCCESS` → 22001).
- **Every `signature_meaning` is bounded ONCE, in `auditLog`**
  (`clampSignatureMeaning`, `SIGNATURE_MEANING_MAX` = 255), before the
  meaning is hashed or stored, so the hash and the row agree and no caller
  can 500 after its mutation committed. `boundedMeaning()` stays the better
  composer for lists of names; this is the backstop for everyone else.
- **Functional-location name is bounded** (`FL_NAME_MAX` = 120,
  `validateFlDraft`), and the **create, update and instrument-link routes
  write their audit row inside the same transaction** as the mutation
  (`auditLog(entry, tx)`), so a location can no longer exist with no
  `FUNCTIONAL_LOCATION_CREATED` row. The update's "after" path is composed
  from the nodes already loaded, with no second read inside the transaction.
- **`PUT /api/functional-locations/:id` no longer 500s after the rename
  committed.** It returned `loadOwnCounts()`'s `{total, active}` object into
  a field declared `integer`; the serializer threw and every rename of a
  location holding an instrument read as "could not save" (and a retry wrote
  a second audit row). It returns `total` / `total` / `active` as integers,
  `activeCount` declared in the schema.
- Tests: new `e2e/functional-location-update.e2e.test.ts` (4: rename with
  an instrument returns integers and exactly one audit row; an over-long name
  is refused before any write; a name at the bound creates with a meaning
  inside the column; a long Block › Area path is clamped, the full path kept
  in `afterValue`), `validation.test.ts` 12 → **13**, new
  `lib/__tests__/audit-signature-bound.test.ts` (3). Mutation-checked: the
  old `counts.get(id)` return fails the rename case. The location delete and
  order e2e, the tree and bounded-meaning unit tests, `audit-immutability`,
  `audit-chain` and `audit` e2e all unchanged and green. No count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 3: backup restore verifies the real chain, strips credentials, creates partitions (2026-10-03)

Closes DATA-1, DATA-5 and DATA-12 of `docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **The restore's audit-chain pre-check maps EVERY hashed column**
  (`verifyBackupAuditChain` in `backup.repository.ts`), exactly as
  `lib/audit-verify.ts` does: `user_name`, `user_role`, `before_value`,
  `reason`, `ip_address`, `user_agent`, `session_id`, `signature_meaning`
  and `redacted_at` beside the nine it passed before. Since 2026-07-04 the
  writer has hashed the expanded set, so no genuine archive could pass the
  check and every restore was run with `force: true` — the only tamper
  check restore has, disabled as routine. A genuine export now passes the
  per-row check on every row.
- **Service credentials no longer leave in a backup.** `system_config`
  secrets (SMTP `password`, `clientSecret`, OAuth2 tokens and pending state;
  SMS `twilioAuthToken`, `vonageApiSecret`; LDAP `bindPassword` —
  `SYSTEM_CONFIG_SECRET_KEYS`, mirroring what each surface masks on read)
  and a webhook target's `headers` are replaced by the same sentinel the
  password hashes use; restore re-applies the TARGET's own current value
  for each, so a restore never wipes a credential and a backup never
  carries one across installations. A key the target never held keeps the
  sentinel, which no provider accepts, so the operator re-enters it.
- **Restore creates the telemetry partitions the archive needs**, in its
  own transaction, before inserting `instrument_telemetry_history` — one
  `partitionDdl()` (exported from the partition worker; `ensurePartitions`
  uses the same one) per month present in the rows. An archive restored
  onto a fresh install, or onto a database whose old partitions retention
  dropped, used to roll the whole restore back with "no partition … found".
- Tests: `backup-restore.e2e.test.ts` 10 → **13** (every exported audit row
  passes the per-row check and a contiguous tail passes the walk — the full
  walk is not asserted because the shared test database carries a chain
  gap from the hard-delete suites, which the file already documents; SMTP
  password sentinel on export, real value after restore; webhook headers
  likewise), `telemetry-partition.test.ts` 14 → **15** (`partitionDdl`).
  Mutation-checked: dropping two fields from the verifier fails the per-row
  case. No count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 2: role-config saves check the caller's privilege; scope and panel bodies are required (2026-10-03)

Closes API-1 and API-2 of `docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`.

- **`PUT /api/config/roles/:role` can no longer grant what the caller does
  not hold.** `config.service.ts` now computes the permission set the save
  WOULD write (`planRolePermissions`, the unchanged toggle + sidebar algebra,
  lifted out so it can run first) and, when that set ADDS a permission,
  applies `assertRoleWithinCallerPrivilege` from `role.service.ts` — the same
  rule the Roles page's own create/update has applied since the hierarchy
  work — BEFORE anything is written: SUPER_ADMIN exempt; otherwise not your
  own role, not a role at or above your level, and no permission you do not

  unaffected. Until now the route, behind `ROLE_MANAGE` alone, let an ADMIN

  declare their body `required`.** `{}` used to pass the schema, write SQL
  NULL (unrestricted / all panels) through `?? Prisma.DbNull`, and then 500
  on the signature line with no audit row. It is a 400 now and nothing is
  written; an explicit `null` (inherit) is still accepted.

## [Unreleased] - Audit fixes, batch 1: telemetry partitions at boot; a refused write is a dead letter (2026-10-03)

Operator: *"fix all the issues"* (after the strict audit,
`docs/audit/2026-10-03-technical-audit.md`). This batch closes INGEST-1 and
INGEST-2 / DATA-2, the two HIGHs that block a fresh customer install.

- **Partitions exist before the first reading.** `ensurePartitionsAtBoot()`
  (`workers/telemetry-partition.worker.ts`) is called from `app.ts` at every
  boot, independent of the job runner, idempotent, never throws (a failure is
  logged loudly and the cron retries). Migration
  `20261003120000_telemetry_partitions_bootstrap` creates the month it runs in
  plus three ahead with a `DO` block on `now()`, so `migrate deploy` on a
  fresh database — the installers' path — covers the window before the first
  boot; applied to both local databases, drift guard PASS. The two partition
  crons carry `fill=4w` instead of `fill=0s`, so a machine that was off at
  00:05 on the 1st/15th runs the job when it comes back.
- **A write the database refuses is recorded, not lost.**
  `writeBatchOrDeadLetter()` in `ingest-core.ts` wraps both `writeBatch` calls:
  on failure the raw payload is dead-lettered against the sender with the
  database's own message and the reading count, nothing is stamped as
  delivered, and the caller gets `WRITE_FAILED` — **503 on HTTP** (declared in
  the response schema) so a device retries after the fault is repaired. Until
  now one row Postgres could not place failed the whole batch's single INSERT
  and the loss was a log line, after the broker had already acked.
- Tests: `ingest-core.test.ts` 10 → **12** (flat and gateway write failures
  dead-lettered, `WRITE_FAILED`, no last-seen stamp),
  `telemetry-partition.test.ts` 12 → **14** (boot creates and reports the
  current month plus `monthsAhead` on the REAL parent; a failing statement is
  logged and returns `[]` — an own-property override on the Prisma proxy, since
  `vi.spyOn(...).mockRestore()` leaves the proxy method undefined).
  `gateway-ingest.test.ts` (12) and `migration-guard.test.ts` (23) unchanged
  and green. No count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Every login lands on the dashboard; no return-URL (2026-10-03)

Operator: *"i logined and go to some page and there only i directly logout,
after that i logined another role user its coming to where i logout that
page, if that page is access for both then its showing other wise showing
access denied, after every login user should come to dashboard page only
dont redirect to other pages"*.

- **The defect.** The layout (`app-layout.tsx`) and the API client's 401
  handler sent an unauthenticated visitor to `/login?returnUrl=<the page>`,
  and both the login page (already signed in) and `useAuth().login` honoured
  it. On a shared workstation that is the page the PREVIOUS user left, so
  the next user's first screen was Access Denied whenever their role lacked
  it.
- **The fix.** All four sites changed: the layout and the API client send to
  `/login` with no query; the login page's signed-in redirect and the hook's
  post-login navigation go to `/` unconditionally. A `returnUrl` still in a
  bookmark is ignored. The open-redirect guard went with the feature it
  guarded.
- Tests: new `login-lands-on-dashboard.test.tsx` (2): the signed-in visitor
  to `/login?returnUrl=/alarms` lands on `/`; the hook's login on that URL
  lands on `/`. **The second sets `window.location` as well as the router's
  location** — the old code read `window.location.search`, and a mutant
  that put that read back passed the router-only version. Mutation-checked
  after the fix. No count moved.

## [Unreleased] - The trend page's breadcrumb leads back to the dashboard selection the reader left (2026-10-03)

Operator: *"in dashboard when i click on all instruments trends option,
trends page is opened but when i click on its not going to all instruments
page its going to instruments page"*, then *"and also same in area trends
also"*.

- **The defect.** The dashboard's selection — All Instruments, a Block, an
  Area — lives in its URL as `?fl=`. The readings table's Trend arrow told
  the trend page only `from: 'dashboard'`, so its crumbs read Dashboard /
  <code> / Trend: the Dashboard crumb went to the dashboard's TOP level and
  the code crumb to the instrument's detail page. Nothing led back to the
  view the reader had been looking at. The GRAPHICAL view was worse: its
  four room / tile navigations sent no state at all, so from an Area's floor
  the trend page claimed Dashboard / Instruments / <code> / Trend — a path
  never taken.
- **The fix.** `trailFor(nav.breadcrumb)` (`dashboard/location-nav.ts`,
  pure) turns the dashboard's own breadcrumb into links — `/?fl=<id>`,
  encoded as the dashboard encodes it, `/` for the root — and the dashboard
  hands that trail to BOTH the readings table (`trail` prop, in the Trend
  arrow's router state beside `from`) and the floor view (every way into the
  trend page now goes through one `goTrend()` carrying origin and trail). The
  trend page reads it with `trailFrom(location.state)` (validated shape;
  malformed = none) and `trendCrumbs()` HEADS its crumbs with it, so the
  trail reads Dashboard / All Instruments / <code> / Trend, or Dashboard /
  CWH Block / Stability / <code> / Trend, each a link back to exactly that
  view. A refresh or pasted URL still falls back to the hierarchy.
- **Second pass, same day** (operator: *"still its going to instrument page
  not going to all instruments widget"*): the INSTRUMENT crumb was the one
  being pressed to go back, and it linked to the detail page — a page the
  reader never saw on the way in from the dashboard. From the dashboard the
  code is now a PLAIN crumb (named, not linked); the only links are the
  trail before it, so the hop back is All Instruments / the Area. From the
  Instruments list the detail page IS the way in and the crumb still links.
  `trend-breadcrumbs.test.ts` 13 → **14**.
- Tests: `trend-breadcrumbs.test.ts` 9 → **13**, `location-nav.test.ts`
  18 → **21**, `telemetry-table.test.tsx` 17 → **18** and
  `floorplan-empty-rooms.test.tsx` 5 → **7** — the last two read the state at
  the DESTINATION through a probe route, since the state is what the next
  page receives. No count moved. Not seen on screen.

## [Unreleased] - Fix: popups inside the hero band were clipped and painted over; every Select was transparent (2026-10-03)

Operator: *"instrument selection dropdown was not showing values properly in
dropdown"*. Reproduced by rendering the Settings page with the list open in
headless Chrome against the built stylesheet; THREE causes, two of them on
every page, none in the picker itself:

- **`PageHero` clipped its content.** The band's root carried
  `overflow-hidden` to clip its two decorative circles, and that clipped every
  popup a caller's toolbar opens inside it — the Settings picker's list, the
  Export menu on the Alarms and Audit heroes — to the band's bottom padding.
  Only a sliver of the search box showed. The circles now sit in their own
  `absolute inset-0 overflow-hidden rounded-[inherit]` wrapper
  (`data-testid="page-hero-decoration"`); the root no longer clips.
- **The band's toolbar wrapper trapped the popup under the next card.** Its
  `backdrop-blur-sm` is a `backdrop-filter`, which forms a stacking context,
  so the list's `z-50` ranked only among the toolbar's children and the
  widget card below (a positioned sibling of the band) painted over the
  options. The blur is gone — it softened the circles' edges behind a
  translucent plate, nothing more — and the toolbar is `relative z-10`, so it
  stays above the band's siblings whatever is added to the wrapper later.
- **Every native `Select` in the app had no background.** `cn()` runs
  tailwind-merge, which read the chevron's untyped `bg-[right_0.6rem_center]`
  as a background COLOUR and dropped the `bg-white` before it as a duplicate.
  On a white card that is invisible; the Settings page's Block select is the
  first one on the band, and it rendered dark with its white border. The
  position carries the `position:` hint now
  (`bg-[position:right_0.6rem_center]`), which tailwind-merge files under
  background-position. Verified by reading the MERGED class string out of the
  dump — `bg-white` was simply absent.
- Tests: `page-hero.test.tsx` 6 → **8** (root not clipped, decoration
  clipped; toolbar no backdrop filter, `relative z-10`), new
  `select.test.tsx` (4: `bg-white` AND the hinted position survive the merge
  at every size; a caller's background override still wins). Both read the
  FINAL class string, which is the one tailwind-merge emits — a test on the
  source literal passes for the version that does not work. The picture was
  checked before and after in headless Chrome. No count moved.

  mouse) and `model-tiles.html` (a geometry-free tile board). Deck rebuilt

## [Unreleased] - Mean Kinetic Temperature on the Data Report, per instrument (2026-10-03)

Operator: *"in attributes isMktcalculationenabled attributes is true then in
data report mkt value should come, if false then mkt value should not come in
data report"*.

- **What prints**: on the Data Report's `Interval :` row, a right-hand
  `MKT : 23.5` cell at the instrument's temperature precision, and `MKT -
  Mean Kinetic Temperature` in the legend — only when the instrument's
  `isMktCalculationEnabled` attribute is on (`1` / `True` / `yes` / `on`,
  case-folded). Off, absent or unreadable = no cell, no legend entry; the
  interval takes the row as before. The block never grows taller and no cell
  is ever empty.
- **How it is computed**: ICH Q1A(R2) / USP <1150>, ΔH/R = 10,000 K, in SQL
  over EVERY reading in the period (`getRangeSummary` → `mktExpMean`), the
  same population as the report's Max / Min — never over the printed
  interval rows, which would miss the hot readings between them. Temperature
  slot only. `packages/shared/src/types/mkt.ts` holds the constant, the
  degrees conversion and the pure reference `mktCelsius` the SQL is tested
  against; `isMktEnabled` is the ONE reader of the flag, OFF by default — the
  opposite of the limit enable flags, because a derived figure on a §11
  report must fail toward absence.
- **The SERVER decides**: `summaries[key].mkt` on `GET /:id/telemetry?points=`
  is a number iff the flag is on and the key is the temperature slot; the
  browser prints the row iff it received a number and never re-reads the
  attribute. Declared in the response schema (mutation-checked).
- **On this installation every instrument carries
  `isMktCalculationEnabled = 0`**, so no report shows MKT until it is set
  to `1` on an instrument (Settings page or Attributes panel, audited).
- Pinned by 6 shared unit cases, 2 API e2e, 2 Data Report cases. Shared
  type files 32 → 33 (`mkt.ts`); no other count moved.

## [Unreleased] - A limit or range attribute may carry text beside its number (2026-10-03)

Operator, on being shown why CWH/RDU/101-00's humidity limit had vanished
from every screen with `Enable_Humid_NMT = True`: *"text is included in limits
and ranges show that text in reports and show max and min values, in
dashboard show the same text only"*.

- **The defect**: `parseLimitValue` accepted only a bare number. That
  instrument's `h_hl` had been edited to `60 (For Reference)`, so the
  humidity high bound resolved to NULL — no set point, no RH Max in the Data
  Report, no high-humidity alarm possible, nothing on screen saying why — and
  the enable flag beside it looked like the thing that had failed.
- **The number inside the text is the bound** (`parseLimitValue` takes the
  FIRST numeric token: `60 (For Reference)` → 60, `NMT 27` → 27, `25 C` → 25;
  a value with no digits is still no limit). Alarms are evaluated against it,
  status is judged on it, the chart's limit LINE is drawn at it, and the
  report's Max / Min print from it — all exactly as for a bare number. Stated
  once: a value holding two numbers resolves to the first; keep the number
  first or alone.
- **The text is what PRINTS, verbatim, wherever the bound is quoted**
  (`limitDisplayText` / `resolveLimit().text` in `@digilog/shared`, ONE
  reader): the dashboard SET POINT badge (`NMT 60 (For Reference)`,
  `18.0 - 27 (For Reference)`), the trend page's bound cells (without the
  unit — the text may carry its own) and chart limit pills, the Data Report's
  `Temp. Limit :` / `RH Limit :` cells, the Trend report's `N above …` line and
  its chart raster, the alarm Limit cell on all three alarm tables, and the
  Alarm Report's set-point columns. A bare number prints at the instrument's
  precision as before; a bound that is not in force (switched off, inverted,
  absent, room-sourced) carries no text either.
- **Server-resolved, frozen with the number**: `telemetry-overview` rows
  carry `limitText {tempMin, tempMax, rhMin, rhMax}`; the chart summary
  carries `limitMinText` / `limitMaxText` beside the bound its breach counts
  were taken against; an alarm snapshot freezes `thresholdHighText` /
  `thresholdLowText` (a range alarm `rangeLowText` / `rangeHighText`) so an
  edit tomorrow cannot re-caption a closed excursion. All declared in the
  response schemas (mutation-checked: dropping an inner key fails the e2e).
  The browser never re-derives the text from an attribute.
- **Not changed**: the room-detail chart's agreed band (several instruments,
  numbers only), notification and webhook `${limit}` (a device may parse it as
  a number), and the Settings / Attributes panels, which show the stored value
  as typed. The 2026-09-01 "every server resolver agrees" rule still holds —
  both resolvers now also agree on the text.
- Pinned by 7 shared unit cases, 3 API e2e (`telemetry-overview`,
  `instrument-telemetry-range`) + 1 unit (`limitSnapshot`), and web cases on
  `set-point`, `telemetry-table`, `data-report`, `band-gauge`,
  `trend-report-chart`, `alarm-display` and `alarms-report`. No count moved.
- **Still true for CWH/RDU/101-00**: its humidity LOW bound and temperature
  LOW bound are withheld because `Enable_Humid_NLT` / `Enable_Temp_NLT` are
  `False` — that is the flag doing what it is for, not this defect.

## [Unreleased] - Delete a functional location, with everything in it for a super admin (2026-10-03)

Operator: *"add delete option for functional locations for super admin"*.

- **What existed**: `DELETE /api/functional-locations/:id` (permission
  `FUNCTIONAL_LOCATION_DELETE`, re-auth `DELETE_FUNCTIONAL_LOCATION`), refusing
  any location that held an area or an instrument (409), and ONE Delete button
  on the detail page that sent the request without the re-auth flow — a role
  that required re-auth got a 401 with no way forward. On this installation
  every location holds instruments, so nothing could be deleted.
- **A SUPER_ADMIN may now delete a location WITH everything in it**
  (`?cascade=true`): a Block's Areas go with it and every instrument in any
  of them is UNLINKED — set to no location, never deleted; its readings and
  alarms stay. One `FUNCTIONAL_LOCATION_DELETED` audit row per location
  deleted, each naming the instruments it released (`instrumentsUnlinked`;
  the Block's row also `areasDeleted` and `instrumentsUnlinkedInAreas`), in
  one transaction. Any other role holding the delete permission still gets
  the 409 for a non-empty location (its message now tells a super admin the
  way through) and a 403 `SUPER_ADMIN_ONLY` if it asks for the cascade. An
  empty location deletes as before, for any role with the permission.
  **What a cascade does not touch, stated once**: a role or user whose
  instrument scope named the location keeps the stale id (its location
  branch then grants nothing; the instruments are reachable again when
  re-linked or named outright), and an alarm webhook target scoped to it
  likewise.
- **Where**: a trash button on every Block card (*Delete block*) and beside
  every Area row (*Delete area …*) on the Functional Locations page, and the
  detail page's Delete — all through ONE flow (`delete-location.tsx`):
  `deletePlan()` (pure) decides from the tree's own counts whether the role
  may delete it as it stands; the confirm names the areas and the
  instruments that become unassigned ("Delete with everything in it") or,
  for an empty one, says it holds nothing; then the audited, re-authenticated
  DELETE; the tree is re-read, the detail page returns to the Area's Block or
  the list.
- **Two bugs fixed on the way**: the list page gated *Arrange order* /
  *Arrange areas* on a `functional_locations.update` node that does not exist
  (the tree's is `.edit`), so every non-super-admin lost them; and the detail
  page's create / edit writes and the list page's create now go through the
  re-auth flow like the order save already did. And a third, pre-existing
  and unrelated: the order route's audit `signatureMeaning` listed every
  block name, and `audit_trail.signature_meaning` is `VARCHAR(255)` behind a
  raw insert — a long list was a 500, which is what the order e2e had been
  failing with on the test database. `boundedMeaning()` lists what fits and
  counts the rest (the full order is in `afterValue`).
- Tests: `functional-location-delete.e2e.test.ts` (4, over the real route and
  database; the super-admin gate mutation-checked), `bounded-meaning.test.ts`
  (3), `functional-location-order.e2e.test.ts` green again (14),
  `index-page.test.tsx` 6 → 11, `detail-page.test.tsx` 5 → 7 (the cascade flag
  and the non-super-admin refusal mutation-checked). `tsc` clean on both
  apps, `vite build` OK. No count moved: no permission, reauth action, audit
  action, model, migration, route or page. Not seen in the running app.

## [Unreleased] - The drawn floor plans get the "vivid status" look (2026-10-01)

Operator: *"these layouts look wise not good, make those layout more
professional and beautiful and colorful ui"*. Shown three concept images made
from the real Module-E render (`Layouts/CWH/concepts/look-A-vivid-status.png`,

wall, door, room, card position or card shape moved (card shapes and widths
compared before and after on the three older floors; three shapes are 1.5-3
units taller to make room for the pills).

- **Room floors are a gradient of the room's STATUS colour** - green in limit,
  red out of limit, violet for a sensor error, amber offline. A room with no

  pill is SOLID in the status colour with white text, so a state can never be
  mistaken for a quantity's tint (an offline amber next to an in-limit
  temperature's orange is the pair that would otherwise read alike). The text
  is centred in its pill and shrinks to fit (`100.0 %RH`, `Error`).

  shadow is a little deeper; room names are darker and semi-bold.

## [Unreleased] - Sensor offsets: Temp / Humid Off set correct readings as they arrive (2026-10-01)

Operator: *"for instruments profiles Add 2 attributes Temp Off set, Humid Off
set, those should be visible only for superadmin … values should be integer or
decimal … whenever temperature is received and temp off set value is 2 then 2
will be added to temperature value and that value should show every where …
same like humidity also … give configuration also"*, then *"there should be +
or - option if + it should add, if - value should be decrease"*. Choices: applied
at INGEST; negative allowed; names as written; the device value NOT shown.

- **Two attributes on the instrument profile**, `Temp Off set` and `Humid Off
  set` (added to `T&RH Sensors` locally through the audited profile PUT; AWS
  needs the same). Their value is a number with a **+ / -** sign — + adds, -
  subtracts — stored sign-first (`2` → `+2`); anything else is a 400
  `INVALID_OFFSET`. Typed in a + / − selector beside the number wherever an
  attribute value is typed (Attributes panel, Settings page, New Instrument
  form); bulk-upload cells are validated per row.
- **Applied as the reading ARRIVES** (`ingest-core.ts` → `applySensorOffsets`,
  both the direct and the gateway path, each child its own offset): the
  corrected value is what is STORED, so every screen, report, PDF and alarm
  uses it with no change to any of them, and an offset change affects new
  readings only. Only the slot keys (Configuration → Telemetry Slots) are
  corrected, only when the value is a reading — a failure word (`NA`) is stored
  as sent, so RS485 detection still sees it. What the device sent is kept in
  the new `instrument_telemetry_history.raw_value` (migration
  `20261001150000_telemetry_raw_value`, nullable, the partitioned parent) and
  shown nowhere. A failure to apply stores the reading UNCORRECTED and logs it.
- **SUPER_ADMIN only.** Every other role: absent from `GET /:id/attributes`,
  from profile key lists and the usage endpoint (so the New Instrument form and
  the bulk template never ask), from the Attribute Access picker; 403 on
  create, 404 on edit/delete; offset columns in their bulk file are unknown
  headings. Their profile save can neither drop the hidden keys (which would
  cascade-delete the offsets from every instrument) nor add one. Offsets are
  never sent to a device (downlinks and the child change event strip them —
  firmware applying them too would correct twice) and a device's own report of
  one is refused and dead-lettered.
  **Not hidden: the audit trail.** Setting an offset writes the usual
  `INSTRUMENT_ATTRIBUTE_SET` row with its value, visible to anyone with
  `AUDIT_READ` — a §11 record is not filtered by role.
- **Configuration → Sensor Offsets** (def `sensor-offsets`, 33 → **34**;
  SUPER_ADMIN card; dynamic page): master switch (default ON — nothing happens
  until an offset is typed) and the attribute keys for each slot.

  replaces the two cards: Approvers (roles + users) and a table of every report
  type (mode, remarks, password). **The two stored rows are unchanged** —
  `report-approvers` and `report-downloads` — each saved WHOLE through the
  generic dynamic PUT, and only when it changed; both keys are excluded from

  no def, migration, model, enum or permission moved.

  Series** (the trend page's card), **Trend Page Report** (the trend page
  header's Export as PDF), **Temperature Trend**, **Humidity Trend**,
  Instrument Alarms, Alarm Report, Audit Trail (PDF). A split type reads the
  setting it came from (`inheritsFrom`) while its own keys are absent, so

  (`reportDownloadsRow`).
- **Code-review fixes to `f84671f`:**
  - the configured mode and remarks are refused BEFORE the password on both
    routes (a refused request verified, and counted toward lockout, a password);
  - a kind is BOUND to its audit `reportType` (`reportTypeMatchesKind`, 400
    `REPORT_TYPE_MISMATCH`) and Excel is accepted for the Audit Trail alone, so
    a Direct kind cannot be borrowed to write a download record for a reviewed
    report. Stated plainly: the PDF is built in the browser, so the server
    controls the RECORD, not whether a file can be produced;
  - an EMPTY instrument list is unscoped ONLY for the Audit Trail; any other
    report with none (an Alarm Report of no alarms, or an older Alarms row the
    backfill could not resolve) is visible only to UNRESTRICTED viewers and the
    signers — it was visible to every role-mate and approver;
  - an eligible approver needs `REPORT_REVIEW_READ` as well as `APPROVE`;
  - `/report-approvers/current` returns the ACTIVE approvers (what a request
    would freeze), with users as a COUNT (`approverUserCount`) rather than ids,
    so the dialog cannot promise a disabled approver.
  - Not changed: a request still resolves each candidate approver's scope one
    by one (fine at this plant's size; noted by the review).
- Tests: shared 35, API e2e 30 (+ unit 12, export-log 16, config 62), web
  dialog 16, alarms 30, data report 7, trend 24, reports 12, Report Settings 5.
  Mutation-checked: the empty-list rule fails its case when reverted. Not seen
  on screen.

## [Unreleased] - Report downloads: Direct or Request per report type; approvers configured, not chosen; requests scoped by role and instrument (2026-10-01)

Operator, over several messages: *"per user or per role option should be
removed in request place and add that in configuration … if there role
selected then for that role users can see the report data, and also who are
requesting report also that role users can see the data"*; *"if one operator
user send request to supervisor then all operator user can view and download
the report, and also all supervisor users can view and download reports, and
also remove view draft … which are assigned to role or user for that users
only assigned instruments report requests should come"*; *"provide one
configuration for which one we need report request and normal time period
selection download option … for which report type remarks should be there or
not … request or direct download configuration should be come for all report
types"*; *"password reauthentication should be required or not also should be
selectable"*; *"add report downloads configuration in super admin settings"*.
Choices put to them: Audit Trail PDF in the configuration like the others;
password required on Direct; defaults = today; scope "any" instrument;
several approvers; existing requests keep their assignee.

- **Configuration → Report Downloads** (new def `report-downloads`, 32 → 33;
  SUPER_ADMIN-only card beside Report Approvers; rendered by the dynamic page).
  Per report type — Data Report, Trend Chart, Instrument Alarms, Alarm Report,
  Audit Trail (PDF) — **Download mode** (Direct / Request approval),
  **Remarks required**, **Password required**. Defaults are today's behaviour
  (Request, remarks on, password on), so nothing changes until a super admin
  does. `coerceReportDownloads` (stored row) and
  `coerceReportDownloadsResponse` (the narrow route's per-kind shape) in
  `@digilog/shared` are the two readers; every switch fails CLOSED. Served by
  `GET /api/config/report-downloads/current`.
  - **Direct**: the dialog reads "Download — <report>"; the PDF is audited
    (`REPORT_GENERATED`, now with `reportKind`) and THEN saved — fail-closed.
    **Request**: unchanged workflow, minus the picker.
  - **Enforced on the server, both ways.** `POST /api/audit/report-export-log`
    refuses a PDF whose type is Request (409 `REPORT_REQUIRES_APPROVAL` — it
    was a way round the approval) and requires a valid `reportKind` for a PDF;
    `POST /api/report-reviews` refuses a Direct type (409 `REPORT_IS_DIRECT`).
    Remarks and the password are demanded exactly as configured, and checked
    BEFORE the password, so nobody signs a refused act.
  - **Password = Yes asks EVERY role** (`enforceReauthAlways`); No asks
    nobody. For these PDFs the setting replaces the per-role
    `DOWNLOAD_REPORT` policy, which still governs the Audit Trail's **Excel**
    export (not a PDF, not configured here: always direct, remarks required).
  - The password is typed IN the download dialog now, beside the remarks
    (`SignaturePasswordInput`), not in a second re-auth prompt.
- **No Send to.** The requester chooses nobody: a request goes to EVERY
  approver role and every approver USER configured under Configuration →
  Report Approvers (new setting **Approver users**, beside the roles; options
  from the new `GET /api/config/report-approvers/candidates`). The set is
  **frozen on the request** — migration `20261001120000_report_review_approvers_scope`
  adds `report_reviews.approver_roles`, `approver_user_ids`, `instrument_ids`
  (arrays, backfilled from the old single assignee and, best effort, from
  `requestMeta.instrumentCodes`); the old `assignee_*` columns are kept and no
  longer written. Models 37 / enums 13 unchanged. Applied to both local
  databases; **NOT on AWS — the next deploy applies it**.
- **Who sees a request**: the requester's ROLE-mates (by the frozen
  `requestedByRole`) and every approver may view its data and download the
  approved copy; only approvers decide (`REPORT_REVIEW_APPROVE`, separation of
  duties unchanged, SUPER_ADMIN still exempt). **All of them only within their
  INSTRUMENT SCOPE** — a request is visible when the user's scope covers ANY of
  its instruments; the Audit Trail PDF is about none and is not scoped. The
  two signers and SUPER_ADMIN are not scope-bound. Out of scope = 404. ONE
  predicate (`isParty` / `mayDecide` / `inScope` in
  `report-reviews/service.ts`) used by the lists, the detail read, the decision
  and the download log; the lists' SQL is its translation. The server checks
  that every instrument a request names is real and inside the REQUESTER's
  scope. Notifications go per USER, filtered by scope — never a role
  broadcast, which would name the instruments to approvers who cannot see them.
- **Reports page**: View draft REMOVED (with `openDraft`); a PENDING row opens
  its frozen data beneath it as tables, as an approved one does; the second tab
  is **Requests** (raised by me or anyone in my role); Send to lists the frozen
  approvers. `components/assignee-picker.tsx` deleted.
- One delivery path for every page: `lib/report-delivery.ts`
  (`deliverReport`) — Alarms page, Audit Trail PDF, Data Report card, the trend
  page's four downloads. The Alarms report sends the ids of the instruments its
  PRINTED alarms belong to.
- **Found and fixed on the way:** the web hook first read the narrow route's
  response with the stored-row reader, which turned every type into Request —
  Direct could never have reached a dialog. Caught by the dialog test; the
  response reader is separate and both are tested against each other's shape.
- Not changed: the PDF renderer's draft watermark and `toBlobUrl()` now have NO
  caller (View draft is gone); kept as a renderer capability.
- Counts: config defs 32 → **33**, web hooks 23 → **24**
  (`use-report-downloads.ts`), web lib 20 → **21** (`report-delivery.ts`),
  shared type files 30 → **31** (`report-downloads.ts`). No permission, reauth
  action, audit action, route or sidebar item moved.
- Pinned by: 21 API e2e (`report-reviews.e2e.test.ts`, a seven-user cast incl.
  out-of-scope approver and role-mate) + 5 new PDF cases in
  `audit-export-log.test.ts`, 11 unit (`service.test.ts`), 12 shared unit, and
