## [Unreleased] - Approved PDF: the signatures are a TABLE, and each signer's ROLE is frozen on the record (2026-09-25)

Operator: *"in downloaded report reviewed by and approved by was coming
right, those should be come in table, Name, Role, Date & Time for both should
come side by side"*, then *"name, role, date & Time should come one below
one, headings should be one row left side and reviewed by and approved by on
top side by side"*.

- **The approved PDF's end block prints a signature table**: **Reviewed By**
  and **Approved By** as the two column headings across the top (the
  operator's words — the first is the requester), and **Name**, **Role**,
  **Date & Time** as the three rows down the left. Drawn with autotable in
  `pdf-report.ts` (`ReportConfig.signatureTable`, height reserved before the
  block is placed); the two "Requested By: name (id) — date-time" lines are
  gone from that copy. The line form (`signatures`) still exists for any
  other caller and is still tested. Printed Date & Time keeps the right.
- **The ROLE is FROZEN at the act, never looked up live.** Migration
  `20260925120000_report_review_roles` adds `report_reviews.requested_by_role`
  and `decided_by_role` (nullable VARCHAR(50), no enum — models stay 37,
  enums 13); the service writes `ctx.userRole` on the request and on the
  decision; the response schema declares both (Fastify would strip them
  silently — e2e asserts them over HTTP). A signature block must read back
  the way it was signed, and a user's role can change afterwards.
  **Backfill, recorded in the migration**: rows written before the column
  took the signer's CURRENT role from `users` by username — the best fact
  available, not the role at signing; a signer who no longer exists stays
  NULL and prints a dash. Local: 3 of 3 requests and 2 of 2 decisions
  filled. **Applied to both local databases; AWS gets it on the next
  deploy (`migrate deploy`).** The API dev server was stopped ~15 s for
  `prisma generate` and restarted; Vite untouched.
- `reviewSignatures()` in `lib/report-review.ts` now returns
  `SignatureColumn[]` (label, name, role, dateTime); `ReviewSummary` carries
  `requestedByRole` / `decidedByRole`.
- Tests: e2e 19/19 (roles asserted on the request and the decision); web
  `report-review` 9/9 (the table's columns, a null role, the draft carries
  neither form), `pdf-report-snapshot` (every heading, name, role and
  date-time in the rendered text; the line form still prints for another
  caller), Reports page 13/13; tsc both apps and vite build clean. The
  rendered PDF was not looked at.

## [Unreleased] - Graphical view full screen: the trend widget's pattern, through a portal (2026-09-22)

Operator: *"full screen option you are not given properly, i need like how
full screen option there in trend widget like that i need for layout"*.

- **The defect.** The floorplan view lives in a react-grid-layout item, which
  is positioned with a CSS transform, and `position: fixed` inside a
  transformed ancestor is fixed to THAT ancestor — so the overlay opened
  inside the panel's own box, not over the screen. The trend and Data Report
  widgets never met this: their pages have no transformed ancestor.
- **The fix.** The full-screen overlay is rendered through `createPortal` to
  `document.body`, and it is now the trend widget's chrome: the dark title bar
  with the plan name and the toggle in the same place (icon + "Normal
  screen"), the drawing filling the rest, Escape to leave; no plan switcher,
  no legends. tsc and `vite build` clean. **Not seen on screen.**

  area ≥ 0.005²), `sharedEdges` / `mirrorOpening` (an opening on one room's edge
  re-projected onto the neighbour's coincident edge, which usually runs the

  edge at `offset`/`width` with an optional door leaf, or CONNECTOR with a
  label; `kind` a validated string, not an enum; cascades with either room).

  flatten a polygon room — and an explicit null clears it. Three link routes

  existing `UPDATE_FLOORPLAN_ROOM` re-auth); an OPENING is checked against the

  carries "A ↔ B", no new placeholder). 8 e2e in two new files; the existing

  `polygonDoorPlacements`, `polygonSharedOpenings` over the shared module;
  `doorToEdgeOpening` is the ONE place a wall-named door is reconciled with
  edge order — the bottom and left walls run the other way round a clockwise

## [Unreleased] - `send-scenario-telemetry.ts`: every reading state, to every placed instrument, continuously (2026-09-22)

Operator: *"send data to all instruments continously with all type values,
like below limits values, higher than limits, NA, error what ever types are

- New `apps/api/scripts/send-scenario-telemetry.ts`. Each placed
  non-gateway instrument gets ONE scenario by its position in code order
  (four in fourteen in limit; one slot each for temperature/humidity above
  and below its limit, probe `"NA"` text (RS485 Error), outside the sensor
  RANGE (OL), humidity never sent (grey NA), and OFFLINE — a report every 8

  refuses a non-local API without `--force`.

  h_hl 60`), the way the gateway does — an MQTT `attributes/report` as each
  device, one system `INSTRUMENT_ATTRIBUTE_REPORTED` audit row per key — because
  without a bound nothing can be "above the limit"; 99 of 100 had none since
  the 2026-09-16 key deletion. Only instruments with none of the four are
  written; `--no-limits` skips it. **All 100 local instruments now carry the
  four gateway limit keys.**
- Proven on the first round: accepted 100/100; the latest table holds 16
  string values and 7 instruments with no humidity, and within a minute the
  passes raised 29 INSTRUMENT_LIMIT, 14 RS485_FAILURE and 14 SENSOR_RANGE
  alarms — the fabricated alarms the header warns about; `purge-alarms.ts`
  clears them. Left RUNNING detached (`--interval 30`), log in
  `%TEMP%\cc-scenario-telemetry.log`; stop it by killing that node process.

## [Unreleased] - Graphical view: readings fill their tiles, one colour per condition (2026-09-22)

Operator: *"in layouts show instruments live temperature and humidity values
and if in limts green color, if its crossed or below the limits show red, if
error highlight with other color, if offline also show with other color"*.

**Measured first, not assumed:** every one of the 100 placed instruments
ALREADY had a value tile on its plan (`tileLayout` over the live rooms: 96
FULL, 4 VALUES_ONLY, 0 dropped) — but the reading font was capped at 12 units
inside rooms 100-500 units wide, so the values were there and unreadable; and
a failed probe painted the SAME red as a limit breach.

- **The font fills the tile.** `room-geometry.ts` `fillFont()` grows the
  step's base font until the tile is full, bounded by the tile's height (both
  chips must still fit — the same `twoChipsHeight` equation, solved for the
  font, so the existing chip-fit guarantee survives), by its width (an
  eight-glyph label inside the tile), and by a ceiling of 26. Never below the
  base the step already fitted. On the live plans the readings now print at
  12-26 units (most rooms 26, twice the old size; Module-F's 63-wide room and
  QC 3's two smallest stay at 12 — width refuses them).
- **The chip spans the tile** (`cw = tile.w − 6`, was text-width): the
  reading is a coloured band, so the colour reads from across the room before
  the number does. The instrument code shrinks to its tile instead of
  overrunning it at the larger font.
- **A FOURTH colour, VIOLET, for a sensor fault.** `ChipTone = InstrumentStatus
  | 'ERROR'`; `tileValues()` (pure, exported from `floorplan-view.tsx`) gives a
  failed (`Error`) or saturated (`OL`) probe the `ERROR` tone, never
  `OUT_OF_SPEC` — a dead probe is neither a breach (nothing was measured) nor a
  silence (the logger is still talking). The legend gains **Sensor error**.
  Green = in limit, red = crossed, amber = offline / partial, unchanged; a
  breach on an offline instrument is still red (the judgement outranks the
  age). The server's `sensorError` / `rangeError` is the source; nothing here
  re-derives it.
- Pinned by `__tests__/floorplan-values.test.ts` (7) and
  `__tests__/tile-font.test.ts` (7); mutation-checked three ways (error tone
  back to red: 1 fails; growth removed: 2 fail; height bound dropped: 1
  fails). `room-geometry.test.ts`'s chip-fit cases pass unchanged at the grown
  size. tsc and `vite build` clean. **Not seen on screen** — the size ceiling
  (26) and the violet are the two things to judge by eye.

## [Unreleased] - Alarm status wording repaired: `Cleared â€” Unacknowledged` (2026-09-21)

Operator: *"in alarm page in middle of the text symbols coming"*. Not a
rendering bug — the STORED wording was wrong.

- **Cause, from the audit trail.** The `alarm-limits` config row was rewritten
  on 2026-09-16 14:04 by a Python client (`Python-urllib/3.14`, an agent's PUT
  to repoint the alias keys) that read the row through Windows' default
  codepage and sent it back as UTF-8. Each em dash in `statusActiveAck` and
  `statusClearedUnack` became `â€”`. That CONFIG_CHANGED row's before-value
  still holds the correct text; the shipped defaults in `@digilog/shared` were
  never wrong. Only that one row, of 32, carried the fault; `alarms`,
  `instrument_attributes` and the rest were clean.
- **Repaired with the new `apps/api/scripts/repair-config-mojibake.ts`**, dry
  run by default, `--apply` to execute. It reverses the exact fault — every
  character mapped back to its Windows-1252 byte, the bytes decoded as strict
  UTF-8, and only a value where all of that succeeds and differs is touched —
  so ordinary text is never "corrected". Each repaired row is written with an
  audited CONFIG_CHANGED (whole row before and after, targetType `config`),
  the same record the dynamic PUT writes. Applied: 2 values on `alarm-limits`,
  audit row 5765; 0 rows still carry the bytes; the chain shows only the 10
  July anomalies (positions 67..360).
- **No code changed.** The Alarms page reads these wordings live from
  `/api/config/alarm-limits/status-texts`, so a refresh shows the fix.

## [Unreleased] - Which fields the Settings page shows is administered (2026-09-21)

Operator: *"in settings page what attributes and details should display in one
configuration page, in that configuration page any attribute or any field hide,
then that field should not show in the settings page, in configuration page give
hid/un hide options"*. Asked whether "details" meant the Instrument ID alone
(the widget's only non-attribute tile) or also Name / Type / Profile / location,
they took the first.

- **Where.** Configuration → Instrument Attributes — the page that already has
  one row per key with its display name — gains a **Show in Settings** toggle
  per row and one for the **Instrument ID** tile above the rows. No new
  configuration page or card (the 2026-09-16 "dont give as seperate
  configuration" precedent).
- **What is stored.** A second setting on the existing `attribute-labels` row:
  `settingsHidden: {instrumentId: boolean, keys: string[]}` — the HIDDEN set,
  so a key added to a profile tomorrow shows until someone switches it off.
  Global like the names, edited per profile, written whole in the same save and
  merged by the same rules (`mergeSettingsHidden`, pure, exported beside
  `mergeLabels`): a row decides its own key, a renamed row carries its switch,
  a key that left this profile drops out unless another profile still lists it.
  **No count moved** — no def, page, route, hook, permission, migration or enum.
- **Reader.** `coerceSettingsHidden()` / `isHiddenInSettings()` in
  `@digilog/shared` (+ `SETTINGS_HIDDEN_NONE`, `SettingsHidden`). Absent, older
  or malformed reads as nothing hidden — never as hide-everything. The def's
  zod refuses a bad shape and accepts the field's ABSENCE, so a client that
  predates it still saves. `GET /api/config/attribute-labels/current` returns
  the coerced set beside the labels, both inner keys declared in the response
  schema (Fastify strips an undeclared one silently; mutation-checked).
  `useAttributeLabels()` returns `settingsHidden` / `isHiddenInSettings(key)`
  beside `labelFor` — one fetch, so a tile cannot be labelled and hidden from
  two versions of the row.
- **Settings page.** Filters its attribute tiles and the Instrument ID tile by
  the set; in Edit a hidden field has NO input, so nothing on that page can
  write it. Header line now reads "the fields configured for it".
- **Scope, stated plainly.** Presentation over the Settings page ONLY, per the
  request. The attribute is still stored, still served by the API, still on the
  instrument detail page, the New Instrument form and the bulk template, and
  Attribute Access still decides who may edit it. A key typed freely on one
  instrument — one no profile lists — has no row on the config page and
  always shows.
- **Tests.** 5 shared unit (`attribute-labels.test.ts`), 3 API e2e
  (`attribute-labels.e2e.test.ts`; the unset-row case now asserts the new
  field), 2 hook, 5 Instrument Attributes page (toggle state incl. case-fold,
  toggle-only dirty + save body + no profile rewrite, un-hide, rename
  carry-over + another-profile keep, only-profile drop; the two existing save
  assertions grew the field), 3 Settings page (hidden key, hidden ID, Edit
  writes neither). Mutation-checked: the response schema (3 e2e fail), the
  Settings filter (3 fail), the merge's left-this-profile rule (2 fail).
  `tsc --noEmit` both apps and `vite build` clean.
- **Not verified:** on screen. The operator holds the browser session; the
  layout of the toggle column (a compact Key / Display name / Settings header
  row was added above the key rows) is the thing that needs their eye.

## [Unreleased] - AWS: the local database's data copied into RDS (2026-09-18)

Operator: *"copy the data from local database and same data should deploy in
instance database"*. Every `public` table of the local `compliance_core_db`
(PostgreSQL 18) was loaded into RDS `compliance-core-db` (PostgreSQL 16)
except **`audit_trail`** (RDS keeps its own chain: the local one is keyed with
a different `AUDIT_CHAIN_KEY`, is known corrupted, and is the record of a
different machine), **`sessions`** and **`_prisma_migrations`** (identical on
both sides, 34). RDS snapshot `compliance-core-db-pre-datacopy-20260918` first.

- **Method.** `pg_dump --data-only --schema=public --inserts
  --load-via-partition-root` on the laptop; the file went to the instance by
  `scp` through an SSM-tunnelled SSH session (`AWS-StartSSHSession`, key pair
  `user_mgt`, no port opened). On the box, ONE transaction under
  `session_replication_role = replica`: `TRUNCATE` of every public table
  except the two protected ones (no `CASCADE`, so a reference from outside
  the list aborts instead of reaching further), the dump, then row-count
  guards (101 instruments, 2,006 attributes, 103 credentials, 137 rooms, 8
  floorplans, 216 alarms, 849 deliveries, 400 dead letters, 1,775 readings,
  6 users, 32 config rows) and an `audit_trail` unchanged check — a miss
  rolls back. Three rollbacks happened before the commit, each leaving RDS
  untouched: PG18's `\restrict` psql meta-commands, the PG17-only
  `transaction_timeout` GUC, and the `graphile_worker` schema riding along
  (fixed by `--schema=public`).
- **Also copied:** the two uploaded files (branding image, floorplan image)
  into `/var/lib/digilog/uploads`, and the local `INSTRUMENT_TOKEN_KEY` into
  the box's env so the 103 stored credentials stay decryptable.
- **What RDS lost:** its 2 users (`superadmin`, `111111`) → the local 6
  (`superadmin`, `101010`–`101014`, local passwords); 6 notifications, 1
  admin request, 2 help articles, and 1 config row that existed only there.
- **A defect the copy introduced, found by `verify-chain` and repaired the
  same minute.** A data-only dump of `public` also carries
  `setval('audit_trail_chain_position_seq', 5354)` — the LOCAL position —
  even though `audit_trail` itself was excluded. The first audit row written
  afterwards (the verification `LOGIN_SUCCESS` at 06:02:24Z) was numbered
  5354 instead of 48 and `verify-chain` reported a gap. The checksum is
  computed BEFORE the sequence assigns the position, so the hash chain was
  never wrong; the one row was renumbered 5354 → 48 (guarded: matching id,
  action and link to row 47) and the sequence set to 48, with the API
  stopped so nothing else could extend the gap. `verify-chain` → `intact:
  true`, 50 rows, 0 anomalies. **Next time exclude the sequence too:**
  `--exclude-table=audit_trail_chain_position_seq`.
- **Passwords on the copied users (operator, later the same day):** `101010`-`101014`
  reset to `Welcome@123` through `POST /api/users/:id/reset-password` (audited
  `PASSWORD_RESET`, sessions evicted), then, on "clear the flag, keep Welcome@123
  without prompt", `force_password_change` / `is_temporary_password` cleared by a
  direct UPDATE (no API clears them; no audit row of its own). Superadmin untouched.
- Nothing in the repo changed for this; the scripts were one-off and are
  described here. The instruments report to the LOCAL broker, so on AWS
  they read as silent until a device is pointed at 13.204.15.17.

## [Unreleased] - Retained downlinks no longer wait on a down broker; start-app.bat starts EMQX (2026-09-16)

Operator: *"fix that cascade hang also when broker is down"* and *"EMQX should
start whenevr bat file is started"*.

- **Bridge `publish()`**: the decision is now the pure `publishDisposition`
  (tested). A RETAINED publish while the broker is offline is handed to
  mqtt.js's outgoing store and resolved AT ONCE — delivered on reconnect,
  which is what retained state is for — instead of waiting for a PUBACK that
  cannot come and letting every caller time out (2 s each). An offline EVENT
  is still refused, closing still refuses everything. Found when a 400-removal
  profile cascade held its response ~27 minutes against a stopped broker.
- **Profile cascade** announces removals AFTER the response, not before it.
- **`scripts/start-app.ps1` step 14 (of 15 now)**: when `MQTT_BROKER_URL` is
  local and nothing listens on its port, EMQX is started (`EMQX_HOME`, else
  `%USERPROFILE%\emqx-5.3.2`, else any `emqx-*` there) and the port polled
  for up to 90 s; a missing or slow broker is a WARN naming what stops
  (telemetry, alarms), never a Die. A remote URL is left alone. `stop-app`
  does not stop the broker — it is not this checkout's process.
- Not run end to end: the stack and broker were already up, and the script
  refuses to start over a running API (by design). The script parses; the
  broker block was exercised by hand with the same command.

## [Unreleased] - Removing a profile key removes the attribute from its instruments; names and keys unique ignoring case (2026-09-16)

Operator: *"when i removed attributes for profile in configuration those are
not removing for instruments and also in one profile same keys or same dispaly
names should not repeat in small letters or capital letters difference also"*.

- **Cascade.** A key dropped from a profile's list is now deleted from every
  instrument in that profile that carries it, case-folded. Each deletion is a
  `INSTRUMENT_ATTRIBUTE_REMOVED` row with the value it held and the operator's
  remark, and each device is told (retained slot republished without the key,
  gateway change event with `null`). `PUT /api/instrument-profiles/:id` takes
  `reason` and REFUSES a removal that would delete recorded values without one
  (`400 REASON_REQUIRED`, listing `affected: [{key, instruments}]`). New
  `GET /api/instrument-profiles/:id/attribute-usage` returns which keys the
  profile's instruments carry with counts, so the page states the consequence
  before the save: the Instrument Attributes page opens the remark dialog
  listing each removed key and how many instruments lose it, then PUTs the
  keys with the reason. A key nobody carries saves as before. A rename by case
  alone is not a removal. This is the ONE exception to "profiles inherit
  prompts, never values"; adding a key still back-fills nothing. 4 e2e
  (usage folded by case; refused without reason, nothing moved; cascade with
  audit rows per instrument; unused key needs no reason), 3 page cases;
  mutation-checked (dropping the fold, and dropping the reason gate, each fail).
- **Uniqueness ignoring case.** The `attribute-labels` def's `zodSchema` refuses
  two keys or two display names that differ only by case (400). The page flags
  a duplicate display name on the row, naming the key that holds it, and
  blocks Save — among this profile's rows and against other profiles' keys (a
  key this profile itself lists is excluded, or a carried-over name would
  block its own rename). Duplicate KEYS were already refused on the page
  case-insensitively and de-duplicated by `parseInstrumentAttributeKeys`.
- Not seen on screen.

## [Unreleased] - Settings edits in place; the Instrument ID is changeable (2026-09-16)

Operator: *"in settings when user clicks on edit values should be editable but
another edit popup was showing and also in settings Instrument id should be
changable"*.

- **Settings widget, inline edit.** Edit no longer opens the Attributes panel
  in a dialog; the tiles become inputs in place (Instrument ID and every
  attribute the role may edit, from the same `/attribute-access/me` rule the
  panel applies), with Save and Cancel in the header. Save asks ONE remark for
  the batch of changed attributes — `RemarkDialog` gained a `changes` list —
  then PUTs each changed KEY with that reason through the panel's endpoints
  inside one re-auth, and the new code last through `PUT /api/instruments/:id`.
  The callback is idempotent (the re-auth hook replays it after a 401). Nothing
  changed writes nothing. A wildcard ID is refused before any request. 13
  tests; mutation-checked.
- **`PUT /api/instruments/:id` accepts `code`.** It was immutable because the
  code is the MQTT client id and topic segment. That is now handled after the
  commit by `afterCodeChange`: the old retained attribute slot is cleared and
  the set republished under the new code; a gateway's roster moves and each
  child's slot moves with it; the parent roster of a renamed child is
  republished; the auth cache is invalidated so the old client id is refused at
  once. **The device itself must reconnect with the new ID — the platform
  cannot reconfigure it.** Name follows the code when it was the code.
  Duplicate → 409, wildcard → 400. 6 e2e over a captured publisher; the
  instruments e2e case "never its code" re-pointed; `LOCAL_SETUP_WINDOWS.md`
  §"code is immutable" corrected.

## [Unreleased] - Ubuntu / Debian installer: `digilog_<version>_amd64.deb` (2026-09-09)

Operator: *"build the complete application installation exe file for ubuntu"*.
Two premise corrections stated first: Ubuntu's installer form is a `.deb`, not
an `.exe`; and this laptop cannot build it (Linux-native `bcrypt` and Prisma
engines; no WSL, no Docker, virtualization off in firmware). Four decisions
taken with the operator: build on a GitHub Actions runner; `.deb`; bundle
PostgreSQL; "work for any Ubuntu version".

- **`scripts/linux/build-deb.sh`** — the Linux counterpart of
  `build-installer.ps1`: builds the app, does the clean-room `npm ci --omit=dev`
  + `prisma generate`, downloads Node 24.20.0 (official linux-x64), portable
  PostgreSQL 18.6.0 (zonky `embedded-postgres-binaries-linux-amd64`, own
  `lib/`, ltree + pgcrypto verified present) and EMQX 5.3.2 (the ubuntu20.04
  tarball — bundled Erlang, oldest glibc), stages `/opt/digilog/{node,runtime,
  pgsql,emqx,emqx-templates,scripts}` + five systemd units, and runs
  `dpkg-deb --build --root-owner-group`. "Any version" is met by building on
  the oldest supported runner with self-contained binaries; the only declared
  dependencies are `libc6 (>= 2.31)`, `openssl`, `adduser`, `procps`,
  `ca-certificates`.
- **`scripts/linux/digilog-lib.sh`** — provisioning library sourced by
  `DEBIAN/postinst`: service user + dirs, CA/server certs (SAN localhost,
  hostname, 127.0.0.1, LAN IP), `digilog.env` generated once (`0640
  root:digilog`), `initdb` (scram, UTF8, port 5433, localhost) + role + db +
  extensions + `migrate deploy` + seed with the bundled node only, pre-upgrade
  `pg_dump` before any schema change, EMQX config rendered from the SAME
  `scripts/emqx/` templates as Windows (stray-token guard), dashboard password
  after boot, health wait.
- **`DEBIAN/postinst|prerm|postrm`**: fresh vs upgrade decided by the presence
  of `digilog.env`; `apt remove` keeps data, config and certs (the Windows
  uninstaller's rule); `apt purge` destroys them and the user. Initial
  superadmin password from `DIGILOG_ADMIN_PASSWORD` at install, else generated
  into a root-only file.
- **systemd**: `digilog-db` (postgres as `digilog`, readiness via `pg_isready`
  in `ExecStartPost`), `digilog-emqx` (`emqx foreground`), `digilog-api`
  (`EnvironmentFile=/etc/digilog/digilog.env`, `Requires` the DB, only `Wants`
  the broker — a broker fault must not take the app down; `ProtectSystem=strict`
  with `ReadWritePaths` on data and logs), `digilog-backup.timer` nightly 02:00
  → `digilog-backup.sh` (same naming, 14-day rotation and
  `LAST-BACKUP-STATUS.txt` as the Windows task).
- **`.github/workflows/build-deb.yml`** (`ubuntu-22.04`, Node 24): builds the
  package on tag `v*` (GitHub Release with the .deb), on pushes to `data-layer`
  touching the packaging inputs (artifact), or by hand; caches the vendor
  downloads; **smoke-installs the .deb on the runner** — three services active,
  `/api/health` 200 over HTTPS, a real superadmin login, one backup run, then
  `apt purge` and an assert that the data dir is gone. That is the
  clean-machine proof the Windows installer has never had in CI.
- **`schema.prisma`** gains `binaryTargets = ["native", "debian-openssl-1.1.x",
  "debian-openssl-3.0.x"]` so one package runs on 20.04 and on 22.04+;
  Windows dev only pays a one-time engine download at `generate`.
- **`.gitattributes`** forces LF on `scripts/linux/**`, `scripts/emqx/**` and
  the workflow — a CRLF `postinst` fails with `/usr/bin/env: 'bash\r'`.
- **Docs**: `docs/deployment-methods/method-c-ubuntu-deb.md` (also shipped
  inside the package as `/usr/share/doc/digilog/README.md`), the methods README
  table, `PHARMA_DEPLOYMENT_21CFR.md` §4b, the EXE plan pointer, root `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Verified here:** `bash -n` on every script, a render of the EMQX template
  through the Linux `sed` path matching the PowerShell dry-run, and a parse of
  the workflow. **Not verified here:** the build and the smoke install — those
  run on the GitHub runner on push; `gh` is not logged in on this machine, so
  the run must be read on the Actions tab (or after `gh auth login`).

## [Unreleased] - The installer bundles the EMQX broker; the auth hook admits the bridge (2026-09-08)

Operator, after an offline/intranet audit found that the running app needs no
internet but the installer did not carry the MQTT broker: *"add emqx to
installer bundle and fix docs"*.

- **`scripts/build-installer.ps1 -EmqxZip`** (mandatory) stages
  `emqx-5.3.2-windows-amd64.zip` — the LAST Windows build — into `stage\emqx`
  with `data\` and `log\` stripped; `scripts\emqx\*` (the two config
  templates) and `provision-emqx.ps1` join the named script list.
- **`scripts/provision-emqx.ps1`** (new; called by `install.ps1` before the
  services are registered and by `upgrade.ps1` before the API restarts):
  appends `MQTT_BROKER_URL` / `MQTT_CLIENT_ID` / `MQTT_USERNAME` /
  `MQTT_PASSWORD` / `EMQX_NODE_COOKIE` / `EMQX_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` to
  `digilog.env` only if absent; renders `etc\emqx.conf` + `etc\acl.conf` from
  the templates (stray-token guard, stock files kept as `*.orig`); creates the
  data dir under `ProgramData`; re-registers the `emqx` service through
  `emqx.cmd uninstall` + `install` (erlsrv bakes the generated config paths in
  at install time, so a config change IS a re-register); waits for
  `emqx_ctl status`; sets the dashboard admin password; opens TCP 1883/8883.
  `-DryRun` renders to `%TEMP%\digilog-emqx-dryrun` and prints every privileged
  command — run against this box's broker, the output matches the working
  `cluster.hocon` key for key.
- **`scripts/emqx/emqx.conf.template`**: the working dev configuration with the
  per-install values as `@@`-placeholders, plus two deliberate differences —
  dashboard bound to `127.0.0.1` only, WebSocket listeners off — and ONE
  authenticator (the HTTPS hook, `verify_peer` against the install's own CA).
  **`scripts/emqx/acl.conf`** is this box's ACL verbatim (the stock file's two
  allow-all rules are what it replaces).
- **The auth hook admits the ingest bridge** (`mqtt-auth-routes.ts`): username
  `MQTT_USERNAME` with `MQTT_PASSWORD` → allow (constant-time compare over
  SHA-256 digests); the bridge name with a wrong, empty or missing password →
  deny, never a fall-through to the token path; no credential configured →
  deny. This is what removes the built-in-database user — the one step that
  needed the dashboard or an API key — from the customer install. Four e2e
  cases in `mqtt-auth.test.ts` (RED first, 14/14 after).
- **Uninstall** stops and removes the `emqx` service and the `DigiLog MQTT`
  firewall rule; the broker's data survives unless `-PurgeData`.
  **`installer/DigiLog.iss`** copies `emqx\` `onlyifdoesntexist` (the running
  service holds the files) and creates `ProgramData\DigiLog\emqx`.
- **Docs corrected:** `docs/deployment-methods/method-a-native-windows.md` and
  `tasks/EXE-PACKAGING-PLAN.md` both said MQTT/EMQX was removed in 2026-06 —
  the third time that stale claim has been found (root `CLAUDE.md` 2026-08-24,
  `DEPLOY-WINDOWS.md` the same day). `docs/PHARMA_DEPLOYMENT_21CFR.md` gains
  §4a, the production broker runbook it had never had. `.env.example` and
  `LOCAL_SETUP_WINDOWS.md` §9A.3 note the bridge-via-hook change.
- **Not verified here:** a real `Setup.exe` build and a clean-VM install (needs
  Inno Setup, the four downloads and admin on a VM). What IS verified: the
  four API e2e cases, `tsc`, the dry-run rendering against the local 5.3.2
  broker, and a parse of all six PowerShell scripts.

## [Unreleased] - SUPER_ADMIN may approve any report request, their own included (2026-09-08)

Operator: *"super admin should be able to approve own requests or other
requests"*, after finding no Approve button on the Reports page for a request
they had raised themselves as `superadmin`. The two-person control shipped on
2026-09-07 refused the requester outright, SUPER_ADMIN included.

- **`isSelfDecision(ctx, row)`** in `report-reviews/service.ts` is now the one
  statement of the rule: the requester cannot decide their own request unless
  they are SUPER_ADMIN. `decide()` uses it for the `SELF_APPROVAL` 403; the
  page's `mayDecide` mirrors it (presentation — the 403 is the control).

  name on the Requested By and Approved By lines. The e2e asserts exactly that
  (`decidedByName === requestedByName`) so it is a recorded decision, not an
  accident.

  refused on a request they raised"), and a page test for SUPER_ADMIN seeing
  Approve / Reject on their own row and on a row assigned to nobody they are.
  Mutation-checked both sides: dropping the exemption fails 1 test in each.
- **Not changed:** the Send-to picker still never offers SUPER_ADMIN as an
  assignee and `coerceApproverRoles()` still strips it — SUPER_ADMIN already
  counts as assignee of every request. Nothing is granted to any role by
  default; ADMIN still needs `View Reports` / `Approve / Reject Reports`
  under Roles & Access before an ADMIN user sees the page.
- No count moved.

## [Unreleased] - Report review workflow: every PDF download is a request an approver signs (2026-09-07)

Operator: *"when ever user click on download then directly pdf should not
download, as per requested time period data should go per review once review
completed and approved then user and approved user can get that approved data
in side bar new option there user can download reports, who ever requested and
approved users electronic signatues should come if report was downlaoded"*.
Four decisions put to them and taken as recommended: one approver; the approver
is a user or a role chosen at request time; every PDF download; the approver
sees a DRAFT PDF of the exact report. Spec
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-report-review-workflow-design.md`, plan
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-07-report-review-workflow.md`, nine commits.

**What changed for the user.** Pressing any PDF download opens the same dialog
plus **Send to** (a user or a role), then the password re-auth. Nothing saves.
A **report request** is recorded and the assignee notified in-app. **Reports**
appears in the sidebar (`/reports`): *For my approval*, *My requests*,
*Approved*. The approver views the DRAFT (watermarked `DRAFT — NOT APPROVED`,
no signatures) and approves or rejects with remarks + password; the requester
is notified. Approved reports download for the requester, the approver and
SUPER_ADMIN with two signature lines — Requested By and Approved By, each
`name (user id) — date-time`. Each download is audited. Rejected requests stay
visible to their parties. The Audit page's Excel export is not a PDF and stays
direct; the flag-disabled Send for Review button there (retained UI for the
module removed 2026-07-18) is gone.

**The record is the frozen document.** `ReportSnapshot` v2 records every
drawing call and the chrome; the DRAFT and the approved copy are both replays
of one snapshot through the one renderer, so what was reviewed is byte-for-byte
what is downloaded. Rendered here and read back: watermark on the draft, both
signatures on the approved copy, the bold out-of-limit cell intact.

**API.** New module `report-reviews` (24 → **25**): `POST /` (REPORT_REVIEW_READ +
DOWNLOAD_REPORT re-auth), `GET /?list=queue|mine|approved`, `GET /:id` (404 for
a non-party, never 403), `POST /:id/approve|reject` (REPORT_REVIEW_APPROVE +
APPROVE_REPORT / REJECT_REPORT re-auth; assignee only; the requester never,
SUPER_ADMIN included; conditional UPDATE on PENDING → 409 on a second
decision), `POST /:id/download-log` (APPROVED, party, BEFORE the file). No
DELETE. Model `ReportReview` + enum `ReportReviewStatus` (35/12 → **36/13**),
migration `20260907120000_report_reviews`, both databases, drift guard PASS.

**Counts.** permissions 42 → **44**, reauth 48 → **50** (categories 8), audit
actions 98 → **102** / templates 92 → **96** (categories 7), sidebar 13 → **14**,
routes 51 → **52**, tree groups 12 → **13**, nodes 53 → **55**, feature
privileges 41 → **43**. Re-derived by the commands in `CLAUDE.md`.

**Tests.** 5 unit + 15 e2e (three users, three roles, action-reauth pinned and
restored FIRST in afterAll; mutation-checked: no pending guard → 409 case
fails, no self-approval rule → separation-of-duties case fails); shared
372/372; web: 6 snapshot cases (no watermark → draft case fails), 10 client
cases, 3 dialog cases, 8 Reports page cases, and the three page tests re-pinned
to replay the submitted snapshot. `tsc` clean in shared, api, web; `vite build`
clean. **Not seen on screen** — the operator holds the browser session.

**Out of scope, stated:** email/SMS for report events (the notification RULES
are keyed on `NotificationEventType`, which has no report events); a second
review stage; editing or withdrawing a request; expiring stale requests.

**Review fix, same day — the approver's DRAFT was NOT watermarked.** The `DRAFT — NOT APPROVED` mark, the page numbers and the end block are all painted at finalisation, which only `save()` ran; `openDraft` handed the RAW document to the new tab via `doc.output('bloburl')`, so the approver opened a clean, unpaginated, unwatermarked PDF — the one path the safeguard exists for. The test that "proved" the watermark called `save()`, a path the draft never takes. `ReportDoc.toBlobUrl()` now finalises (once — a second call cannot print a second page number) and `openDraft` uses it; the draft test renders through that path and asserts `Page 1 of`, and the `openDraft` test's stand-in returns a different URL from `doc.output` so the raw path fails it. Mutation-checked: dropping the finalise call from `toBlobUrl` fails the draft test.

## [Unreleased] - RTC sync: `digilog/rtc/time` every 10 minutes and on request (2026-09-05)

Operator: *"create another topic for rtc sync, {"method":"getTime"} user will
send request with this key, when ever we receive request we need to send utc
time, and also request is received or not for every minute that current time
utc time stamp should sent, this is global, add it for gateway instrument"*,
then, later the same day, *"make it every 10 minutes"*.

New `modules/instruments/listeners/rtc-sync.ts`. A device publishes
`{"method":"getTime"}` on `instruments/<code>/rtc-request`; the platform
publishes exactly `{"unix":<epoch MILLISECONDS, a 13-digit number>}` (operator:
*"you have to send the payload like this it seems {"unix":1792221233122}"* —
the shape moved three times in one afternoon: `{"method":"time","utc":<ISO>,"epoch"}`,
then `utc` as a number, then this; the firmware's parser is the authority) on the
GLOBAL topic `digilog/rtc/time` — at once on a request, and every 10 minutes
on the wall-clock boundary (:00, :10, :20 …) regardless — it ticked every
minute for its first hours; `RTC_TICK_MS` is the one place the period lives
(`startRtcTicker`, started in `app.ts` after the
downlink publisher exists, stopped before the bridge closes, both timers
`unref()`'d). Not retained. The time topic sits outside `instruments/` so the
bridge's own subscription does not echo it and one literal ACL grant covers
every device. Anything but `getTime` on the request topic is ignored with a
log; an unknown code is dropped. `rtc-request` joined
`MQTT_RESERVED_TOPIC_SEGMENTS`. ACL: three edits (device publish
`rtc-request`, bridge publish `digilog/rtc/time`, all subscribe
`digilog/rtc/time`); local broker restarted; **AWS needs the same.** The
gateway's Connection instructions show both topics and a time sample. Tests:
8 unit (incl. the ticker under fake timers), 3 e2e over the real bridge.
No count moved; no migration.

**Proven live, and a defect it exposed, fixed:** the first watch of
`digilog/rtc/time` received the 12:07 and 12:08 ticks together at 12:09:03 —
the bridge had queued them while reconnecting (QoS 1, `clean: false`) and
flushed them late. A gateway setting its clock from those would be two
minutes wrong. `MqttBridgeHandle.publish` now REFUSES a non-retained publish
while the client is offline (`bridge offline — event not queued`) and still
queues retained state, which may wait. Pinned in `e2e/mqtt-rtc-sync.test.ts`.
The change event on `…/children/attributes` gets the same protection: a
stale attribute change is dropped rather than replayed, and the retained
per-child slot still carries the state.

## `…/children/attributes` is a CHANGE EVENT, not a retained bundle (2026-09-05)

Operator, on seeing the retained whole-set bundle arrive the moment the
gateway subscribed: *"when user subscribed all the instruments attributes
values are sending once, i dont need like that, when ever any instrument
attribute value was changed send at that time only"*. So the topic built that
morning is reshaped: `instruments/<gw>/children/attributes` is now published
ONLY when a child's attribute changes (in the app, or from a device report),
with `retain: false` (`EVENT_PUBLISH_OPTIONS`; `publishRetained` gained an
`options` parameter, default unchanged), carrying ONLY the changed key under
the child's `devN` — `{"gateway","devices":[{"devN":"<code>","<key>":"<value>"}]}`,
`null` for a removed key. (First cut of the reshape carried the changed child's
complete set; the operator's next message, *"only changed key should sent"*,
took it down to the key alone within the hour. The per-child slots still carry
the complete set.) One message per key. Then *"remove the time stamp"* — `ts`
is gone too; the message is `gateway` + `devices` and nothing else. Link, unlink and a
gateway's own edit publish nothing there; membership stays the roster's. The
per-child slots stay RETAINED, so a device that wants state on connect still
has it. **Assumption, stated:** the event carries the changed child only; if
every child on every change is wanted, that is a one-line switch in
`buildChildAttributeChange`. The retained copy on the local broker was
cleared with `scripts/clear-child-attribute-bundles.ts` (zero-byte retained
publish); the seed script is deleted. Tests reshaped: 3 unit, 3 e2e (one
asserts `retain === false` off the captured publish options — "not retained"
is the whole point). The Connection instructions panel calls it the Change
topic.

## Attribute REPORT: the device → platform attribute topic (2026-09-05)

Operator: *"create two topics for attributes, one will i publish one will i
receive"*. The receive side already existed (the bundle,
`instruments/<gw>/children/attributes`). This adds the publish side:
`instruments/<code>/attributes/report`, in the telemetry batch's shape with
attribute values where readings would be — flat for an instrument's own
attributes, a `devices` list or a flat `devN` block from a gateway for its
children. New module `modules/instruments/attribute-report.ts`; the bridge
dispatches the topic BEFORE its own-downlink check (which would otherwise
swallow it, since it contains `/attributes/`).

**A device write is not a person's write, and the code says so.** Every
accepted key is audited as the NEW action `INSTRUMENT_ATTRIBUTE_REPORTED`
(audit actions 97 → **98**, templates 91 → **92**; a SYSTEM action — no user —
with the reporting device's code in the row and a fixed reason). An UNCHANGED
value is neither written nor audited, so firmware re-reporting its
configuration every minute does not fill the hash chain. Which keys a device
may write is ADMINISTERED — new setting *Device-writable attribute keys* on
the existing `instrument-attributes` def (blank = any key, the operator's
choice); a refused key is dead-lettered by name. The role-based attribute
gate is not consulted: a device is not a role, and the list is the control
that stands in for it. After the commit the per-instrument slot and the
gateway's bundle are republished, so the device reads back what the platform
holds. `report` joined `MQTT_RESERVED_TOPIC_SEGMENTS` (a child coded
`X/report` would have its downlink read as a report). ACL publish grant
widened; local broker restarted; **AWS needs the same.** The Connection
instructions panel shows the report topic and a sample for both kinds. No
migration; no count moved but the two audit registries. Tests: 5 unit, 8 e2e
over the real bridge and database.

## Gateway: ONE CHILD PER MESSAGE — a flat payload with `devN` routes to that child; samples keyed `t` / `h` (2026-09-05)

Operator: *"make temperature key as t and humidity key as h"*. The live
`telemetry-slots` alias lists already accepted `t` and `h`, so the platform
change is to every sample payload (Connection instructions panel,
`LOCAL_SETUP_WINDOWS.md`): `{"t": 21.5, "h": 47}`.

**Found in the data while checking the keys, and fixed:** since 12:09 today
the gateway IOTGW01 had been publishing each sensor as its own FLAT message on
its own topic — `{"devN":"CWH/RDU/002-00","id":2,"ty":2,"t":"20.3","h":"60.9"}`,
no `devices` wrapper — and the ingest, seeing no batch, stored all of it as
the GATEWAY's own readings: 110 rows keyed `id`/`ty`, 104 keyed `devN`, on
IOTGW01, with the children named in `devN` receiving nothing. That is the
plant firmware's real form. `ingest-core.ts` now treats a GATEWAY's flat
payload that carries a string `devN` as a one-block batch: routed to that
child through the same child map, `devN` stripped, a foreign `devN`
dead-lettered. A gateway's flat payload WITHOUT `devN` is still its own
reading (`{"rssi": -60}`), and a non-gateway's `devN` is still just a key —
there is no child map to route through, and inventing one would let any
device write for any other. `id` and `ty` are firmware fields of unknown
meaning and are stored as readings under those keys, as before. **The 110 +
104 rows already on IOTGW01 stay** — telemetry is a §11 record and is never
deleted to tidy a mistake; they are readings from before the form was
understood. Pinned by a new e2e in `gateway-ingest.test.ts` (child gets
`t`/`h`/`id`/`ty`, never `devN`; gateway gets nothing; gateway's own flat
still lands; foreign `devN` dead-lettered). The panel shows this
one-child-per-message form for a gateway beside the batch.

**Proven live within minutes of the reload:** the gateway's messages naming
`CWH/RDU/001-00` now land on that child; the ones naming `CWH/RDU/002-00` are
dead-lettered against IOTGW01 with *"not linked to gateway"* — because **no
instrument is coded `CWH/RDU/002-00`**; the registered code is
`CWH/RDU/002-01`. That is a firmware or registration mismatch for the operator
to settle, and the dead-letter log on IOTGW01 is where it shows.

**A second defect found in the same messages, fixed:** the device's own
timestamp arrives as an epoch STRING (`"ts":"1788599495138"`), which
`new Date(string)` cannot read, so every reading was silently stamped with its
ARRIVAL time — measured 43 s late on a §11 record. `parseDeviceTs()` in
`payload-parser.ts` now reads a 13-digit string as milliseconds and a 10-digit
string as seconds (the two widths firmware emits), for the envelope and for a
per-block `ts` alike; ISO strings and epoch numbers behave as before.
`device-ts.test.ts` (6).

## Gateway batch: a LIST of blocks, each naming its instrument under `devN` (2026-09-05)

Operator, pasting the gateway's `mosquitto_pub` batch: *"send it instrument id
as value for devN key … devN is common key for all, value will change"*. The
gateway firmware emits a list of sensor blocks with the identity INSIDE each
block under one common key, so the batch may now be:

```json
{"devices":[{"devN":"CWH/RDU/001-00","temperature":22.5,"humidity":54},
            {"devN":"CWH/RDU/002-00","temperature":23,"humidity":43}]}
```

`parsePayload` folds the list onto `dev1`, `dev2`, … (the position is only a
slot, and that name is what a rejection reports); `fanoutDevices` resolves each
block's code from a string `devN` and strips it from the readings — an identity
is not a measurement. Without `devN` the outer key is the code exactly as
before, so the code-keyed object still works. Both shapes pass through the same
child-map authorisation — a gateway still writes only for its own linked
children, and a block naming a foreign instrument is dead-lettered by CODE.
`devN` wins over the outer key when both are present; a non-string `devN` is a
rejected block naming its slot; an empty `devN` falls back to the key.
**"Instrument id" here is the instrument CODE** (the wire's identity since
2026-09-04), never the UUID — no UUID fallback, by the operator's earlier
choice. (An `id`-keyed numbered-object shape lived for about an hour the same
day and was replaced by this before anything used it.) The Connection
instructions panel shows the list shape as THE batch example. Tests: 8 unit
(`gateway-fanout-slots.test.ts`, parser + fan-out), 1 e2e in
`gateway-ingest.test.ts` (both shapes, the foreign-code dead-letter). Docs:
`LOCAL_SETUP_WINDOWS.md` §9A.3, `docs/recreation/06-api/endpoints.md`.

## Child attributes BUNDLE: every child's attributes in one retained message per gateway (2026-09-05)

Operator: *"when ever i changed multiple instruments attributes, how it will
send back to gateway instrument all the linked instruments to one topic"* →
*"one message for all children with full set, go"*.

A third retained downlink slot per gateway, `instruments/<gw>/children/attributes`,
carrying EVERY child's complete attribute set, plus the one change that
prompted the publish (`changed`, `value: null` for a removal, `null` for a
membership-driven republish). **Its shape is the telemetry batch's, mirrored**
(operator, later the same day: *"can u do same for attributes also"*): a list
under `devices`, each block `{"devN": "<code>", "<attribute>": "<value>", …}`,
and `changed` as `{devN, key, value}`. (The first cut keyed children by code
under `children` with a nested `attributes` object; replaced within the hour,
before any device read it. `isActive` went with it — the roster carries the
flag, and a block is its attributes alone as a telemetry block is its readings
alone.) The per-child slots and the roster STAY —
this sits beside them, not instead of them, so a device reading per-child slots
keeps working and the "MQTT retains only the last message per topic" recovery
property is carried by the bundle being the whole set every time. Under
`/children/`, because `instruments/<gw>/attributes` is the gateway's OWN
attribute slot. Republished from the same two places the per-child downlink
and the roster publish (`announceAttributeChange`, `announceRoster`), cleared
with the roster on gateway delete/demote. New module
`modules/instruments/child-attributes-bundle.ts` (pure builder + publisher +
loader); `scripts/publish-child-attribute-bundles.ts` seeds the slot for every
gateway (dry run by default). ACL: the device subscribe line gained
`instruments/${clientid}/children/attributes`; the local broker was restarted;
**the AWS broker needs the same edit and restart.** No count moved; no
migration. Tests: 6 unit (payload), 4 e2e (wiring, incl. "standalone edit
publishes no bundle"). `LOCAL_SETUP_WINDOWS.md` §9C.1 documents the wire shape.

**The Connection instructions panel now shows the attribute PAYLOADS** the
way it shows the telemetry sample (operator: *"show the payload for attributes
… same like telemetry"*): under "Attribute updates (platform → device)", each
downlink topic is followed by its subscribe command and a sample payload with
the instrument's real codes and example values — the per-instrument slot
(`attributes` + `changed` + `ts`), and for a gateway the whole-set bundle and
the roster too. Only on the MQTT/MQTTS tabs, since only the broker can be
subscribed to. 3 new render tests (45 in the file).

## Instrument History widget on the Instruments page (2026-09-05)

Operator: *"same like trends page time series, provide one widget same like
that in All instruments page, in that widget provide Block and Area and
instrument selection if user want Area wise instruments history report he can
download from there all instruments in that area, and also multiple selection
and download report for only selected instruments"*. Two decisions put to them
and taken: one PDF **section per instrument**, and a **full merged readings
table** on screen (which needed a new endpoint).

**New endpoint `GET /api/instruments/telemetry-history`** — the merged, paged,
newest-first readings of several instruments (`getMultiInstrumentHistory`).
Pivoted in SQL, one row per (instrument, instant) carrying every key reported
at it, so a page boundary can never split an instant's temperature from its
humidity; `total` counts instants. Values are RAW and unfiltered by key: which
key is an instrument's temperature is per instrument (`telemetry-overview`
says), and a site-wide alias filter here would silently drop an instrument
whose keys have drifted. **Visibility is applied to the ID SET** before the
query — an out-of-scope instrument is absent from rows and count, never a 403.
Pinned by `e2e/telemetry-history.e2e.test.ts`, including the scope case
against the OPERATOR fixture. No new module, permission, model or route file;
`INSTRUMENT_READ` gates it like its siblings. Registered before `/:id`, as
`/telemetry-overview` is.

**The widget** (`routes/instruments/history-widget.tsx`) is a DASHBOARD PANEL,
`dashboard_history`, placed directly under the readings table (operator, later
the same day: *"all instruments report widget comes in dashboard not in
instruments page, in dashboard below the all instruments readings table"* — it
was first mounted on the Instruments page and moved). New catalogue entry in
`@digilog/shared` `PANELS` (frozen snapshot updated), a row in
`DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_LAYOUT` at y 9 with the floorplan and alarms shifted down,
in `AUTO_HEIGHT_PANELS` (it ends at its pager like the table), and rendered by
`routes/dashboard/index.tsx` inside a `PanelCard` with eyebrow `History`. In
`embedded` mode the widget drops its own header — the card owns the title — and
portals Block, Area, Interval and the download into the card header through
`usePanelToolbarSlot()`, the same portal the readings table uses; the period
presets and custom range stay in the body because seven buttons and two date
inputs cannot share a header that must not wrap. Assignable per role and per
user on Roles & Access → Panels like every other panel.
**`appendMissing` changed for it, for every panel from now on:** a panel a
STORED layout does not know used to be appended at the bottom, which would
have put this one under the floorplan and the alarms on every layout ever
saved. It now lands directly under the panel that precedes it in the shipped
layout, shifting the rest down; the bottom only when that predecessor is not
on the layout. Pinned in `dashboard-layout.test.ts`. It is the trend page's
Time Series card for many instruments. Block and Area selects (the Alarms
page's pattern, not a tree widget); a tick list of the instruments in scope —
**once a Block or Area is chosen, everything in it is selected until something
is unticked**, so "the whole Area" and "these three" are one control
(`history-selection.ts`, pure and pinned; ticks from a previous Area are
dropped, and re-ticking the last one collapses back to "all"). **With no scope
chosen nothing is selected**: the list is then the whole plant, and a default
of "everything" would fire a plant-wide history query for every visitor of the

## Data Report: bigger and bolder, a full interval schedule, faults in bold, the interval in the dialog (2026-09-05)

Operator, in two messages against the pushed 2026-09-04 report: *"in data report
make headings to center and in header, and increase font sizes and thickness"*,
then *"latest time values comes first, which ever value is crossed the limit that
value should show bold in report, and if there is not data at that interval show
NA, and also if i selected time period and downloaded report then its showing
where data is available but how i need is at which time it started that was first
data point and from next on as per interval it should come if 5 minutes then after
5 minutes data packet should come like that and also remove header on header,
interval selection should come at data report time period selection below on top
of remarks, Error and OL also show bold"*.

**Typography is now PER-REPORT, and the Data Report opts up.**
`lib/pdf-report.ts` gained `ReportTypography` + `DEFAULT_TYPOGRAPHY` (the exact
values every report printed at before) and `ReportConfig.typography` for
overrides. `DATA_REPORT_TYPOGRAPHY` in `data-report.ts` raises the company name,
title, labels, table body and table headings, prints the company name and title
BOLD, and CENTRES the column headings (`headStyles.halign`, which `columnStyles`
never reached — the headings sat left over centred cells). Body readings stay
regular, as the reference's do. The alarm, trend and audit reports print
byte-for-byte as before, and a test pins that the shared default did not move;
the shared `tablePt` ceiling (ten portrait columns on the alarm report) is why
this is an override rather than a global bump. The parameter block's label
column widened 26 → 32 mm (`scopeColumnStyles` gained a `labelWidth` parameter;
its default is unchanged) so `Temp. Limit :` does not wrap at 10 pt — a wrapped
label reads as two fields.

**A defect found on the way, fixed for every report:** autotable's default
margin is 40 pt = 14.11 mm while the rest of the chrome sits on a 14 mm gutter,
so every table started 0.11 mm inside the title bar and the 182 mm parameter
block overran the page by 0.22 mm — autotable logged "could not fit page" on
every Data Report. Tables now take the chrome's own gutter.

**The rows are a SCHEDULE anchored on the first reading, every slot printed,
newest first** (`scheduleRows`, replacing `firstPerInterval`). With an interval:
the first row is the earliest reading in the period; each later slot is one
interval on, to the period's end inclusive; a slot holds the FIRST stored
reading inside it or nothing, and an empty slot prints `NA` in both value cells
at the time the reading was due — a gap in a log is information. At Raw every
reading prints. Both orders are newest first (the reference's oldest-first was
transcribed on 2026-09-04 and reversed today on the operator's instruction).
`NA` is keyed in the legend only when a cell printed it, the same rule as NMT.
`recordCount` in the audit row counts printed rows, gaps included.

`addTable` gained `bold[row][col]`, applied through autotable's `didParseCell`
so `body` stays plain strings and the review snapshot stays re-renderable.
`dataReportCell` decides each cell with the on-screen table's precedence: out of
the probe's span → the administered out-of-range word; non-numeric → the
administered failure word; no reading → `NA` (regular); otherwise the number,
bold iff `outOfSpec`. The words come from `useSensorWords()` via the caller —
no literal in the report code. Mutation-checked: removing the bold hook, the
typography, the app-name switch, or changing `NA` to a dash each turn the suite
red.

**Consequence: the Data Report now reads the WHOLE period on the paged path,
at Raw too.** Until today the Raw report was built from the sampled chart path,
which drops a non-numeric reading BEFORE sampling — so the failure word could
never have appeared at Raw. The sampled call is still made (for `historyTotal`
and the whole-range extremes), then every stored reading is read once, sized by
that count, and pivoted with `toTableRowsWithErrors` — the on-screen table's own
builder. The REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLE disclosure remains for the case where the
paged fetch returns fewer than the total; the existing 2,000-row cap notice
covers the rest. `numericRows` is no longer used on this path.

**"Remove header on header" → the app-name line under the company name is
gone from this report** (`ReportConfig.showAppName`, default true; only the Data
Report sets it false). Assumption, stated: the reference carries the site line
and the title with nothing between them, and the second stacked heading is the
one element of ours it lacks. If the operator meant the blue accent strip at
the top of the page instead, that is a one-line change in the same place.

## The trend page's Time Series download is the DATA REPORT (2026-09-04)

Operator: *"for time series widgets there is report download option in trend
page, that report should be like data report template i need same like that
details, table template everything"*. Reference: `Data Report.pdf` at the repo
root. Same approach as the Alarm Report (2026-09-01): the reference's shape,
transcribed from its own text into a pure module, laid onto the shared chrome.

**What prints now** (`routes/instruments/data-report.ts`, rendered by
`renderDataReport` in `trend-report.ts`): the site header; the title
"Temperature and RH Data Report"; a two-column parameter block — Block / Area /
Location / Inst ID against Start Date / Start Time / End Date / End Time, then
`Temp. Limit` against `RH Limit`, `Temp. Max … , Temp. Min …` against `RH Max … ,
RH Min …`, and `Interval` alone on the right; a four-column table DATE, TIME,
TEMPERATURE (°C), RELATIVE HUMIDITY(%), oldest first; the legend (Temp, RH, and
NMT / NLT only when a printed limit uses the word); Printed By, Printed Date &
Time and the Remarks box from `createReport()`. `pdf-report.ts` untouched. The
parameter block reuses the alarm report's `scopeColumnStyles`, so the two
documents' centre lines land in the same place.

**Interval rows are FIRST STORED READINGS, never averages** (operator, choosing
the recommended option). With an interval selected on the page, the report prints
one real reading per bucket, buckets aligned to the period START (the reference's
rows run 16:36, 17:36, 18:36 from a 16:36 start). At Raw every reading prints.
`firstPerInterval` is pure and pinned: every returned row IS an input row.

**Two fetches when an interval is set, and why.** The sampled chart path
(`points=`) supplies the period's true row count and the whole-range extremes;
"first reading in the bucket" then has to be judged over EVERY reading, not over a
sample that may not hold it, so the paged table path — which has had no ceiling
since 2026-09-02 — is read once, sized by that count. At Raw the sample is the
rows and, when the period holds more than came back, the report says so in a
REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLE note, as the trend report does.

**Deliberately NOT copied from the reference**
- Dates and times are the ADMINISTERED formats (`useDatetimeFormat`), not its
  `27-05-2026` / `16:36` — the same call the alarm report made.
- A limit prints at the instrument's own precision through `formatSetPoint`
  (`NMT 27.0`, `NLT 18.0`, `18.0 - 27.0`), the way every screen prints it; the
  reference's `NMT 27` is its own system's rounding.
- Temp. / RH Max and Min are the SERVER's extremes over every reading in the
  period (`summaries`), never of the printed rows — with an interval selected a
  maximum over the printed rows could sit below an excursion between two of them.

**Placement facts**: Block and Area are resolved BY ID through
`/api/functional-locations` (`resolveBlockArea`, the same walk the alarm report's
`useFilterScopeLabels` makes), Location is the instrument's `Location` ATTRIBUTE
(`overview.locationAttribute`, never the superseded column), Inst ID is the code.
Note the Instrument Trend PDF still prints the drawn ROOM under "Location"; that
document was not touched here.

**Audit type UNCHANGED** — `Instrument Time Series` — so rows already logged under
it stay one report's history; the filename becomes `data-report-<code>-<date>.pdf`.
`recordCount` is the number of rows printed.

**Removed**: `renderTimeSeriesReport`. **Tests**: `data-report.test.ts` (19, against

aligned to the period start, the whole period is fetched before bucketing, the

## [Unreleased] - MQTT client id is the instrument CODE (2026-09-04)

Operator: *"35dd00b3-240d-4604-a054-00dd79024386 this is CWH/RDU/001-00
instrument mqtt client id, i want client id as CWH/RDU/001-00"*. Confirmed:
code ONLY, no UUID fallback; and remove the hand-added `#` grant for that UUID.

**What the wire looks like now.** Client id = `code`; publish to
`instruments/<code>/telemetry`; subscribe `instruments/<code>/attributes` (a
child: `instruments/<gatewayCode>/attributes/<code>`; a gateway:
`instruments/<code>/attributes/#` and `instruments/<code>/children`). A code may
contain `/` — 100 of the 101 here do — and the broker substitutes `${clientid}`
literally, so the slashes are simply topic levels.

**Why this was the UUID for four weeks, and why that reason no longer applies.**
On 2026-08-07 the code became free text, and a code of `+` or `#` in the ACL
template `instruments/${clientid}/…` matched EVERY instrument. The wire moved to
the platform-generated UUID so nothing typed reached a topic. This change puts
operator text back in the topic, so the guard comes back at REGISTRATION instead:
`instrumentCodeTopicViolation()` in `@digilog/shared` refuses `+`, `#`, NUL, and a
LAST segment of `telemetry`/`attributes`/`children` — applied by the zod schema,
`bulk-csv.ts` (as an error row, not an exception) and the create form (which
otherwise reports a zod-flatten 400 as "Could not create the instrument."). 0 of
the 101 existing codes are affected.

**The reserved-word rule is not decoration.** The bridge now subscribes
`instruments/#` (`+` is exactly one level and cannot reach a slashed code) and
reads the topic KIND from the last segment. A child coded `X/telemetry` would have
its attribute downlink published on `instruments/<gw>/attributes/X/telemetry`,
which parses as telemetry from an instrument coded `<gw>/attributes/X`.
`isDownlinkTopic` drops the bridge's own retained slots SILENTLY — a log line per
slot per reconnect would bury a real drop — and a test pins that a telemetry
topic whose code contains `attributes` is never mistaken for one.

**Code:** `mqtt-auth-routes.ts` (clientid = code, UUID DENIED), `mqtt-bridge.ts`
(`instruments/#`, prefix/suffix parse, lookup by code), `attribute-downlink.ts` +
`child-roster.ts` (topics keyed on codes; `AttributeDownlink.code`/`gatewayCode`),
`instruments/routes.ts` (resolves the gateway code for downlink and roster),
`connection-instructions.tsx` (client id and every topic = code; the `id` and
`gatewayId` props are gone, and `TokenDialog` no longer takes `id`),
`create.tsx` (client-side refusal with the reason), the two demo scripts.
New `scripts/migrate-mqtt-topics-to-code.ts` clears the UUID-keyed retained
slots and republishes them code-keyed (dry run by default) — run locally:
102 cleared, 102 published.

**Broker:** `emqx-5.3.2/etc/acl.conf` — bridge subscribe and publish grants are
`instruments/#`; the 2026-09-03 TEMPORARY TEST GRANT for client id `35dd00b3-…`
(publish/subscribe on `#`, a bypass of the whole binding for one device) removed.
EMQX restarted (it was down when this started). **The AWS broker needs the same
edit and restart when this deploys.**

**Proven live against the running broker and bridge (8/8):** connect as
`ZZ/PROOF/…` accepted; a reading published on `instruments/ZZ/PROOF/…/telemetry`
landed on that instrument; subscribe to own attribute slot granted, to another's
refused; publish to another's telemetry topic landed nothing; connect with the
UUID refused (`Not authorized`); a valid token under another instrument's code
refused; a fresh device saw no foreign retained message. The two throwaway
instruments were created and deleted with audit rows.

**Consequence to act on:** the one device connected in the last 7 days
(CWH/RDU/001-00, direct MQTT, last seen 2026-09-03) is on the UUID and is refused
at CONNECT until reconfigured with `CWH/RDU/001-00` as client id and
`instruments/CWH/RDU/001-00/telemetry` as topic.

**Tests:** shared schema +8, `mqtt-topic.test.ts` rewritten (11), `bulk-csv` +1,
`attribute-downlink` +1, `child-roster` +1, `e2e/mqtt-auth` +2 (slash code
allowed, UUID denied), `e2e/mqtt-ingest` +2, downlink/roster e2e rekeyed,
`connection-instructions.test.tsx` rekeyed (42). No count moved — no model,
enum, migration, permission, reauth action, config def, page or route.

## [Unreleased] - Ingest accepts a `values` envelope (2026-09-03)

Operator: *"still data was not coming to temperture and humidity"* — for
`CWH/RDU/001-00`, receiving `{"h":"46.3","t":"25.7","id":3,"ty":3}`.

**The diagnosis, which the database gave outright.** That instrument stored
`temperature` and `humidity` — 1149 rows each — until 2026-09-01 15:12:56, and
since then stores a SINGLE key `values` of type `json` holding the whole object.
All 102 other instruments still store `temperature`/`humidity`. So the device
changed format in the field: it now publishes `{"values": {...}}`, and the flat
parser read `values` as the one reading key. Data was arriving the whole time and
being stored under a key nothing reads. The temperature/humidity cells were blank
not because ingest was broken but because `t` and `h` never existed as keys.

**The near miss worth recording:** the first check ran the FLAT payload the
operator had pasted through `parsePayload`, saw `t`/`h` resolve correctly, and
concluded the pipeline was fine. It was the payload that was wrong, not the
parser. A pure-function test that uses the bytes you *believe* are on the wire
proves nothing about the bytes that are.

**The fix.** `parsePayload` gains a third shape. No count moved — no model, enum,
migration, module, config def, page, route, permission or reauth action; one pure
function learned one shape.

- **Unwrapped ONLY when `values` holds an object AND the payload carries no other
  reading keys.** `{"values":{"t":1},"t":25}` is ambiguous, so it is NOT unwrapped
  and both are stored. Unwrapping there would silently DISCARD the outer reading,
  which is the one failure mode a §11 ingest path must not have. A `values` that
  is a number, string or array is an ordinary reading and is left alone.
- **The envelope's contents are readings VERBATIM.** `ts`/`quality` are defined at
  the TOP level only, so an inner `ts` is stored as a reading rather than being
  silently dropped or silently honoured as the record's timestamp. Inner-`ts`
  support was deliberately NOT added: no device here sends one, and a timestamp is
  what a §11 record is anchored to — a second source for it needs a real payload
  to test against.
- **An empty envelope yields zero readings**, exactly as a bare `{}` already does.
  No new rejection path was invented.
- **Hardcoded, not administered.** `telemetry-slots` administers key NAMES; this is
  payload SHAPE. `payload-parser.ts` is deliberately PURE — no database, no imports
  — and threading a config value in for one vendor would cost the property that
  makes it cheap to test and impossible to break from a config screen. If a second
  envelope name turns up, make it a config THEN.

**Verified against the live device, not just in tests.** After the reload, readings
land as `h`, `t`, `id`, `ty`; the last `values`-keyed row falls out of the window.
32 tests (22 parser + 10 ingest) and every ingest e2e — `instrument-ingest`,
`gateway-ingest`, `mqtt-ingest`, `tcp-ingest`, `ws-ingest`, `gateway-fanout` — run
individually by exit code; `tsc --noEmit` clean. Three mutations, all caught:
removing the branch fails 8 (across BOTH files), unwrapping unconditionally fails
2, accepting an array fails 1.

**The write-path test is the load-bearing one.** `ingest-core.test.ts` asserts on
the rows handed to `writeBatch`, not on the parser's return value — the parser test
alone would not have caught the original defect, for exactly the reason above.

**NOT done: the 64 pre-fix `values` rows were left alone.** The readings are intact
inside the stored JSON and can be recovered whenever wanted, but inserting derived
`t`/`h` rows into a regulated table alongside the originals is a separate decision
with a duplication question attached, and nobody has asked for it.

## [Unreleased] - The browser tab is named and iconned from config (2026-09-03)

Operator: *"in the favicon tab option rename it as T&RH-Monitoring and also this
rename is give as configuration and also that icon also should be changebale in
configuration"*.

Two new settings on the EXISTING `branding` config — `tabTitle` (default
`T&RH-Monitoring`) and `faviconUrl` — plus one new upload route. Applied at runtime
by `apps/web/src/lib/document-identity.ts`, called from `useBranding()`.

**No count moved.** 35 models, 12 enums, 42 permissions, 48 reauth actions, 24 API
modules, 30 config defs, 23 config pages, 50 routes — all re-derived, all unchanged.
There is no migration, no new permission and no new reauth action: these are
settings on a def that already exists and an endpoint inside the `uploads` module
that already exists, the same precedent as the four `alarm-limits` enable-attribute
settings. The one count that DID move is `apps/web/src/lib/` 19 -> 20, for the new
module.

**`tabTitle` is deliberately NOT `appName`.** They have always been different
strings — the shipped `<title>` read "Compliance Core - Instrument Monitoring &
21 CFR Part 11" while `appName` read "DigiLog" — and `appName` is what the sidebar,
the header and the login card print. Folding them would have renamed three visible
surfaces nobody asked to rename. **Found while verifying: this installation had
ALREADY set `appName` to `T&RH-Monitoring`** (and `logoText` to `TRH`), and the tab
still said Compliance Core, which is very likely what prompted the request. The two
now read the same here while remaining independently settable.

**A blank title is refused, not fallen back on.** Same rule as every other
administered wording in this app: the only fallback is the SHIPPED default, never
another field and never an empty tab.

**The favicon follows the BACKGROUND's pattern, not the LOGO's** — uploaded to disk
with only the path stored (`.max(512)`), because a branding change is audited and an
inlined data URI would land twice in a §11 before/after record. A favicon is small
enough that a data URI would have worked; the audit record is the tiebreaker, not
the file size.

**Its own upload route rather than a reuse of `/branding-background`**, which writes
to the same directory and would have "worked". The two differ in what they ACCEPT: a
favicon is the one case where an operator reaches for a `.ico`, so
`POST /api/uploads/branding-favicon` passes `FAVICON_TYPES` (the shared list plus
the two mime types Windows uses for an icon). Folding them would have admitted
`.ico` as a page background and a profile photo too, for nothing. The shared
validator gained an `allowed` parameter rather than being forked, so the four upload
routes still cannot drift into one of them being the weakest.

- **SVG is refused and must stay refused.** `/uploads/branding/` is in
  `PUBLIC_GET_PATHS` and served from the API's own origin; an SVG can carry script,
  so accepting one would be same-origin script execution reachable by anyone holding
  `CONFIG_UPDATE`. Pinned by a test that says so.
- **A `.cur` renamed to `.ico` is refused** — the two share the ICONDIR header and
  differ only in the type word, so all four magic bytes are matched.
- The UUID filename gives every upload a fresh URL, which is what defeats the
  browser's very aggressive favicon caching. No cache-buster was added.
- The previous favicon is NOT deleted, same rule as the background: it may still be
  named by an audited before-value, and a §11 record pointing at a missing file is
  worse than an orphaned image.

**The icon `<link>` is REPLACED, not mutated.** A browser does not reliably repaint
the tab when an existing link's `href` is merely rewritten; removing the element and
appending a fresh one is the recipe that is honoured. Asserting on the attribute
alone would have passed for the version that does not work, so the test asserts the
element IDENTITY changed and the old one is disconnected. It still ends with exactly
one link per rel and SKIPS the swap when the href is already correct, because several
components call `useBranding()` on one page.

**The client-side file check is deliberately LOOSER than the server's.** A `.ico`
frequently arrives with an EMPTY `file.type` — the browser could not map the
extension — and a bare `!file.type.startsWith('image/')` guard therefore rejected the
exact format the separate route exists for, before the request was made, under a
message listing ICO as accepted. It now refuses only what the browser positively
identifies as a non-image; the server's magic bytes are the boundary.

**`BRANDING_TAB_TITLE_DEFAULT` is exported from `@digilog/shared`** and used by the
zod default, `defaultBranding` and the Branding page's placeholder and preview. This
repo's rule is that no component may default a label to a literal — the
`alarmTypeName()` / `coerceTrendWidgetTexts()` precedent. `index.html` is the one
unavoidable hand-kept copy: it is read before any JS runs.

**`apple-mobile-web-app-title` follows the title too** (the name under an iOS
home-screen icon). It is a `<meta>`, not the manifest, so "baked at build time" does
not cover it and it would otherwise sit on the previous product name for good. The
applier never INVENTS the tag.

**Both icon `<link>`s are rewritten, and the `type` hint with them.** Leaving
`apple-touch-icon` on the shipped logo would surface later as "the home-screen icon
is still the old one"; and the static tag ships `type="image/png"`, so swapping in an
`.ico` while still advertising PNG is the mismatch that presents as "I uploaded my
icon and nothing happened".

**Deliberately NOT changed — the PWA manifest.** `vite-plugin-pwa` bakes
`name: 'DigiLog - 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance'`, `short_name: 'DigiLog'` and its icons
at BUILD time. An installed app's name and icon changing underneath the user is not
something a config write should be able to do, and it cannot be done at runtime
anyway. The INSTALLED PWA therefore still reads DigiLog; the browser tab does not.

**Verification.** 359/359 shared, 27/27 API upload routes, 16/16 jsdom applier tests,
8/8 on the new config card, plus `src/e2e/config.test.ts`, `auth.plugin.test.ts` and
every web test touching branding, each run individually and measured by exit code.
`tsc --noEmit` clean on api and web; `vite build` clean. **15 mutations across four
groups, every one caught:** wrong `rel`, unconditional title, missing blank guards,
missing type rewrite (5/1/1/1); ICO dropped from the allow-list, ICO magic bytes
shortened so a cursor passes, the CONFIG_UPDATE gate removed (3/1/1); the shipped
default changed, `.min(1)` dropped, the 512 cap raised to `logoUrl`'s (2/1/1); and
mutating the href instead of replacing the element, dropping the
skip-when-unchanged, dropping the iOS meta, restoring the strict client guard
(2/1/1/1). Probed against the RUNNING server:
`GET /api/config/branding` already returns both new keys with their defaults filled
into the pre-existing row, and `/api/uploads/branding-favicon` is in the live
OpenAPI document.

**NOT verified: nothing was seen on screen.** The operator holds the browser session.
The full `apps/web` suite cannot be used as evidence either way — it reported 38, then

`[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"`, and **100 of those were with my
