## [Unreleased] - Inactivity alarms: raised when an instrument goes quiet, cleared when it returns (2026-08-31)

Operator request. A THIRD alarm source beside `RULE` and `INSTRUMENT_LIMIT`.

**Why this is not four alarm rules.** `AlarmRule` already supports
`metric: 'OFFLINE'` and the evaluator already handles it — it has simply never
been switched on (the database holds ZERO alarm rules). Four rules, one per
Block, would have worked with no code. They were not chosen because a
location-targeted rule cannot reach an instrument with no functional location —
there is one today, and every freshly commissioned device is one until somebody
assigns it AND remembers the rule exists. This source covers every instrument
with nothing to author.

**Counts.** Config defs **25 → 26**. Shared type files **18 → 21** — one is this
feature (`inactivity-alarms.ts`); the other two (`dashboard-layout.ts`,
`panel-style.ts`, `telemetry-period.ts` net) were already stale in
`packages/shared/CLAUDE.md` and are corrected here, not caused here. Everything
else UNMOVED and re-derived: 36 models, 13 enums, 42 permissions, 48 reauth
actions, 24 API modules, 24 config pages, 51 routes, 20 hooks, 19 lib modules.
`AlarmSource` gains a VALUE, which is not a new enum.

**Two hand-authored migrations**, `20260831120000_inactivity_alarms` (the enum
value) and `20260831120001_inactivity_unique_active` (a partial unique index,
one ACTIVE inactivity alarm per instrument, mirroring
`alarms_active_instrument_limit_unique`). SEPARATE on purpose: Postgres refuses
to use a newly added enum value in the transaction that added it. Both applied to
`compliance_core_db` and `compliance_core_db_test`; the `DROP TABLE
instrument_telemetry_history` Prisma emitted was stripped, as in the previous
fifteen; drift guard **PASS**.

**It ships OFF, and that is the opposite of `alarm-limits`.** `loadLimitConfig`
reads `enabled !== false`, so an absent row means ON. `loadInactivityConfig`
reads `enabled === true`. The failure modes are not symmetrical: a limit feature
failing closed stops watching for excursions, while this one failing OPEN raises
one alarm per silent instrument — 101 on this installation right now, each with a
notification, a webhook fire and its own e-signature to acknowledge.

**The clear signal is PRESENCE, and this inverts the instrument-limit rule.**
There, a missing reading HOLDS an alarm open, because absence cannot prove
recovery. Here absence IS the alarm, so presence is the proof. A pass written by
copying the limit pass's shape inherits its `continue`-on-null and strands every
inactivity alarm ACTIVE for good — which looks like working software until
somebody asks why nothing clears. `inactivity-decide.ts` is a separate module
with the asymmetry written into both, and five e2e cases fail if it is lost.

Also decided and tested:
- **A grace period, default 15 minutes**, because `activeWindowMinutes` is 3 here
  and no instrument declares an interval, so a 30-second blip crosses it. The
  grace delays RAISING only — a returning instrument clears on the next pass.
  **The effective threshold is the LATER of the grace and the activity window**,
  since the pass needs both conditions; setting a grace shorter than the window
  changes nothing. Said so on the config page.
- **An instrument that has NEVER reported does not raise.** It has not gone
  inactive; it was never active, and no telemetry is coming to clear it.
  Decommissioned instruments do not raise either — but an alarm already open on
  one still CLEARS if it starts reporting, because retiring an instrument must
  not strand an unanswered outage.
- **Severity defaults to MAJOR, not CRITICAL.** Losing sight of an instrument
  says the record has a hole in it; an instrument-limit alarm says the product
  went out of specification. Ranking them the same makes the ranking useless.
- `graceMinutes` is **clamped** on read, not trusted: a row edited by hand could
  otherwise carry a negative (raise on everything) or a NaN (compares false
  against every threshold and raises on nothing, silently).
- The snapshot freezes `graceMinutes`, the `activeWindowMinutes` in force,
  `expectedIntervalSec` and `lastSeenAt`. The window is administered live, so an
  inspector asking why an alarm fired must get the threshold as it stood.

**On the Alarms page:** Type reads `Inactivity` (checked BEFORE the limit branch,
or it falls through to "offline out of limit", which is not a limit); Value is
"—" because it was raised by the absence of a reading; Limit reads `quiet > 15m`
from the frozen snapshot. The `OFFLINE` type filter is relabelled `Inactivity`
and still matches on `metric`, so ONE token catches both these and any
rule-based offline alarm — two overlapping tokens would make an operator choose
between two spellings of one question.

**Boolean config settings are now an on/off TOGGLE, not a checkbox** (operator).
New `components/ui/toggle.tsx`, swapped in at `dynamic-config.tsx`'s boolean
branch — which changes EVERY dynamic config page, deliberately: one control
style everywhere is the point. A checkbox states an intention a Save button
commits; a toggle reads as something already done, which is the right reading for
"raise alarms when an instrument stops reporting". `Checkbox` stays where it
belongs — the multi-select option list on the same page still uses it. Built on a
real `<input type="checkbox">` with `role="switch"`, so keyboard and
screen-reader behaviour is the platform's rather than re-implemented.

**One test-design bug found and fixed while writing this.** The first e2e file
passed every "does not raise" case for the wrong reason: the TEST database
carries the default 1440-minute activity window, not the live 3, so an instrument
silent for 120 minutes still counted as REPORTING. It now pins
`instrument-activity` and restores it, the same discipline
`instrument-scope-selection.test.ts` applies to `telemetry-slots`. Worth naming
because a green suite was hiding it.

Verified: api `tsc` clean, web `tsc` clean, `vite build` clean, shared rebuilt.
API **210 tests / 17 files** over the alarm modules, workers and every alarm e2e,
including 17 new unit and 14 new e2e tests. Web **898 tests / 64 files**.
`verify-migrations.ps1`: **PASS — migrations reproduce the reference schema
exactly**. Mutation-checked: replacing the clear branch with the limit pass's
"absence holds it open" failed 8 tests across both files.

**NOT visually verified** — the operator's session was live throughout, so the
new config page and the toggle have not been seen rendered.

## [Unreleased] - Alarms: a browser-fillable e-signature, and the Acknowledge button off-screen (2026-08-31)

Operator, reporting three things. Two of them were one bug.

### The e-signature password was being filled by the browser

**This has regulatory weight.** 21 CFR §11.200 requires a signature to be
executed by its owner; a password the browser types means anyone standing at an
unlocked workstation can acknowledge an alarm as whoever the browser remembers.
The field looks completely normal while it happens.

`routes/alarms/acknowledge-dialog.tsx` used
`<input type="password" autoComplete="off">`. **Chrome deliberately ignores
`autocomplete="off"` on credential fields** — the password manager was built to
override sites that opt out. That is the whole bug, and it also explains the
second report: a `type="password"` input that is NOT inside a `<form>` makes
Chrome scan the entire document for something to treat as the username field. It
found the Alarms **search box** and typed the logged-in username into it the
moment the dialog opened. That looked like a defect in the search box and was
not.

`components/reauth-dialog.tsx` already carried the defence — the acknowledge
dialog, written later, simply did not. It has been extracted to
**`components/ui/signature-password-input.tsx`** and BOTH now use it, so there is
one implementation rather than a protected copy and an unprotected one. Four
measures, each defeating a different heuristic and all needed together: mount as
`type="text"` and become `type="password"` a tick later (this is the one that
actually stops the fill); `autoComplete="one-time-code"`, which Chrome honours;
a `name` generated per mount, since a stable name is a key a credential can be
saved against; and `secureField`, blocking copy/cut/paste/drag.

New `components/ui/__tests__/signature-password-input.test.tsx` asserts the four
**separately**, because a simplification that drops one still passes a test that
only checks the others. Mutation-checked: disabling each measure in turn failed
its own test and no others.

The search input also gained `name="alarm-search"` and `autoComplete="off"` —
belt and braces, not the fix. An unnamed text box with no autocomplete hint is
what Chrome reaches for when it goes looking for a username.

### The Acknowledge button was off the right of the screen

- **`Generated Value` and `Cleared Value` headers are stacked onto three lines**
  (word / word / unit legend). On one line they were the widest headings on the
  page and set their columns' width. Separate blocks, not a wrap, so the break is
  identical at every viewport width. `Acknowledged by` stacks too, and the Type
  cell now wraps to two lines as the mockup draws it.
- **The action column is PINNED to the right edge** (`sticky right-0`, with its
  own background and an edge shadow). The stacking above narrows the table, but
  twelve columns will still overflow a small enough screen — and the one thing
  that fell off the end was the page's only action. A table you must scroll
  sideways to acknowledge an alarm from is a table nobody acknowledges alarms
  from. This makes the button reachable regardless of width, rather than hoping
  the width now fits.

**No count moved** — `signature-password-input.tsx` is under `components/`, which
is not one of the counted directories (`hooks/`, `lib/`).

Verified: web 891 tests / 64 files, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean.
**The width fix is NOT visually verified** — the operator's session was live, so
whether the button now sits on screen at their viewport is unconfirmed; the
pinned column is what guarantees it is reachable either way.

## [Unreleased] - Alarms page rebuilt: server-side search, range, sort and paging (2026-08-31)

Operator supplied `Alarms.png` and asked for the page to look like it.
**No count moved** — re-derived 2026-08-31: 36 models / 13 enums, 42 permissions,
48 reauth actions, 24 API modules, 25 config defs / 24 config pages, 51 routes,
20 hooks / 19 lib modules. No migration.

Files: new `apps/api/src/modules/alarms/list-query.ts` (+ tests) and
`apps/api/src/e2e/alarm-list-filters.e2e.test.ts`; new
`apps/web/src/routes/alarms/{alarm-stat-cards,alarm-filters}.tsx`;
rewritten `apps/web/src/routes/alarms/index.tsx`; extended
`alarm-display.ts` and its tests; `apps/api/src/modules/alarms/routes.ts`.

**The bug the redesign exposed.** The page filtered and counted IN THE BROWSER
over `GET /api/alarms?limit=500`. The four state boxes therefore counted the
newest 500 alarms while reading as plant-wide totals, and the existing comment
defended this as a feature ("a box's number and the list under it can never
disagree"). Adding a date range inverts that reasoning: a range that predates the
oldest fetched row would have returned nothing while looking like it had
searched. This is the same shape as the `GET /:id/telemetry` truncation fixed
2026-08-27 — a `limit` and a range meeting in one query.

**`GET /api/alarms` now filters, counts, sorts and pages server-side.** New
params `search`, `from`, `to`, `type`, `status`, `severity`, `page`, `pageSize`,
`sort`, `dir`; the response gains `total` and `counts`. The legacy `state`,
`acknowledged`, `instrumentId`, `functionalLocationId` and `limit` params all
still work — the dashboard's selection panel and the trend page's alarms widget
send `limit`, and it is now an alias for `pageSize` with the same 500 ceiling.

- **`total` is DERIVED by summing the four quadrant counts, never counted
  separately.** The quadrants partition the filtered set exactly (unit-tested), so
  a card's number and "showing N of M" are answers to one question and cannot
  race each other against a live evaluator.
- **The status filter is excluded from the count query and only the count query.**
  Choosing a box must not zero the other three, or an operator could never see
  what they were about to switch to. Every other filter narrows the counts too, so
  the boxes always describe what is listed.
- **A bad filter is a 400, not a shrug.** An unreadable date or a reversed range is
  refused by field; silently dropping the bound would list alarms from outside the
  range under a header saying the range was applied. An unknown SORT key falls back
  instead — it changes the order, not which rows.
- **Every fragment is ANDed, never merged** (`buildAlarmWhere`). Search and the
  location filter both want an `instrument` key; merged, a later key would replace
  an earlier one and widen the result — which, since visibility scoping composes
  the same way, is the shape of an access-control bug.
- Row payload gains `instrumentName`, `locationName` (the FUNCTIONAL location) and
  `roomLabel`, for the new Location / Room column.

**The page**, per the mock: four gradient state cards with icons, a filter bar
(search, raised-between, type, status, a Filters button revealing location and
severity), a dark-banner table with sortable headers, a Location / Room column,
two-line timestamps, unit-bearing values, a per-row state accent, and pagination.

Seven deliberate departures from the mock, each agreed with the operator first:

1. **No sparkline and no "↑ 2 from yesterday".** Nothing in this system stores
   alarm-state history, so both would have to be inferred from the rows on screen.
   An invented trend on a monitoring screen is worse than no trend.
2. **No ⋮ row menu.** The page has one row action; a menu that opens to a single
   item is more clicks than the button it replaced.
3. **Pagination is the canonical `<Pagination>`**, not the mock's `« ‹ 1 2 › »` —
   `pagination.tsx` documents one style everywhere.
4. **The table's dark banner is painted from `var(--theme-primary)`**, not a
   hardcoded indigo, so it follows all ten colour presets.
5. **The page icon keeps `PageHeader`'s theme-tinted tile**, not a crimson gradient
   shield; that component exists to stop per-page gradients.
6. **Cleared-Unacknowledged is AMBER, not the mock's blue** (the mock's own table
   pills were amber; only its card was blue). It is the overnight excursion nobody
   answered for and must not read as neutral. Active-Acknowledged takes the blue.
7. **The Instrument ID stays dark, not severity-coloured.** Every alarm on this
   installation is CRITICAL, so a coloured ID would be red on every row — no
   information, and it makes an identifier look like a status. The left accent bar
   and the status pill carry state instead.

**Two more defects fixed on the way.** The status pill was keyed off `severity`,
so on an installation where every alarm is CRITICAL every pill on the page rendered
red regardless of state; it now takes the four-state tone. And a FAILED request
rendered "No alarms have been raised." in the table underneath the error banner —
a statement about the record, made while the record could not be read, which on a
monitoring screen reads as "nothing is wrong". That one was found by the new render
test, not by looking. The Status dropdown and the four cards read and write the same
value, so they cannot disagree.

A third: SWR's `keepPreviousData` leaves the last good rows on screen with `error`
set on any failed revalidation, and calling that "could not load alarms" over a full
table is plainly false. The two failures are now worded apart — a stale refresh says
the list may be out of date; only a first load with no data says it could not be
loaded.

New `apps/web/src/routes/alarms/__tests__/alarms-page.test.tsx` mounts the real page
(13 tests). Its fixture deliberately returns ONE row against counts of 16/2/8/0 —
what a paged response actually looks like — so a card that counted the rows in hand
would show 1 and fail.

**Removed as dead:** `filterByQuadrant()`, `quadrantCounts()` and `filterByTab()`
from `alarm-display.ts`, with their tests. The first two are what produced the
window-limited counts; a comment stands in their place saying so, because the
obvious "improvement" for a future reader is to reintroduce them.

The four state counts come from ONE `groupBy` rather than four `count()`s:
`_count.acknowledgedAt` counts non-null values, which IS the signature axis, so
grouping by `state` and reading `_all` against it yields the whole 2x2 in a single
pass — and four separate counts would be four separate points in time beside a live
evaluator.

**The counts are visibility-scoped, and that is proved rather than assumed.** They
come from a `groupBy`, which is a different query path from the `findMany` behind the
rows, so "the rows are scoped" is not evidence the boxes are — and this module's own
docstring names the summary counts as part of what the scope withholds. Five e2e
cases drive the seeded OPERATOR (SUPER_ADMIN short-circuits visibility, so an
admin-driven version would pass against a route with no scoping at all) with a
one-instrument scope, and assert that `counts` and `total` describe three alarms
rather than six, that another filter does not widen it, that searching for an
out-of-scope instrument code returns nothing, that an EMPTY selection means see
nothing, and — as a positive control — that an unrestricted role still sees all six.

Verified: web 887 tests / 63 files, `vite build` clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean on
both apps; API 172 tests over the alarm modules and e2e including 22 new ones in
`alarm-list-filters.e2e.test.ts`. Both new test files were mutation-checked rather
than trusted for being green — four deliberate breaks (orderBy tiebreak removed,
empty location array dropped, reversed-range guard disabled, visibility dropped from
the count query) each failed the tests written for them, and the positive control
kept passing.

## [Unreleased] - Alarms page reworked: four-state filter, units, duration (2026-08-29)

Operator request, several parts. **No count moved.** Files:
`apps/web/src/routes/alarms/{index,alarm-display}.tsx|ts` and its tests.

- **Heading only.** The descriptive paragraph under "Alarms" is gone. The
  breadcrumb (`Home / Alarms`) was KEPT — it is navigation, not prose, and every
  other page carries one; say so if it should go too.
- **The Active/History tabs and the "Unacknowledged only" checkbox are replaced by
  FOUR filter boxes**: Active Acknowledged, Active Unacknowledged, Cleared
  Acknowledged, Cleared Unacknowledged. Selecting one filters the table; selecting
  it again clears the choice. **Nothing selected shows EVERYTHING** — with only
  four boxes and no "All", defaulting to one would have opened the page having
  silently hidden three quarters of the alarms.
  - The two axes stay separate in the model (`quadrantFor` composes `tabFor` and
    `needsAcknowledgement`). Cleared-but-unacknowledged — the overnight excursion
    nobody saw — remains its own state, which is the whole reason the page never
    collapsed them.
  - Counts come from the SAME rows the table can show (the request is capped at
    500), so a box's number and the list beneath it cannot disagree.
- **Severity column removed** from the table; `Instrument` renamed **Instrument ID**.
- **Readings carry their unit**: `28.0 (°C)`, `47 (%RH)`, on the triggering value
  AND the cleared value. Implemented as `triggeredWithUnit`/`clearedWithUnit`
  ALONGSIDE the existing `triggeredText`/`clearedText`, which still return the bare
  number and are what the tests pin — "the value" and "the value as displayed" stay
  separate so a wording change cannot quietly alter what a §11 record is understood
  to say the reading was. A missing reading stays as an em dash rather than
  becoming "— (°C)".
- **The "N instruments have no usable limits set … IOTGW01" banner is gone.** The
  separate "Limit alarms are turned off" banner was KEPT — different message, and
  it says no limits are being checked at all.
- **New Duration column, after Status**: raised → cleared as `HH:MM` plus a unit
  letter, `00:01M` / `01:22H`. Header carries the legend.
  - **Days are deliberately never used**: a three-day excursion reads `72:00H`. An
    hour count stays directly comparable between rows; `3d 04:00` does not, and
    comparison is the point when ranking excursions by exposure.
  - An alarm that has not cleared shows an em dash, not a running total: the
    operator asked for the span between generated and cleared time, and a number
    that keeps moving in a column of settled ones reads as a closed figure. Tooltip
    says why. Easy to change to a live elapsed time if that is wanted.
  - Reversed or unparseable timestamps return the dash rather than a negative.

**The new pure logic is tested (44 in this file, up from 28) and the tests were
mutation-checked**, not just observed green: breaking the paperwork axis in
`quadrantFor` failed exactly 3 of them, and restoring it returned all 44. This
repo has shipped vacuous tests before, so a green run on new logic is not by
itself evidence.

## [Unreleased] - Set Point text darkened (2026-08-29)

Operator: the limits are too light to read. **No count moved.** Files:
`app.css`, `routes/dashboard/telemetry-table.tsx`.

`.tv-spec` was `#64748b` (slate-500) at 12px — **4.76:1, which passes AA on
paper** and was still reported as hard to read. Worth recording as a judgement,
not just a value change: a set point is the number the reading is compared
against, so it has to be legible, not merely compliant. Now `#334155` at 13px,
semibold: 10.4:1 on both zebra tones.

The size moved INTO `.tv-spec`. The cell previously carried a Tailwind
`text-[0.75rem]`, which could never have taken effect — these rules are unlayered
and outrank every utility (see the block header). A utility that cannot win reads
as if it applies and is worse than none, so it is gone and the size has one home.

## [Unreleased] - Readings: green in spec, red box on a breach (2026-08-29)

Operator: "temperature and humidity font colors should be green colors, if it
cross the limit then it should be red color and make box background red".
**No count moved.** One file: the `.tv-*` block in `app.css`.

- Both channels read **green** while within limits. This replaces the rule from
  earlier the same day where the value took its COLUMN's hue, so temperature read
  **orange while perfectly in spec** — and orange is the colour of a warning
  everywhere else in this product, so a good reading looked like a mild alarm.
- A breach now takes the **whole cell**: red ink on a red field (#991b1b on
  #fecaca, 5.9:1) with a bar down the edge, instead of red text alone.
- `.tv-val-temp` and `.tv-val-rh` stay separate although currently identical —
  they are the hooks for per-channel treatment if it is wanted again; merging them
  would mean re-threading the component to bring it back.

**⚠ The specificity here is load-bearing.** The zebra rules are
`.tv-row:nth-child(odd) > td` — weight (0,2,1) — which OUTRANKS a bare
`.tv-val-bad` at (0,1,0), so the obvious one-class rule would have been overruled
and a breach would have kept its striped background. The breach selectors are
written as `.tv-row > td.tv-val-bad` (and a `:hover` twin) so they match that
weight, and they sit after both the zebra and hover rules, which settles the tie.
If a future edit "simplifies" these back to `.tv-val-bad`, the red field silently
stops appearing on every other row.

Unchanged and deliberate: which readings count as a breach still comes from
`outOfSpec`, the same rule the alarms agree with, so the colouring and the
"out of spec only" filter cannot disagree.

## [Unreleased] - Tabular / Graphical toggle restored; Arrange is SUPER_ADMIN-only (2026-08-29)

Two operator requests. **No count moved.** Files:
`routes/dashboard/{index,panel-grid}.tsx`.

### The view toggle is back

Removed on 2026-08-28, restored on 2026-08-29 on the row BENEATH Arrange (new
optional `toolbar` slot on `PanelGrid`). **Tabular is the default**; Graphical
swaps in the floorplan. It reads `?view=` again — in the URL like `fl` and `agg`,
so a graphical view is linkable and survives a refresh. Anything other than
`graphical` reads as table, so a hand-edited URL degrades to the default rather
than a blank slot.

- **It governs only the two READING panels.** Trend and Alarms show in both views:
  they answer questions that are not about how you happen to be looking at the
  readings.
- **The toggle appears only when there is something to switch between** — a role
  that cannot see the floorplan panel gets no toggle, rather than a button that
  empties the grid.
- **⚠ Hiding a panel must not delete it, and this is the trap:** react-grid-layout
  reports only the items it was GIVEN, so filtering the items and then pressing
  Arrange + Save would persist a layout with the other reading panel MISSING — and
  a panel absent from the layout never comes back. `onGridChange` merges the hidden
  item back into the draft at its stored position. **Exercised in the browser, not
  just reasoned about:** switched to Graphical, saved a layout while the table was
  hidden, switched back — the table returned.

### Arrange is SUPER_ADMIN-only

`canArrange` on `PanelGrid` gates the whole edit session, not just the button:
`interactive` is ANDed with it, so nothing can be dragged even if edit mode were
somehow entered. The saved arrangement still APPLIES to everyone — this governs
who may CHANGE it, not who may see it.

**Client-side only, and worth knowing:** `PUT /api/config/my-dashboard-layout`
still accepts a user's own layout, so a non-super-admin could set one by calling
the API directly. That is not a privilege escalation — the layout affects only
that user's own dashboard — but if the intent is that non-super-admins can never
have a custom layout, the route needs the same gate. Not done, because it was not
asked for and it would change an endpoint every user currently relies on.

**Not verified in the browser:** the non-SUPER_ADMIN path. There is no second
account whose password is known here; the gate is a one-line role check and tsc
passes, but nobody has watched a non-super-admin load the page.

## [Unreleased] - Instrument Readings rebuilt to the SECOND screen-2 reference (2026-08-29)

`screen-2.png` was **replaced at 18:29**, ten minutes after the table was built to
its first version, with a materially different design. This entry supersedes the
previous one. Check the image's mtime before assuming the code drifted from it.
**No count moved.** Files: `routes/dashboard/{telemetry-table,use-telemetry}.tsx`,
`app.css`.

What changed from the first version: **gradient headers, each with an icon**;
**zebra rows** instead of per-column body washes; the hue moved **into the reading
itself** rather than the cell behind it; **unit suffixes** (°C, %) on the values; a
**Filters** control; and a **rows-per-page + pager** footer.

- **The reading takes its column's hue while in spec — and red still wins on a
  breach.** Every row in the reference happens to be within limits, so the image
  cannot show what a breach looks like; adopting hue alone would have silently
  deleted the only limit signal left on this screen (Status reports online/offline,
  not spec). Both states are decided by `outOfSpec`, the rule the alarms agree with.
  Verified live: "out of spec only" returns 17 rows carrying 18 red readings — one
  row breaches on both channels — so the filter and the colouring cannot disagree.

- **Header gradients run between two contrast-passing steps.** 11px bold uppercase
  is NOT "large text" under WCAG, so it needs 4.5:1 on white; the reference's tones
  measure 3.1-3.6:1. Each gradient's lightest end still passes. Do not flatten
  these to the image's raw values.

- **The trend cell is an ICON, not a sparkline.** The reference draws a little line
  per row. A real one needs each instrument's HISTORY, which
  `/api/instruments/telemetry-overview` does not return — 101 rows would mean 101
  history requests — and a decorative squiggle shaped like a chart would be read as
  data it is not. It links through to the true series.

- **Room names are clamped to two lines.** This install's instrument names run past
  70 characters ("Working standard & reference Standard storage Room (or) stability
  Room"), which wrapped to six lines and made one row as tall as four. Full text on
  hover.

- Filters and paging are **client-side**: the overview payload is already the whole
  visibility-scoped set in hand, so paging costs no request and cannot disagree
  with the counts beside the search box. Page number is derived and clamped, never
  stored — a stored page survives a filter that shortens the list and strands the
  reader on an empty screen.

Verified on :5176 against 101 live rows: 25 per page, pager advances (page 2 starts
CWH/RDU/026-00), status filter returns 0 for Online (all 101 are offline, matching
the header count), refresh revalidates, console clean. tsc clean; 131 dashboard
tests pass.

  codebase forbids. Values stay in-spec green / breach red via the same `outOfSpec`
  the alarms agree with — the breach signal the dark table carried is preserved.

⚠ The `.tv-*` rules are **unlayered**, so they beat every Tailwind utility whatever
its specificity. Every cell background comes from `.tv-*` and never from a `bg-*`
class; mixing the two means the utility silently loses.

Verified on :5176 against 101 live rows: all nine columns fit without horizontal
scroll, codes stay on one line, 101 status pills and 101 trend links render, the
refresh button revalidates, and the console is clean. tsc clean; 131 dashboard
tests pass.
