## [Unreleased] - Technical audit remediation: backup, migrations, audit immutability (2026-08-29)

Acts on the CRITICAL and HIGH findings of `docs/audit/2026-08-29-technical-audit.md`.
**No count moved**: no model, enum, permission, reauth action, audit action, module,
config def, config page or `<Route>` was added or removed — re-derived, unchanged.
One new env var (`AUDIT_HARD_DELETE_ENABLED`), one new npm script
(`check:migrations`), and no migration.

### Backup exported every telemetry reading twice (HIGH — silent data corruption)

`getAllTables()` discovered tables with a bare
`SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public'`.
`instrument_telemetry_history` is `PARTITION BY RANGE (ts)` with one child per
month, and **`pg_tables` lists the partitioned parent AND every child**, because a
partition is an ordinary table. Measured on `compliance_core_db` on 2026-08-29:

```
instrument_telemetry_history           226,582 rows
instrument_telemetry_history_2026_08   226,582 rows   ← the same rows
pg_tables (public)                          42 relations
after the fix                               38 relations
```

So export dumped each reading twice, restore inserted both copies (inserting into
the parent routes the row into its child, then the child's own dump adds it again),
and the `BACKUP_MAX_ROWS_PER_TABLE` pre-flight counted both, tripping at half the
real budget.

**It never threw.** It produced a plausible archive with corrupt contents and a
restore that silently DOUBLED a 21 CFR Part 11 telemetry record. The original audit
said backup would "likely fail outright" at production volume; that was wrong in the
safe direction, and the report has been corrected. A silent corruption is worse than
a loud failure.

Discovery now scans `pg_class` with `relkind IN ('r','p') AND relispartition = false`
— parent kept, children dropped. Backing up the parent is version-proof: a row
inserted into it is routed to whichever partition covers its `ts`, so an August
archive restores into a database whose partitions have since rolled forward.

**Backward compatible, and self-healing:** restore derives its work list from
`dbTables.filter(t => Array.isArray(data[t]))`, so an older archive still carrying
partition keys now has those keys skipped and each reading inserted once. Old backups
are repaired by this fix, not broken by it. **Forward direction needs care:** a new
parent-only archive restored by PRE-fix code trips `BACKUP_INCOMPLETE` naming the
partitions and needs `force=true`. Upgrade the code before relying on a new archive.

### Backup/restore had zero e2e coverage (HIGH)

The disaster-recovery path of a regulated system, the most raw-SQL-heavy module in
the codebase, had 3 unit tests and no e2e. New `src/e2e/backup-restore.e2e.test.ts`:
10 tests covering discovery, single-copy export, a full export→restore round trip
asserting unchanged row counts, and a canary row proving the restore actually
replaced data rather than no-opping.

Confirmed non-vacuous by reverting the fix: 5 of the 10 fail, and the export
assertion reports **9,844 rows for 4,922 real readings — exactly 2×**.

### A migration guard for the table Prisma wants to drop (CRITICAL)

`instrument_telemetry_history` is absent from `schema.prisma` because Prisma cannot
express `PARTITION BY`, so `prisma migrate dev` / `db push` generate
`DROP TABLE "instrument_telemetry_history"` for it — taking every stored reading,
with no other copy in the system.

This is **recurring, not theoretical**: fifteen committed migrations carry a comment
from an author who had just stripped that DROP by hand. It has been generated on
essentially every migration since 2026-08-08 and removed manually each time. It only
has to be missed once.

New `apps/api/src/lib/migration-guard.ts` (pure, no DB), asserted by
`src/lib/__tests__/migration-guard.test.ts` so it runs inside `npm test`, plus
`scripts/check-migration-safety.mjs` for CI and as a gate on `npm run db:migrate`.
Proven to exit 1 on an injected violation and 0 on the clean tree.

**It deliberately does NOT add a Prisma model to silence the DROP.** Prisma would
then emit a plain `CREATE TABLE` for a fresh environment, producing an UNPARTITIONED
table, and ingest would stop dead at the first month boundary when Postgres rejects
every row falling outside a partition range. That trades a loud, one-off migration
hazard for a quiet, recurring runtime one. The reasoning is written at the top of
`migration-guard.ts`.

### Audit hard-delete is now switchable, and the trigger dance has one home (HIGH)

The product ships two endpoints that disable the `audit_trail_no_delete` trigger and
physically delete §11 records, breaking the tamper-evident hash chain. They are well
governed — `AUDIT_DELETE` permission, reauth, 5/min rate limit, meta-audit row
written first — but 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(e) calls for an audit trail that cannot be
modified or obscured, and `bulk-redact` already covers the legitimate "this content
must not be retained" case without breaking the chain.

Whether to keep the capability is a QA/regulatory decision, so **the default is
unchanged**. `AUDIT_HARD_DELETE_ENABLED=false` (that exact string only — a typo must
not silently remove a governed capability) makes both routes answer
403 `AUDIT_HARD_DELETE_DISABLED` and point at redact. Checked before reauth, so a
disabled install does not prompt for a password to refuse the action anyway.

**Known gap, recorded not hidden:** the switch is backend-only. The Audit Trail page
gates its delete button on the AUDIT_DELETE *permission*, not the flag, so with the
flag off a permitted user still sees a button that 403s. Closing it properly means
the server telling the client, not the client re-deriving — see `.env.example`. An
install turning the capability off should also revoke `AUDIT_DELETE` from every role.

Also consolidates the trigger disable/enable dance, which existed in three copies,
into `lib/audit-immutability.ts:withTriggersDisabled`, with the re-enable moved into
a `finally`. Not a live bug — Postgres DDL is transactional, so a throw rolled the
ALTERs back — but it made §11 immutability depend on an invariant nothing stated.

### The four untested modules, and two 500s they exposed (HIGH)

`notification-rules`, `user-groups`, `admin-requests` and `debug-traces` had **zero
tests**. The first two decide who gets told when an instrument goes out of spec;
their failure mode is silence. Three of the four were also **unreachable from the
suite** — registered in `app.ts` but not in `src/e2e/test-helper.ts`, so no e2e could
have called them even if one had been written.

83 new e2e tests, concentrating on failures that would be invisible: that group
membership is really persisted and that deleting a group audits the membership it
destroyed; that a rule's recipients are REPLACED on update but left alone when the
key is omitted, so renaming a rule cannot silently unsubscribe everyone; that
`GET /:id` in debug-traces stays registered after the static routes it would
otherwise shadow. For `admin-requests` the tests pin the 2026-05-20 enumeration
hardening, which had none: identical response shape and 200 whether or not the user
exists, and no email/department/role/status ever returned.

Two real defects surfaced, both fixed centrally in `lib/errors.ts`:

- **P2023 → 400** (was 500). `id` columns are `uuid`, so
  `findUnique({ where: { id: 'not-a-uuid' } })` made Postgres fail to parse the value
  and Prisma threw before the route's own 404 check could run. In production that
  also dispatched a SYSTEM_ERROR notification for an ordinary bad request.
- **P2025 → 404** (was 500). Routes letting Prisma signal "no such record"
  (`findUniqueOrThrow`, bare `update`/`delete`) all answered 500 for a missing row.

Both sit beside the existing P2002 → 409 in a new `prismaErrorToResponse`, covering
every uuid-keyed route rather than the handful the tests touched. That function is
now shared with `src/e2e/test-helper.ts`, whose error handler is a reduced copy of
the real one and had **omitted the P2002 translation entirely** — meaning no e2e
could observe the status a client actually receives for a Prisma failure. Pinned by
`src/lib/__tests__/prisma-error-mapping.test.ts`; the suite's existing 409
assertions all came from explicit `ConflictError` throws, never from a P2002 reaching
the handler, so the mapping could have been deleted with every test still green.

### Verification

`apps/api` `tsc --noEmit` clean. Full API suite **1735 passed / 0 failed across 134
files** (single-fork, against `compliance_core_db_test`).

### Still open

**H3's posture decision** — whether `AUDIT_HARD_DELETE_ENABLED` should default to
`false` — is with QA/RA, along with the frontend affordance gap noted above.

## [Unreleased] - UI redesign, Stage 2: applying the design system (2026-08-28)

Stage 1 (`7ed8329`) built the tokens and the missing primitives and migrated **no
pages**. Stage 2 is the migration. **No count moved**: no model, enum, permission,
reauth action, audit action, module, config def, config page or `<Route>` was
added or removed — re-derived, unchanged. This is presentation only; no endpoint,
query, permission gate or business rule was touched.

### The font was never applied

Stage 1 added Inter as a self-hosted dependency (`@fontsource-variable/inter`) and
set it as `--font-sans`, but `body` reads `--font-body`, which named **Sora,
fetched from `fonts.googleapis.com`** by a `<link>` in `index.html`. Inter was
downloaded, bundled and rendered nowhere — and the faces that *were* applied came
from a CDN this application's factory network may have no route to, falling back
to `system-ui` on exactly the machines Stage 1 self-hosted a font to protect. Both
font variables now resolve to the bundled Inter and the CDN link is gone.

### Converged in one place rather than page by page

- **Radius** — `--radius-sm/md/lg/xl` **aliased** onto `--radius-control`/`--radius-card`,
  not deleted: Tailwind generates `rounded-lg`/`rounded-xl` from them and those
  appear ~700 times, so deleting would have silently dropped the radius from every
  one. `rounded-2xl`/`3xl` rewritten across 59 files.
- **Form controls** — `.ctl`, `.ctl-sm`, `.ctl-check`, `.ctl-radio` in `app.css`;
  134 raw controls across 43 files rewritten onto them. Only `className` was
  touched. The focus ring reads `--theme-primary`, so all ten colour themes now
  reach the form controls; the hardcoded green/cyan/blue/indigo rings it replaces
  reached none.
- **Type** — 37 `<h1>` and 23 `<h2>` onto the two scale tokens. Twelve titles used
  `bg-clip-text`, which renders lighter than solid ink, so the largest text on
  those screens had the weakest contrast on them.
- **Elevation** — five Tailwind shadow steps (279 uses) onto the three `--elev-*`
  layers across 73 files, tinted shadow colours dropped with them.
- **Tables** — `.tbl` gives the fifteen raw tables one header band, separator,
  hover and rhythm. It sets no alignment, size or cell colour on purpose:
  `.tbl th` would beat a `text-right` utility on the cell.

### Screens rebuilt

`dynamic-config.tsx` (which renders every auto-discovered config module, making it
the single biggest lever on that screen class), `config/index.tsx`, the sidebar
(collapsible icon rail), the header (its desktop left half was an empty spacer),
and the login page.

### Accessibility

Pinch zoom un-blocked (`user-scalable=no` fails WCAG 1.4.4). Dialogs gained focus
capture and restore, `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal` — previously a keyboard
user's Tab walked the page *underneath* the overlay. Toasts became a polite live
region: the entire save-confirmation channel had been silent to screen readers.

### Four defects that only appeared in a browser

`tsc`, `vite build` and 813 unit tests all passed over these; see
[[playwright-clicks-dont-land]] in memory for how the screens were finally driven.
Buttons wrapped to two lines and stopped matching the control height beside them;
the dashboard title was unreadable over the operator's wallpaper; config-card
affordances landed at a different height per card; and the login page overrode its
own `Input` primitive with `h-12 border-2`, rebuilding the look the primitive
exists to replace.

### The shared classes were outranking every utility (found in review)

`.ctl` and `.tbl` were added **unlayered**, and in the CSS cascade an unlayered
rule beats every layered rule *at any specificity*. Tailwind v4 emits utilities
into `@layer utilities`, so those classes silently outranked every Tailwind class
on the same element: `.tbl`'s zebra was erasing the `bg-amber-50/20` tint Admin
Requests puts on a PENDING row. Wrapping the selectors in `:where()` did not fix
it, because specificity was never what decided it. They now live in
`@layer components`. **Anything shared added to `app.css` must go in that layer**,
or call sites cannot override it.

Four more from the same review: the toast live region unmounted when empty (a
region must already be in the document for a mutation to be announced, so the
fix one commit earlier was still silent); the collapsed sidebar had no breakpoint
while its toggle is `md:flex`, stranding a tablet with an icon-only drawer and no
way to expand it; `.ctl` had been applied to the audit date fields, which sit
inside an already-bordered wrapper and so drew a second border and focus ring;
and `.ctl-check` was 18px against the `Checkbox` primitive's 20px.

### Buttons and status badges

**94 of 172 raw `<button>` migrated to `<Button>`** across 41 files, which is
what finally makes §9 true: one height, one radius, one focus ring, one disabled
treatment. The remaining 78 are *categorised, not skipped* — positioned overlays
inside another control, clickable cards, rows carrying a `group` class their
descendants style against, and inline micro-chips in dense rows where even the
32px size would not fit. See `tasks/ui-redesign-stage2.md`.

Three defects the migration script had to be taught, each caught by a gate or by
looking rather than by assuming: `hover:bg-slate-100` was being read as a
resting ground (handing bare icon buttons a permanent grey); collapsing
whitespace in the attribute region swallowed a `//` comment; and **the body
decides** — the dashboard's location entry cards are `<button>`s wrapping a
heading and a count, and `<Button>` collapsed them into 40px strips with the
text overlapping. That one was visible only in the browser.

**Segmented controls** (`.seg` / `.seg-btn`) replace four different treatments of
"pick one of these views". The active state is painted by `aria-pressed`, so a
segment cannot look selected while announcing nothing — most set no ARIA state
at all before.

**Status badges** onto `StatusBadge` (4 → 9 files), which pairs every status with
a dot as well as a word. The dashboard had carried a *fourth* alarm-severity
palette disagreeing with the Alarms page on two of four levels. The Users
table's role colours are deliberately untouched: those come from the database,
where an operator picks them per role.

Separately: **Disable and Delete** sat side by side in the same red on every user
row. Disable is amber now — two identical buttons an inch apart, one
irreversible, is how the wrong one gets pressed.

### Page headers, breadcrumbs, and empty states

**PageHeader adoption 2 → 32 pages; breadcrumbs on 34.** §24/§25. PageHeader
gained an optional `icon`, drawn in ONE treatment for every page — the theme's
own colour at a 12% tint — replacing nineteen per-page gradient tiles that had
made the page title compete with the status colours that carry meaning. The
back-chevron above the title went with them: the breadcrumb's parent link is the
way back, and two ways back a centimetre apart is one more than a screen needs.

Migrated with a JSX tag-matcher after a regex managed 2 of 41. It had to be
taught that the innermost `<div>` around an `<h1>` is the TITLE GROUP, not the
header row (picking it turned the description into an "action" and dropped the
icon), and that headers carrying action buttons are better done by hand than by
a re-indenting heuristic that produced valid, unreadable JSX.

**One functional regression, and how it was found.** On `contact-admin` the
script read an `<a href="/login">` back-arrow as the page's icon and dropped the
link — removing the only way back to login from a page a locked-out user
reaches. It also gave that unauthenticated page a "Home" breadcrumb that would
bounce a logged-out visitor into a login redirect. Caught by a script that
compares every link in each migrated file before and after; it flagged eight
files, seven of them false positives (the `/config` chevron, intentionally
replaced by a breadcrumb that links to `/config` as data rather than markup).
A check with seven false positives and one true one is still the check worth
having. Auth screens are now excluded by rule.

Table "Loading…" rows became `SkeletonRows`; empty rows became `EmptyState` with
a title, the consequence, and the action that fixes it — an empty Alarm Rules
table is not a neutral state, it means nothing is being watched.

**All 17 remaining spinners became skeletons**, each shaped like what it
replaces — the rule already written on the primitive is that a skeleton only
beats a spinner when it PREDICTS the layout. Table bodies use their real column
count (nine on the debug traces table, not a tidy five); card grids use their
real grid; System Health draws four stat tiles above a two-column card grid,
because a three-column grid of six would have been a placeholder for a layout
that never appears. Seven screens shared one loader — a tinted circle around a
spinner, each in its own accent — which is why they converted together.

Three are deliberately kept, with the reason in the code: the **app boot
splash** (nothing is known yet — the session has not resolved, so the page may
become the dashboard, a login redirect, a forced password change or the
super-admin lockdown screen), `<option>Loading…</option>` inside a select, and
the multiselect's inline caption. Verified by sampling the DOM during
navigation: the skeleton appears, a `role="status"` region announces it, and it
clears to zero with real rows in place.

### Section icons

**29 section-header tiles** onto the treatment Stage 1's `FormSection` primitive
already defined — `bg-slate-100 text-slate-600` in a control-radius square. Each
had picked its own saturated two-stop gradient (amber on one section of Password
Policy and indigo on the next, violet on Branding, cyan on Debug), and none of it
meant anything: these are parts of ONE screen, so what they need is hierarchy,
not identity. The page icon now carries the theme colour and the section icons
are quiet. Measured 6.92:1, past the 3:1 non-text graphics require.

Eight gradient chips sitting **inside form fields** went too — a tinted box in
front of a field competes with the value being typed into it, and the fields had
grown `pl-12 h-12` to clear them, a 48px control the system does not have.

**Semantic tints are untouched**: the red on an error banner and the emerald on a
success one carry meaning rather than decoration.

One bug introduced and caught here: the `text-white` strip ran file-wide rather
than per-tile, leaving glyphs dark on grounds that had NOT been recoloured (a
success dialog's emerald tile, an error dialog's red one). Repaired by diffing
against HEAD rather than guessing from surrounding markup — a heuristic would
have added white to icons that never had it — plus one by hand whose ground is an
inline `backgroundColor` no class-based sweep can see. An audit then proved all
30 remaining de-inked glyphs sit on quiet grounds.

### The last raw controls, and an unreachable page

The 23 "dynamic classNames" the `.ctl` pass had skipped were mostly not
conditional: 20 were `className={field}`, a single module-level constant per
file. That was the right instinct one layer too low — each dialog avoided
per-field drift internally while disagreeing with the rest of the application.
Three constants now point at `.ctl`, so their hardcoded slate and cyan focus
rings follow the site theme. Only two were genuinely conditional, and one of
them keeps its colour: `export-options`' cell tint ENCODES the chosen format.

**`/config/export-options` had no route.** Its config def declares
`customPagePath: '/config/export-options'` and the Configuration dashboard
renders a card pointing there, but nothing was ever registered — the card fell
through to the dashboard, so the page had never been reachable, which is also
why nobody had noticed it has no header. Registered with the sibling
`CONFIG_READ` guard (**Routes 50 → 51**) and given the standard header. This is
the failure mode memory already records: a config *page* existing here does not
mean it works.

Two more found on the way: the Dialog focus fix from earlier in this branch made
the global `:focus-visible` rule draw an accent ring around the whole panel
(unlayered rule beating a layered utility — the same cascade trap as `.ctl`), and
`alarm-webhooks` has two **hand-rolled** modals that never used the Dialog
primitive, so the `role`/`aria-modal` fix had missed them. Both now announced and
labelled.

### Deliberately excluded

`routes/dashboard/` panel-card geometry (tuned with the operator days earlier),
the `.tv-*` dark tabular view (operator preference, contrast measured across all
ten presets), `--chart-*` literal fallbacks (the PDF export serialises SVG with no
stylesheet), `border-2` on selection states (the width *is* the signal) and on
dashed drop zones. Remaining work is listed in `tasks/ui-redesign-stage2.md`.

## [Unreleased] - Per-card styling on the dashboard (2026-08-28)

Project C2 of two, completing the customisable dashboard. In **Arrange** mode each
card gains an **Edit** button: a colour from a bounded palette, and a custom
heading.

**No migration, no new endpoint, no count moved** except shared type files
**19 → 20** (`types/panel-style.ts`). Models 36, enums 13, permissions 42, reauth
48, audit actions 97, modules 24, config defs 25, config pages 24, `<Route>`s 50 —
re-derived, unchanged.

### A bounded palette, not a colour picker

Operator's decision, and the reason is this application's own rule: colour never
carries meaning alone here — every status is a colour PLUS a glyph PLUS a word.
Free hex would let someone paint an out-of-limit card green, or set text the shade
of its background.

Each tint therefore ships with its **own** text colour, chosen with it, and a test
asserts **WCAG AA (≥4.5:1)** for every pair — so the palette cannot grow unsafely.
A bounded palette is only safer than free hex if something actually checks the
bound. Posting a raw hex directly is refused, and the refusal drops only the
style: a bad colour cannot cost someone their arrangement.

**The tint styles the card's CHROME only.** Status badges, limit lines,
out-of-spec highlighting and chart series colours live inside the panels and are
unreachable from here. They encode compliance state, and a §11 record that looked
different depending on who arranged their dashboard would not be a record.

### It rides on the layout, deliberately

`style` is an OPTIONAL field on each layout item, in the same `dashboard_layout`
column. Colour and position therefore save together, reset together, and follow
the same not-audited rule — they are one preference about one card, and a
half-applied state (a saved colour on a card whose move was cancelled) should not
be reachable. Being optional is also why `LAYOUT_VERSION` did not need bumping:
every layout stored before this still reads.

### The trap, verified before it was written

**Fastify's ajv REMOVES body properties a schema does not declare.** Checked
against the running server: a `style` field absent from the schema came back
**200** and stored nothing — a save that reports success and silently loses the
operator's work. Fastify strips undeclared RESPONSE fields the same way. `style`
is declared in all three places a layout item is described on the wire, and an
e2e case pins the round trip.

### Verification

API **1600 passing / 127 files**, web **813 / 61**, shared **197**, `tsc` clean on
all three, `vite build` succeeds. Live against the real database: a tint and a
custom heading round-tripped, a raw hex was refused while the card's position
survived.

Not verified in a browser. **Neither the drag nor the colour picker has been seen
by anyone yet** — Playwright cannot authenticate against this install's
certificate.

## [Unreleased] - Draggable, resizable dashboard (2026-08-28)

Every assignable dashboard panel is now a grid item: drag to move, drag the corner
to resize, saved per user with a role default beneath. Project C1 of two; C2 (the
per-card edit dialog — bounded palette, status colours locked) is separate and
slots into the same edit mode. Spec:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-dashboard-layout-design.md`.

**One new dependency, one migration, no other count moved.** Models **36**, enums
**13**, permissions **42**, reauth actions **48**, audit actions **97**, API
modules **24**, config defs **25**, config pages **24**, `<Route>`s **50** —
re-derived, unchanged. Shared type files **18 → 19**.

### The Table | Graphical toggle is gone

Operator's call. A grid where each panel is independently placeable cannot also
have two of them sharing one slot behind a switch, and they were already two
separate keys in the panel catalogue. Both readings views can now be on screen at
once, or either dragged away. The `?view=` URL parameter went with it, and each
readings card now names the location in its own heading — under one shared heading
that was implicit; as separate cards it would otherwise be unclear which location
the numbers belong to.

### react-grid-layout, and the version trap

The first UI dependency this app has taken on in a long time, after `reactflow`,
`monaco` and `chartjs` were each removed. Deliberate: drag, resize, collision and
responsive reflow are weeks of fiddly work, and a half-working drag is worse than
none.

**Written against the 2.x API, which differs from every example online.** v2
replaced `isDraggable` / `isResizable` / `draggableCancel` with `dragConfig` /
`resizeConfig`, dropped `WidthProvider` for the `useContainerWidth` hook, and
requires an explicit `width`. It ships a `legacy` entry point keeping the v1
shape; this does not use it. Both stylesheets are imported — omitting
`react-resizable`'s leaves the drag working while the resize corner is invisible,
which looks like a broken feature rather than a missing import.

### Storage: two states, not three

Nullable `dashboard_layout` JSONB on `user_configs` and `role_configs` (migration
`20260828100000_dashboard_layout`, drift guard PASS, both databases). NULL on the
user row means "use the role default"; NULL on the role row means "use the
built-in". **Deliberately unlike `dashboard_cards` in the same tables**, where
`[]` is a deny that must never read as inherit — an empty layout is not an
instruction, and treating a corrupted value as "show nothing" would blank a
dashboard over a bad JSON write. The schema comments say so at both columns.

### A user's own layout is NOT audited

A role's default is. The split is the point: a hash-chained immutable §11 trail
filling with "moved a card 40px left" is one in which the records that matter get
harder to find, while an admin setting a role's default IS acting on other people
— the line this codebase draws everywhere else. The route carries a comment saying
the missing `auditLog` is deliberate, and the e2e asserts the absence in both
directions, so neither mistake can be made quietly.

### The bug the checkpoint caught

The first live run showed an unrestricted viewer resolving to **all nine** panel
keys — including the five that belong to the instrument *trend page*, which the
dashboard has no renderer for. They became empty boxes occupying grid space: four
cards and five holes. `resolveLayout` now considers dashboard panels only. Found
by running it against the real database, not by a test, which is why the
checkpoint was there.

### Also

Drag is off until **Arrange** is pressed, and off entirely below the `md`
breakpoint — a dashboard someone can rearrange by accidentally dragging while
scrolling on a touchscreen is one whose layout nobody trusts again. Only the `lg`
arrangement is stored; narrower breakpoints are derived, so nobody has to arrange
a phone view they never look at. Nothing renders until the container is measured
once, because laying out against a width of 0 puts every card in column 0 for a
frame and reads as the layout having been lost.

### Verification

API **1598 passing / 127 files** (single-fork), web **813 / 61**, shared 16 new
unit tests, `tsc --noEmit` clean on all three projects, `vite build` succeeds,
migration drift guard PASS. End-to-end against the live database: save, the
append-missing rule, zero audit rows on a personal save, and DELETE restoring the
role default.

Not verified in a browser — Playwright cannot authenticate against this install's
certificate. **The drag interaction itself has not been seen by anyone yet.**

## [Unreleased] - Dashboard aggregate widgets (2026-08-28)

A trend card showing the spread across the current drill-down, a list of active
alarms for that same selection, and an "As of" column on the Readings table.
Project B of two; Project A (panel assignment) shipped earlier the same day and
these arrive as two new keys in its catalogue. Spec:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-dashboard-aggregate-widgets-design.md`.

**No count moved.** Models **36**, enums **13**, permissions **42**, reauth
actions **48**, audit actions **97**, API modules **24**, config defs **25**,
config pages **24**, `<Route>`s **50**, shared type files **18** — all
re-derived, all unchanged. **No migration**, no new permission, reauth action or
audit action.

### The trend card

New `GET /api/instruments/telemetry-aggregate?functionalLocationId=&window=`
(`modules/instruments/telemetry-aggregate.ts`), aggregating in SQL over the
instruments the caller may see within the selection, bucketed like
`room-history.ts`. A Block covers its Areas through `resolveLocationIds` — a bare
equality would return only what is pinned to the Block itself, which on this
installation is nothing at all.

Three decisions the code argues rather than assumes:

- **Every value it returns is DERIVED**, and the card says so above the plot. On a
  §11 system a computed number that looks like a recorded one is a
  misrepresentation, not a presentational shortcut — the same reason the
  per-instrument trend page labels an averaged chart and refuses to let its
  sampler invent a point.
- **Limit lines appear only when every instrument in the selection resolves to the
  same bound.** Instruments carry their own limits, and this database already
  holds instruments whose attributes override their room's; drawing the first
  one's limits across a mixed selection would be a false claim about all the
  others. An instrument with NO bound makes the selection mixed rather than
  agreeing. A selection where NOTHING is bounded is reported as unbounded, not as
  mixed, because "these instruments have different limits" would be untrue there.
- **Below two instruments reporting, the card shows the COUNT instead of a band.**
  Added after the endpoint's first live run: 1 of 101 instruments had reported in
  24 hours, and a "spread across 33 instruments" computed from one sensor is
  technically correct and practically a lie. Judged on the PEAK, not the last
  bucket, so one quiet bucket does not make the card flicker between two
  presentations. The per-bucket instrument count is shown either way.

`TimeSeriesChart` gained ONE optional `envelope` prop, absent by default — the
trend page's and room chart's tests staying green is the evidence they are
untouched. Its lo/hi join the y-scale union, since an envelope clipped at the plot
edge would understate the spread it exists to show.

### The alarm list

`GET /api/alarms` gained a `functionalLocationId` filter, expanded via
`resolveLocationIds` and **ANDed with** the caller's visibility scope through
`scopedToVisible`, never substituted for it — a location filter that widened
visibility would be the exact inversion of what both filters are for. Pinned by a
case that names a location the caller cannot see and asserts it returns nothing.

The widget renders NOTHING on a permission error rather than an empty state: "no
alarms" reads as "nothing is wrong" to someone who simply cannot see them. The
existing top-level Alarms count card is untouched.

### The Readings table

**No new panel.** The existing table already IS latest-reading-per-instrument, so
building a second one of that shape would have been a duplicate to keep in sync by
hand. It gains the one thing it lacked: an **As of** column, so a value that
stopped updating an hour ago no longer looks like a live one.

It uses the EXISTING `readingAge` in `status.ts` — a second copy was written
before that was noticed, and deleted. The only genuinely new rule is
`oldestReadingTs`, which deliberately differs from the `latest` timestamp two
lines above it: that one drives the Status tooltip and asks "are we hearing from
this instrument at all"; this asks "how stale might the numbers on this row be",
and the freshest of two values cannot answer that.

### Panel keys

`dashboard_trend` and `dashboard_alarms`, APPENDED to the dashboard group because
the catalogue order is asserted. **No migration:** a role holding an explicit
panel list does not get them until an admin ticks them, since absence of a key
already means "not shown" and that is the right default for new capability.
Deliberately the opposite of what Project A's migration did for the trend keys,
where those panels were already visible and carrying only the dashboard keys would
have taken something away.

### Verification

API **1590 passing / 126 files** (single-fork), web **813 / 61**, `tsc --noEmit`
clean on all three projects, `vite build` succeeds. New e2e
`src/e2e/telemetry-aggregate.test.ts` (13 cases) drives everything through the
seeded OPERATOR over HTTP; its load-bearing case seeds an out-of-scope instrument
with a value extreme enough that its inclusion could not be mistaken for anything
else, because an aggregate leaks silently — as a number that is merely wrong, with
no row on screen to point at.

Not verified in a browser — Playwright cannot authenticate against this install's
certificate.

**Worth knowing:** at the time of writing, 1 of 101 instruments had reported in 24
hours, so the trend card will show its sparse-selection message for most
selections until ingest is running.

## [Unreleased] - Panel assignment, per role and per user (2026-08-28)

Every panel on the dashboard and the instrument trend page is now assignable, per
role AND per user, on Config -> Roles & Access -> **Panels** — beside Instrument
Scope, in the same shape. Spec:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-panel-assignment-design.md`; plan:
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-28-panel-assignment.md`.

**One count moved:** config pages **25 -> 24** (`routes/config/dashboard-cards.tsx`
deleted; the new tab lives inside the existing `role-access.tsx`). Shared type
files 17 -> 18 (`types/panels.ts`). Models **36**, enums **13**, permissions
**42**, reauth actions **48**, audit actions **97**, modules **24**, config defs
**25**, `<Route>`s **50** — all re-derived and unchanged. **No new permission,
reauth action or audit action**: the routes reuse `ROLE_MANAGE`,
`UPDATE_ROLE_CONFIG` and `CONFIG_CHANGED`, exactly like instrument scope.

### What is assignable

`telemetry_table` and `telemetry_floorplan` on the dashboard; `trend_gauges`,
`trend_charts`, `trend_summary`, `trend_historian_table` and `trend_alarms` on the
trend page, **which had no governance at all before this**.

### Hiding a panel is a DISPLAY decision, not an access control

It does not stop the data being fetched from the API — `instrument_scope` is what
restricts data. That sentence is on the editor screen, not only in the design doc,
because an admin who hides the alarms widget believing they have withheld alarm
data has been misled by the UI, and that is the failure this feature can most
easily cause. The trend page's data fetching is deliberately untouched, so a
hidden panel does not change what the signed PDF report covers.

### Storage: like `instrument_scope`, not like `dashboard-cards`

Nullable `dashboard_cards` JSONB on **both** `role_configs` and `user_configs`
(migration `20260828070000_panel_access`, hand-authored, drift guard PASS, applied
to `compliance_core_db` and `compliance_core_db_test`). Three states, kept
distinguishable end to end: `NULL` = inherit (user -> role -> every panel),
`[]` = **NO panels**, `[keys]` = these.

**Deliberately unlike `sidebarItems` sitting beside it.**
`configService.getMyConfig` decides whether a user config wins by testing
`sidebarItems.length > 0`, so an empty user list falls through to the role.
Panels must not copy that: it turns a deliberate deny into a grant. The reasoning
is written at both the resolver and the route so nobody "makes it consistent"
later.

Nullable with **no default** — a `DEFAULT '[]'` would have blanked every existing
role's dashboard the moment the migration ran.

### The migration bug the checkpoint caught

The first version used `UPDATE` alone. On this installation only ADMIN and VIEWER
had `role_configs` rows while the legacy map named six roles, so four were
silently skipped. Harmless here by luck — those four listed both live cards
anyway — but a role whose list held **no** live card would have been widened from
"no cards" to "every panel". The migration now pairs the `UPDATE` with an `INSERT`
for roles that have no config row, and `scripts/verify-panel-migration.ts` proves
the carry-over against the row it came from before that row is deleted.

The carry-over also **adds every trend key** to each migrated role. The trend page
was ungoverned before, so everyone saw all five of its panels; carrying only the
two dashboard keys would have silently stripped the whole trend page from every
role — a narrowing nobody asked for, and one that would have looked like a bug in
the new feature rather than in the SQL.

### One catalogue, replacing two hand-synced copies

`@digilog/shared` `types/panels.ts` is now the only definition. It replaced an
`ALL_CARDS` array in the web config page and a `VALID_CARD_KEYS` set in the API
route that carried a "keep in sync" comment — a drift with a comment on it. A
frozen-key test locks the order, because those keys are stored in the database and
renaming one silently orphans every row that names it.

**Four keys retired**: `total_users`, `audit_trail`, `notifications`,
`quick_actions`. They gated dashboard sections removed when the page was cut to
"tabular view and graphical view", and had been inert ever since. A switch that
does nothing on a governance screen is worse than an absent one — someone will
turn one off believing they restricted something. (The same thing had already
happened once, to eight filter-domain keys; that history is recorded in
`panels.ts` rather than lost with the file that held it.)

### Retired

`modules/config/static-routes/dashboard-cards.routes.ts`,
`routes/config/dashboard-cards.tsx`, and the `system_config['dashboard-cards']`
row (deleted only after the carry-over verified; its final value is in the commit
message). Config -> Appearance is now a single Branding page. Retiring the old PUT
also removes a live hazard: it wrote the **whole** config blob, so two admins
editing different roles overwrote each other silently. The new routes write one
role or one user at a time.

### Verification

API **1566 passing / 124 files** (single-fork), web **798 / 59**, shared 20 new
unit tests, `tsc --noEmit` clean on all three projects, `vite build` succeeds.
New e2e `src/e2e/panel-access.test.ts` (11 cases) drives everything through the
seeded OPERATOR over HTTP, because SUPER_ADMIN short-circuits to "every panel" and
an admin-driven version would pass against a route with no resolution at all.
Not verified in a browser — Playwright cannot authenticate against this install's
certificate.

## [Unreleased] - Instrument visibility: assign individual instruments, not just locations (2026-08-28)

A role or user scope can now name INSTRUMENTS as well as functional locations.
"Area-wise" and "location-wise" already worked — `FunctionalLocation` is the
Block > Area tree and a granted Block already expanded to its Areas — so the new
capability is explicit instrument ids, singly or in any number.

**No count moved.** No model, enum, permission, reauth action, config def, config
page, API module or `<Route>` was added, and **there is no migration**: the
existing `instrument_scope` JSONB column carries the new shape.

### Storage — two shapes, permanently, on purpose

`role_configs.instrument_scope` / `user_configs.instrument_scope` now hold
`{locationIds, instrumentIds}`. Rows written before today hold a bare array of
location ids and are **deliberately never rewritten** — rewriting every
access-control row is a larger risk than a reader that accepts both.

`normalizeScope()` in `modules/instruments/visibility.ts` is that reader, and
there is exactly ONE of it. Before this change there were two independent
`Array.isArray(v)` tests (visibility.ts and the admin GET in roles/routes.ts),
and in both, "not an array" meant *nothing stored* → **unrestricted**. Either one
left behind would have read every legacy restricted row as unrestricted while the
admin screen still displayed the restriction. The legacy-shape cases in
`src/e2e/instrument-scope-selection.test.ts` exist to keep that closed.

Three states are unchanged and still distinguishable end to end: `null` =
inherit, an empty selection = **sees nothing**, anything selected = that
selection.

### Matching is a UNION

`scopeToWhere` compiles to `{ OR: [ {functionalLocationId: {in: …}}, {id: {in: …}} ] }`
— the same shape an alarm webhook target already uses, so no fourth grouping
concept was introduced. **Both branches are always emitted, even when empty:**
`{ OR: [] }` matches nothing in Prisma while `{}` matches everything, and a
"tidy up the empty branch" refactor is one step from the second.

### One documented behaviour deliberately reversed

`scopeToWhere` used to guarantee that an instrument with no functional location
was invisible to any active scope (`IN (...)` never matches NULL). **Naming an
instrument by id now grants it even when it has not been placed** — otherwise
assigning a freshly commissioned device would silently do nothing. The location
branch is unchanged and still cannot reach an unplaced instrument; the e2e suite
asserts both halves so the grant is traceable to the new branch.

### Two pre-existing leaks found in the touchpoint sweep and fixed

Both are the same shape as the `GET /:id/telemetry` gap closed on 2026-08-24 — a
sibling route left on a bare lookup when its neighbour was scoped. "The user
cannot see that instrument's data" was not true while either answered:

- **`GET /api/instruments/:id/dead-letters`** — no visibility scoping at all, and
  it returns `rawPayload`, the device's own message, which carries the readings.
  Now scoped in the lookup: 404, never 403.
- **`GET /api/floorplans/:id/rooms/:roomId/history`** — returned the time series
  for *every* instrument in a room regardless of scope. Now filtered on the room
  MEMBERSHIP query, so an out-of-scope instrument contributes no series at all
  rather than being filtered out of the response after the rows were read. The
  room and its limits are still returned: a room is a space, not an instrument.

**Counts were leaking too — a whole second class, found by the operator.** A
count is a disclosure: it both misdescribes what the caller has and reveals the
size of the estate they are excluded from.

- **`GET /api/instrument-profiles` and `/:id`** counted every instrument in the
  profile. On this install a user scoped to 4 instruments saw a profile card
  reading "101 instruments". The nested relation now carries the visibility
  filter. `PUT /:id` is scoped the same way so an edit cannot make the number
  jump to one the list never shows; `POST /` needs no scope (a new profile is
  empty). **The DELETE guard stays UNSCOPED deliberately** — it exists to explain
  the foreign key's refusal, and the FK counts every instrument regardless of who
  asks; a scoped count there would tell a restricted admin the profile is empty
  and then hand them a raw FK error. Both halves are pinned by tests.
- **`GET /api/functional-locations`** reported "CWH Block: 100" to the same user.
  `loadOwnCounts` now takes the visibility filter. **The tree's SHAPE is
  deliberately not filtered** — every Block and Area is still returned, showing
  0. A location is a place, not an instrument, and hiding locations would make
  the plant's structure change depending on who is looking, including for the
  admin choosing locations to grant.
- Checked and found already correct: `GET /api/alarms/summary` (18 active for an
  unrestricted caller, 2 for the scoped one), `GET /api/instruments`,
  `telemetry-overview`, `eligible-children`, and `GET /api/floorplans` (rooms
  carry no instruments).

**`GET /api/floorplans/:id` was checked and left unscoped, knowingly.** It lists
instrument identity (id/code/name) per room, gates on `CONFIG_READ`, and is
fetched only by the Config → Floorplans placement editor — verified 2026-08-28,
not assumed. The graphical dashboard uses `GET /api/floorplans`, which returns
rooms **without** instruments, plus the room history above. An admin placing
instruments on a plan must see all of them, the same reasoning already on record
for the alarm-webhook config routes. Recorded here rather than left as "I looked
at it", which is how the 2026-08-24 telemetry gap survived beside a scoped
sibling.

### Admin surface

Config → Roles & Access → Instrument Scope gains an instrument picker beside the
location picker (searchable by code, name or location; unplaced instruments
labelled). The two lists add up, and the screen says so.

- **An instrument already covered by a selected location renders ticked, disabled
  and labelled "via <location>"**, above a count line. Selecting a Block always
  granted every instrument in its Areas — on this install, selecting `CWH Block`
  grants 100 instruments, none of which are attached to the Block itself — but
  the picker showed nothing ticked, so a correct assignment was invisible. That
  is the worst combination on an access-control screen. The row cannot be
  unticked individually: the location grants it, so removing one would mean
  deselecting the location.
- Which locations cover an instrument is answered **server-side**
  (`coveringLocationIds` on the picker payload) by `buildCoveringIndex()`, which
  is built by calling `resolveLocationIds` over every location rather than by
  walking `parentId` upward. Containment is a policy decision and a second copy
  of it in the browser is the drift this repo has been bitten by before; deriving
  the index from the one authoritative function means the picture and the query
  cannot disagree. An e2e case walks the picker's own answer and asserts the
  scoped list returns exactly the instruments it claimed, in both directions.

- The picker reads a new **deliberately unscoped** listing,
  `GET /api/roles/instrument-scope/instruments` (ROLE_MANAGE). A scoped listing
  would show an admin who is themselves restricted only their own instruments,
  so they would build a scope silently omitting the rest with no way to tell —
  the reasoning already on record for the alarm-webhook config routes.
- The §11 signature was reworded: `"...set to N functional location(s)"` became a
  false statement the moment instruments could be named. It now names both counts,
  and "NO instruments at all" for an empty selection.
- **Fixed while in there:** the tab defined its editor and picker components
  *inside* its render function, so React remounted them on every parent render —
  a half-finished selection was silently discarded whenever SWR revalidated (on
  window focus, for instance) or another row saved. Hoisted to module scope, with
  an explicit `key` so the editor re-seeds from the server value on save and only
  then.

### Verification

`visibility.test.ts` 26 unit tests (normalizeScope's legacy/new/malformed
branches, the always-two-branch `OR`, the unplaced-instrument grant);
`instrument-scope-selection.test.ts` 21 e2e over HTTP as the seeded OPERATOR, each
restricted case paired with a positive control — including the two routes that
paint the dashboard (`telemetry-overview` and the `points=` chart path) under an
INSTRUMENT-ONLY scope, which is the discriminating fixture: any step that assumed
a scope names locations would come back empty there while the list page still
showed the instrument. A per-user override in the new shape is covered too, since
replace-not-intersect is what "same role, different users, different instruments"
rests on. Related suites re-run green:
telemetry-range, alarm-webhooks, floorplans, instruments, roles,
role-attribute-access, instrument-limit-alarms (284 + 84 passing), web 794/794.
`tsc --noEmit` clean on both projects. Not verified in a browser — Playwright
cannot authenticate against this install's certificate.

## [Unreleased] - Dashboard wallpaper fills the content pane (2026-08-28)

Operator: no gap between the sidebar and the dashboard wallpaper.

`apps/web/src/lib/background-style.ts` switched `background-size` from `contain`
to `cover`. The gap was not a margin — the layer is already flush against the
sidebar (`absolute inset-0` in the content pane). It was `contain`'s
letterboxing: whatever the pane's aspect ratio does not match was left as blank
white scrim, which on a wide screen reads as a white band beside the sidebar.

**The cost, stated plainly:** an image whose aspect ratio differs from the
content pane is now CROPPED, centred, so its edges are what is lost. Nothing
functional rides on the wallpaper. No count moved; no other file changed.

Test updated to assert `cover` (`src/lib/__tests__/background-style.test.ts`,
15 pass). Not verified in a browser — Playwright cannot authenticate against
this install's cert, so the visual check is the operator's.

## [Unreleased] - Instrument trend page: sampling, true range summaries, zoom (2026-08-27)

The Trend page now plots wide ranges honestly. Spec:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-instrument-trend-page-design.md`.

**No count moved.** Re-derived from live code 2026-08-27: **36** Prisma models,
**13** enums, **42** permissions, **48** reauth actions, **24** API modules,
**25** config defs, **25** config pages, **50** `<Route>`s. No migration. One
existing route gained query parameters; one new pure module in
`@digilog/shared`; one preset added to an existing list.

### The bug this fixed

`GET /api/instruments/:id/telemetry` silently returned only the **newest 1000
readings** for any range — `telemetry.repository.ts:getHistory` did
`Math.min(opts.limit ?? 100, 1000)` with `ORDER BY ts DESC`. At this
installation's 30–90 second cadence, a 7-day chart plotted roughly the last
**day** while the x-axis claimed a week, and the summary strip was computed over
that truncated slice. Nothing on screen said so. The PDF report's own fetch had
the same defect and printed the same misdescribed period.

### Backend

- `points` (integer, 1..5000) selects a **chart path** separate from the paged
  table path. Out of range is a **400 from the schema, not a silent clamp**.
  `points` omitted leaves the old `limit`/`offset` behaviour byte-for-byte
  unchanged, and the 1000-row cap stays on that path.
- Response gains `historyTotal` (the TRUE number of readings in the range, not
  the number returned), `historySampled`, and `summaries[key]` —
  `{ count, numericCount, min, max, avg, first, last, belowCount, aboveCount,
  outOfSpecCount, limitMin, limitMax }`.
- **`summaries` is computed in SQL over EVERY reading in the range**
  (`getRangeSummary`), in a query deliberately separate from the row query. A
  `max` derived from the downsampled subset would let a spike the sampler did
  not select vanish from a signed §11 readout — an aggregate that *understates
  an excursion* is the worst failure this surface has.
- `belowCount`/`aboveCount`/`outOfSpecCount` are nullable and **the null is
  load-bearing**: it means no limit was resolved for that key, which is not the
  claim "zero breaches". `limitMin`/`limitMax` ride along from the server's own
  limit resolution, so a printed count and a printed bound cannot disagree
  about which limit applies.
- Pinned by `apps/api/src/e2e/instrument-telemetry-range.test.ts`, including the
  assertion that carries the whole design: **`summary.max` equals the true
  maximum in the range even when that reading is not among the returned rows.**

### Shared

- New pure module `packages/shared/src/types/telemetry-downsample.ts` —
  `lttb()`, Largest-Triangle-Three-Buckets. It **selects** readings and never
  computes one: every returned element is reference-equal to an input element,
  asserted with `toBe` so a refactor that builds new objects fails. Returns the
  input unchanged when it already fits, always keeps the first and last
  reading, preserves order, and degenerates cleanly below `target < 3`. A
  bucket-range off-by-one that hid an excursion in the first bucket was found
  and fixed by its own spike-preservation test.
- `12h` preset added to `PERIOD_PRESETS`. **The default window no longer
  resolves by array POSITION** (`PERIOD_PRESETS[3]`) but by value against
  `DEFAULT_PERIOD` — the positional lookup meant inserting a preset silently
  changed what every trend page opened on. `15m` is kept: removing a preset
  someone may be using was not part of this.

### Frontend

- **Downsampling is by selection, never by averaging.** Averaging invents
  values that were never read, and a two-second excursion is exactly what a
  bucket mean destroys — on a §11 system the excursion is the thing the record
  exists to show. Client-side aggregation remains available, is **off by
  default**, and says so on screen when on.
- When a chart is showing a subset it says so in the flow, not in a tooltip:
  `sampled-note.tsx`, "Showing 2,000 of 28,431 readings." `shown` is the **raw
  reading count**, not the post-bucketing point count.
- **Zoom refetches; it does not magnify.** `routes/dashboard/chart-zoom.ts`
  turns a drag selection into a time range and the page requests it fresh, so
  zooming into a sampled 30-day view reveals the true raw readings for the
  narrower window. Magnifying the subset in hand would claim a resolution the
  client does not have. Fullscreen no longer maps pointer pixels to the wrong
  instant.
- Empty / loading / error states, chart titles, and tooltip units on both
  charts.
- Chart colours moved to `--chart-*` custom properties in `app.css`, each read
  with a literal fallback. **Known limitation, now written down:** the PDF
  export serialises the chart's SVG into a standalone document with no
  stylesheet, so only the fallbacks resolve — the exported chart can never
  follow a future theme. Accepted: a signed record printing yesterday's palette
  beats one printing an invisible line.
- **The signed PDF report's banner was reworded**, because fixing the
  truncation turned a true disclosure into a false one. It used to say the
  report covered "the most recent portion" of the period — true under
  `ORDER BY ts DESC`, false once the rows are spread across the whole range.
  Its out-of-limit counts now come from the server's whole-range summary.

### Review fix wave (2026-08-27, later the same day)

Eight fixes from the whole-branch review. **No count moved** — no model, enum,
permission, reauth action, module, config def, config page or `<Route>` was
added or removed; re-derived from live code 2026-08-27.

- **The signed PDF could print a Maximum BELOW a limit it reported breaches
  of.** `withServerSummary` took the readings count and the out-of-limit counts
  from the server but left `min`/`max`/`mean` derived from the LTTB sample, and
  LTTB can drop the one reading that breached: `Maximum 24.8 °C` printed
  directly above `3 above 25.0`, arithmetically impossible, in the artifact that
  leaves the building. All three now come from the server too.
  **This deliberately overturns the earlier decision to keep them row-derived.**
  That decision's stated reason was that whole-range extremes beside
  sample-derived `first`/`last` would quote two populations. They do not
  conflict: `first`/`last` print as "First reading"/"Last reading" WITH their
  own timestamps — claims about two instants, not about the range — so a range
  minimum below both is expected. The count, extremes, mean and breach counts
  now all describe the same server-side numeric population; the report's
  coverage banner shrank to say exactly that.
- **The on-screen per-chart summary strip that spec §3 asked for was never
  built.** Each chart now carries Current / Minimum / Maximum / Average from the
  server's whole-range summary, at the instrument's own decimals — so the screen
  and the PDF quote the same aggregates for the same figures. "Current" is the
  latest STORED reading in the range, never the last plotted point, which is a
  bucket mean whenever a chart interval is selected.
- **`historyTotal` was the post-slice row count**, so a read that hit the
  200,000-row backstop would have printed an understated denominator both in
  "Showing N of M readings" and in the PDF banner. It now comes from the range's
  own `count(*)` (`chartRangeTotal`), byte-equivalent on every non-truncating
  call. The truncation DIRECTION is now stated in code: the read is `ts ASC`, so
  a capped fetch keeps the oldest readings — the mirror image of the original
  defect.
- **Extra-key charts sampled silently** — the one place left in the feature that
  dropped readings without saying so. They now carry `SampledNote` and a summary
  strip (at the shared fallback precision; an undeclared key has no administered
  decimals).
- **The charts said "No data available" while loading and while the fetch was
  failing** — a positive claim about the record when the truth was "we do not
  know". A skeleton and a per-chart error state with Retry now answer those two;
  only a resolved, empty range reaches the chart's own empty state. The
  page-level error banner was removed: the chart request is the only request
  that error belongs to.
- `useInstrumentTrend` now returns `error`/`retry`/`chartsLoading`; the SWR key
  the page had duplicated byte-for-byte to reach them is gone.
- A dead `room` select and a false comment removed from `/:id/telemetry-keys`'s
  visibility lookup. Four comments describing the old summary behaviour made
  true.

## [Unreleased] - Alarm webhook annunciator (2026-08-27)

Alarms now reach a **device** as well as a person. An operator can point an
IP-addressable hooter (or any HTTP endpoint) at one instrument or a group of
them and have it buzz when any of them goes into alarm. `NotificationRule` is
untouched — alerting people is unchanged.

**Why not the obvious implementations.** Extending `NotificationRule` fails
because `notification-dispatcher.ts` skips a rule with no *user* recipients,
because the rule has no instrument scoping, and — decisively — because
`Alarm.ruleId` is nullable: the `INSTRUMENT_LIMIT` alarms that actually fire on
this installation carry no rule row, so a design hung off `AlarmRule` would
annunciate nothing while appearing correctly configured. A new
`InstrumentGroup` model fails because it would be a fourth grouping concept
beside `FunctionalLocation`, `roomId` and `profileId`. Annunciation is
therefore keyed off the **instrument**, and scope reuses the existing
`role_configs.instrument_scope` shape.

### Data model

- **2 new Prisma models** (34 → **36**), migration
  `20260827120000_alarm_webhooks`, hand-authored, applied to
  `compliance_core_db` **and** `compliance_core_db_test`:
  - `AlarmWebhookTarget` — url, method, headers, contentType, bodyTemplate,
    successRegex, timeoutMs, `fireOnRaised/Cleared/Acknowledged`, severities,
    cooldownSeconds, isActive, `scopeLocationIds`, `scopeInstrumentIds`.
  - `AlarmWebhookDelivery` — the §11 receipt: **one row per attempt**, success
    or failure, storing the URL hit and the body actually sent, plus
    httpStatus, responseSnippet, attempt, status, error.
- **No new Prisma enum** (13 unchanged, deliberately): `method`, `event` and
  `status` are validated strings, the same precedent as `FloorplanRoom.grade`,
  so the vocabulary can grow without a migration. Do not go looking for one.
- Both FKs `onDelete: Restrict`. Deleting a target is a soft operation
  (`isActive = false`); a hard delete is refused with a stated message while
  deliveries reference it, because a delivery row is the evidence of whether an
  excursion was annunciated.

### Scope

- `scopeLocationIds` (functional locations, a Block expanding to its Areas via
  `functional-locations/tree.ts:resolveLocationIds()`) UNIONED with
  `scopeInstrumentIds`. Resolved once, server-side, in
  `modules/alarm-webhooks/target-scope.ts`.
- Unlike `instrument_scope`, both columns are `NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'`, and
  **both empty matches NOTHING — never everything.** A silent misconfigured
  target is a bug someone finds; a plant-wide buzzer gets the feature switched
  off at the panel and never switched back on. A unit test pins `[]`/`[]` to
  zero matches.
- Several targets may match one instrument and all of them fire — the
  local-panel-plus-control-room case, intended.

### Firing and delivery

- Fires on **RAISED**, **CLEARED** and **ACKNOWLEDGED**. The acknowledge hook
  sits **after** the atomic claim, so two simultaneous acknowledgements produce
  one delivery, not two.
- `enqueueAlarmWebhook()` **never throws** — a queue outage or an unplugged
  hooter must cost an annunciation, never the detection of every other
  excursion in the same pass.
- **New graphile-worker task `alarm_webhook`** (5 → **6**), enqueued
  `maxAttempts: 1`; retry is bounded inside the task (3 attempts, ~2s apart) so
  graphile-worker's exponential backoff cannot sound a buzzer twenty minutes
  after the excursion cleared. Event-driven — **no `crontab.txt` entry, on
  purpose.**
- `cooldownSeconds` throttles **RAISED only**. `CLEARED` and `ACKNOWLEDGED` are
  silence signals; never rate-limit the off switch. In-memory per-target map,
  same single-instance caveat as the dispatcher's.
- Success = 2xx **and**, when `successRegex` is set, a matching response body —
  the regex is authoritative, because cheap hardware returns HTTP 200 on
  failure (same lesson as `SmsConfig.httpGatewaySuccessRegex`).
- Body rendering is a **separate renderer**,
  `modules/alarm-webhooks/render-body.ts` — deliberately *not*
  `notification-delivery/template-engine.ts:resolveTemplate()`, which
  HTML-escapes `& < > "` and would ship `&quot;A&quot;` for an instrument named
  `Chiller "A" & B`, corrupting the JSON payload and looking like an
  intermittent network fault. Placeholders come from the exported
  `ALARM_WEBHOOK_VARIABLES`, which the config page's picker renders from.
- Outbound stance, stated for the record rather than revisited quietly: the URL
  is operator-typed and on their LAN, so there is **no allowlist**. The guards
  are a hard timeout, `redirect: 'error'`, no cookies/credentials/session
  token, and a full delivery-log record of every attempt.

### Governance

- **New reauth action `MANAGE_ALARM_WEBHOOK`** (47 → **48**) in the *existing*
  `Configuration` category — categories stay at **8**. Enforced on create,
  update, delete and test-fire.
- **4 new audit actions and 4 new templates** (93 → **97** / 87 → **91**),
  7 categories unchanged.
- **No new permission** (42 unchanged) — the routes reuse `ALARM_RULE_READ` /
  `ALARM_RULE_MANAGE`: a role that can decide when an alarm fires can already
  decide where it is announced. **No new sidebar item** (12 unchanged) — the
  page lives under Config.
- The `/config` card is **SUPER_ADMIN-only**: `visibleSuperAdminCards =
  isSuperAdmin ? superAdminCards : []` (the delegation allow-list went
  2026-08-19), so a non-SUPER_ADMIN never sees the card and no Configuration
  Access grant will surface it. `/config/alarm-webhooks` is still reachable by
  URL, where `RequireRole permissions={[ALARM_RULE_READ]}` admits them — same
  as Alarm Rules, which sits in the same array. (An earlier entry here said
  "default-deny … until `alarm-webhooks` is granted under Configuration
  Access"; that was false and is corrected.)
- Instrument-visibility scoping on `/api/alarm-webhooks` is **split**: the
  config routes (`GET /`, `GET /:id`, mutations) are deliberately not scoped,
  matching the alarm RULES routes — a half-scoped config surface is worse than
  an unscoped one. `GET /:id/deliveries` **is** scoped, because it is not
  configuration and returns `requestBody` verbatim (instrument code + reading).
  TEST rows (`alarmId: null`) are returned; they name no instrument.

### Surface

- **New API module `alarm-webhooks`** (23 → **24**), registered in **both**
  `app.ts` and `src/e2e/test-helper.ts`. Seven routes:
  `GET /api/alarm-webhooks`, `POST /`, `GET /:id`, `PUT /:id`, `DELETE /:id`,
  `POST /:id/test`, `GET /:id/deliveries?status=` (server-side filter).
  `POST /:id/test` fires regardless of scope and flags, so a hooter can be
  commissioned without waiting for a real excursion — and is audited, because
  it makes a real buzzer sound.
- **New config page** `apps/web/src/routes/config/alarm-webhooks.tsx`
  (24 → **25** config pages; 49 → **50** `<Route`s), with a card in
  `config/index.tsx`. **No new config def** (25 unchanged) — alarm webhooks are
  a CRUD module with their own tables, not a `system_config` row.

### Counts after this change (each re-derived from live code 2026-08-27)

36 models · 13 enums · 42 permissions · 48 reauth actions in 8 categories ·
97 audit actions · 91 audit templates in 7 categories · 24 API modules ·
25 config defs · 25 config pages · 50 routes · 6 worker tasks · 12 sidebar items.

## [Unreleased] - Room doors, cleanroom grade, instrument trend page, governed report downloads (2026-08-24)

Two features on top of the instrument dashboard: (A) drawn doors and
per-instrument tiles on the graphical floor view, and (B) a cleanroom-grade
overlay, a per-instrument trend page, and a governed report-download gate.
Counts re-verified against live code 2026-08-24; only reauth actions moved
(46 → 47, 7 → 8 categories) — models, enums, permissions, sidebar items,
modules, config defs/pages, audit actions/templates are all unchanged.

**C. Trend page — the band gauge (2026-08-24)**

- `routes/instruments/band-gauge.tsx` + `trend-header.tsx`; `trend.tsx`
  restructured (data layer untouched). The two latest-value cards are replaced
  by a gauge that draws the LIMIT BAND with the reading marked in position and
  both headroom figures stated — in GMP monitoring nothing is "a value";
  everything is a value inside a band.
- The gauge states an absent band rather than drawing an empty track, and
  handles the three mis-administrations the schema permits (one bound only,
  low === high, low > high) — all reachable, since both bounds are
  operator-typed instrument attributes.
- **Behaviour change:** an instrument with NO limits no longer shows a green
  "In spec". `LatestValueCard` returned `OK` when both bounds were NULL; the
  gauge reads "Not assessed". Nor does it assert "In spec" over a reading the
  server has already resolved as STALE/PARTIAL — the header prints that word a
  few rows above.
- `ChartSeries` gains an optional `color` (default: the rank-based palette
  slot, so dashboard callers are unaffected). Temperature is slot 1 and
  humidity slot 2 on screen AND in the printed chart — both charts previously
  drew slot 1, so one quantity had two identity colours.
- No new dependency, route, config def, page, model or enum. Counts unchanged.

**A. Room doors + per-instrument tiles**

- `floorplan_rooms.doors Json?` (nullable) — an array of `{wall, offset,
  width, kind}`, normalized against the wall so a door stays attached when
  the room moves. Migration `20260824100000_floorplan_room_doors`, applied to
  both databases.
- Doors are drawn as real gaps in segmented walls with a swing arc; drawn and
  edited in Config → Floorplans. They ride the existing
  `UPDATE_FLOORPLAN_ROOM` reauth + audit path — no new permission or reauth
  action.
- **On `PUT /api/floorplans/:id/rooms/:roomId`, an omitted `doors` key leaves
  the column unchanged; only an explicit `null`/`[]` clears it.** Deliberate —
  a client that doesn't know about doors can't silently wipe them; this is a
  §11 data-loss guard, not an oversight.
- **Fixed a defect:** each room box on the graphical floor view now renders
  ONE TILE PER INSTRUMENT (own code, limits, decimals). The box previously
  rendered only `rows[0]`, so a room's second instrument was invisible,
  including when it was the one breaching a limit.
- New pure module `apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/room-geometry.ts` (wall
  splitting, door placement, tile layout with fixed degrade steps).

**B. Cleanroom grade, trend page, governed report downloads**

- `floorplan_rooms.grade` nullable `TEXT` (`A|B|C|D|CIRCULATION|UTILITY`),
  validated by zod, deliberately **not** a Postgres enum so the vocabulary can
  grow without a migration (enum count stays at 13). Migration
  `20260824140000_floorplan_room_grade`, both databases. Hue encodes grade,
  saturation encodes status — design spec
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-24-graphical-view-visual-design.md`.
- New route `/instruments/:id/trend`: period + interval header, latest-value
  cards, limit-lined charts reusing the existing `TimeSeriesChart`, a raw
  paged time-series, an alarms widget, and per-user extra telemetry keys in
  `localStorage`. `main.tsx` `<Route>` count 48 → **49**
  (`grep -cE "<Route" apps/web/src/main.tsx`).
- Trend charts average client-side when an interval is selected, and say so
  on screen ("Averaged over 5 minutes — the table below shows every reading")
  — a derived point must never look like a stored reading.
- New reauth action `DOWNLOAD_REPORT` under a new `Reports` category
  (46 → **47** reauth actions, 7 → **8** categories —
  `grep -cE "^\s+[A-Z_]+:" packages/shared/src/types/reauth-actions.ts`).
- `POST /api/audit/report-export-log` now requires `remarks` and enforces
  `DOWNLOAD_REPORT` reauth. It reuses the **existing** `REPORT_GENERATED`
  audit action — no new audit action was added (93 actions / 87 templates /
  7 categories unchanged). The Audit Trail export moved onto the same
  dialog, so every report download in the product is now governed.
- `GET /api/instruments/:id/telemetry` gained `offset` (paging); new
  `GET /api/instruments/:id/telemetry-keys` returns the keys an instrument
  has actually sent.
- **Fixed a pre-existing security gap:** `GET /:id/telemetry` had **no
  instrument-visibility scoping** (a bare `findUnique`) while its sibling
  `GET /:id` did — telemetry was readable for instruments outside the
  caller's resolved scope. Now scoped the same way: 404 (never 403, which
  would confirm existence) when out of scope; callers with unrestricted
  scope are unaffected.
- New shared module `packages/shared/src/types/telemetry-period.ts` (period
  presets, interval specs, range resolution).

## [Unreleased] - Filter / AHU / asset domain removed (2026-08-20)

Every remaining filter, AHU, asset, cleaning and filter-activity surface is
gone. The Phase 0 strip (2026-07-18) removed this domain's modules, models and
pages; what it left behind was the vocabulary — in shared types, config lists,
the audit registries and two Postgres enums. None of it was reachable, and
several pieces were user-visible as dead options.

**Deleted (consumer-free — `grep` for importers returned 0 for each):**

- `packages/shared/src/pipeline-executor/**` — 11 source + 11 test files, the
  filter cleaning-cycle executor. Exported from the shared barrel and imported
  by nothing since the strip.
- `packages/shared/src/types/action-tape.ts` — consumed only by the above.
- `apps/web/src/types/filter.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/report-types.ts`,
  `apps/web/src/lib/format-by-least-count.ts` (an equipment-group helper),
  `apps/api/src/e2e/checklist-submission.test.ts`,
  `apps/web/src/lib/__tests__/report-range.test.ts` (re-implemented logic from
  `pm-schedules/index.tsx` and `cleaning-cycles/history.tsx` inside the test
  file, so it exercised only itself).

**Pruned to what the app has:**

- `EXPORT_SURFACES` 10 → 1 and `REPORT_DEFS` 9 → 1 (both keep Audit Trail).
  Config → Export Options was offering per-role PDF/Excel toggles for nine
  deleted pages. Stored `export-options` and `report-page-titles` were both
  `{}`, so no orphaned sub-key needed pruning.
- `AUDIT_ACTIONS` 116 → 93; `AUDIT_TEMPLATE_DEFAULTS` 151 → 87; template
  categories 14 → 7. `ALARM_ACKNOWLEDGED` / `ALARM_CLEARED` moved to the
  Instruments category — the alarm subsystem is live again for instrument
  limits. Config → Audit Templates had been listing 53 editable templates for
  actions nothing can emit.
- `audit-helpers.ts`: 12 asset badges, the Block/Area/AHU/Filter kind labels and
  17 placeholder substitutions. Verified by diffing the live placeholder set
  against the substitution set — 17 dead, 0 missing.

**Deliberate reversal, on operator instruction.** `CLAUDE.md` recorded the audit
registries as retained per 21 CFR §11 ("stop emitting, keep historic rows
renderable"), the precedent set by the UNS and rule-chain tear-outs. Receipt
taken before removing them:

```
SELECT action, count(*) FROM audit_trail
 WHERE action ~* 'FILTER|AHU|ASSET|EQUIPMENT|CLEANING|CHECKLIST|PM_|RFID';
-- 0 rows (compliance_core_db)
```

No `audit_trail` row is deleted or altered and the hash chain is untouched. The
**production RDS is a separate database and was not queried** — if it holds such
rows they now render as title-cased action keys rather than sentences.

**Enum values (migration `20260820100000_drop_filter_domain_notification_events`).**
`NotificationType` loses 10 values (three `CHECKLIST_*`, two `PM_OVERDUE_*`,
`PM_SCHEDULE_QNN`, `GUEST_CLEANING_REQUEST`, three `STAGE_APPROVAL_*`);
`NotificationEventType` loses three `CHECKLIST_*`. Hand-authored from
`migrate diff` with the usual three destructive statements stripped (see the
header of `20260811120000_instrument_floorplans`). Verified 0 rows carry any
doomed value in **both** databases first; applied to `compliance_core_db` and
`compliance_core_db_test`; drift guard PASS. Model and enum counts are
unchanged at 34 / 13 — values were removed, not types.

**Dead behaviour found and removed on the way** (none of it filter-*code*, all
of it filter-*shaped*, and each reachable in principle):

- `config-discovery.ts` ran `migrateFilterPmScheduleIntoPmSettings()` on every
  boot, which would **create** `pm-schedule-settings` — a key with no def. It is
  gone, and the eight filter-domain config keys are swept by
  `cleanupDeadConfigKeys()` instead.
- `config.service.ts` added a role to `qnn-notifications.visibleRoles` whenever
  a Sidebar save included `quality-notifications`. That is not a sidebar item
  and that config key has no def, so the block could only resurrect a dead key.
- `plugins/auth.ts` allow-listed `/api/guest/cleaning-request` as
  **unauthenticated**. No such route exists; an allow-list entry for a path
  nobody serves is a hole waiting for someone to mount `/api/guest/*`.
- `backup.repository.ts` resequenced `deviation_number_seq` and `qnn_seq` after
  a restore. Neither sequence nor either table exists in this database.
- PWA manifest said "DigiLog - Filter Management" with a "Filter Operations"
  shortcut — the name users see when installing the app.
- `notification-dispatcher.ts` carried three checklist email templates,
  field maps, labels and summaries; `notification-rules` offered three checklist
  event types in the rule builder.
- `notification.service.ts`'s `createNotification` took a hand-kept union that
  had drifted **both** ways — it listed three `BLOCK_CHANGE_*` values never in
  the enum and omitted seven that are. Replaced with the generated
  `NotificationType`, which cannot drift.

**Tests repointed rather than deleted where only the example died.** The audit
template actor-placeholder check became a property over the whole registry;
`audit-helpers` gained a registry-wide guard that no template leaves a literal
`{token}` for an inspector; eight fixtures using permission constants that no
longer exist (`ASSET_VIEW`, `FILTER_OPERATE`, `CHECKLIST_SUBMIT`, …) now name
live ones. One **vacuous** test was found and fixed:
`sidebar-visibility.test.ts` asserted `isSidebarItemVisible('report-reviews', …)`
is true — but `report-reviews` is not a sidebar item, and an unknown id has no
privilege group either, so it passed for the wrong reason. It now targets
`home` and asserts the premise before the property.

Counts re-derived: audit actions 116 → 93, audit templates 151 → 87, template
categories 14 → 7, export surfaces 10 → 1, report defs 9 → 1. Unchanged:
34 models, 13 enums, 42 permissions, 46 reauth actions, 23 API modules,
25 config defs, 24 config pages, 48 routes.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean on api and web; `vite build` clean; api 1351,
web 623, shared 238, queue 10, integration 2 skipped (by design) — zero
failures. Restore point: tag `pre-filter-domain-strip`.

`apps/web/src/lib/datetime-input.ts` and its test went too, on a follow-up
request. It was orphaned by this removal — its only callers were the deleted
filter and PM pages. All eight exports (`isoToDateInput`, `startOfDayIso`,
`endOfDayIso`, `datetimeInputToIso`, `isoToDatetimeInput`,
`toIsoIfNaiveDatetime`, `NAIVE_DATETIME_RE`, `DATE_ONLY_RE`) were checked
individually for outside use — zero each. Web suite 623 → 599 tests, 41 → 40
files; `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` clean after.

## [Unreleased] - Role Assignments page removed (2026-08-19)

`/config/role-assignments` and its Configuration card are gone. It was dead in
this fork, not merely unused — receipts before deleting:
